Fire Prowrestling S: 6Men Scramble is a pro wrestling game and part of the long-running Fire Pro Wrestling series. The arcade-style format is largely unchanged from previous entries; as the name suggests, the key new feature in this entry is 6-player simultaneous matches in both tag-team and battle royal formats.

Numerous game modes are available: Victory Road is the single-player campaign mode where the player must defeat a series of opponents to win the title belt; One Night Match is a standard exhibition match mode; Open League and One Night Tournament are tournament modes; and Elimination Match, Battle Royal, Death Match, and Gruesome Fighting are all special exhibition match types with specific rules or ring setups. The series' famously robust create-a-wrestler mode also makes an appearance, allowing the player to create completely custom wrestlers in both appearance and move set, which can then be used in any of the other game modes.

title: Fishing Kōshien
description: Fishing Kōshien is a fishing game based on a TV show produced by TV Osaka. "Kōshien" refers to an annual high school baseball tournament held in Japan, and the show (and this game) adapts that format to fishing; eight high schools each send a team of three to enter a fishing tournament, and each round tasks the contestants with a different type of fishing. The game consists of four rounds: a black bass morning tournament, Kenzaki boat fishing, Japanse carp fishing, and Saipan big game fishing. Each round eliminates two teams from competition, and the goal is to be the winning team at the end of the competition.

title: Fishing Kōshien II
description: Fishing Kōshien II is a fishing game based on a TV show produced by TV Osaka, and a follow-up to Fishing Kōshien. It features an identical format to the previous game: eight teams of three enter a fishing tournament, and each round challenges the player to a different kind of fishing. The four rounds consist of a black bass tournament, offshore boat fishing in Kenzaki, a carp relay race, and a big game survival match. Compared to the first game, the visuals have been revamped to use full-3D fish models rather than the 2D sprites of the original.

title: Fist
description:
Fist is a 3D 1-on-1 fighting game in the tradition of Street Fighter II and a follow-up to Seifuku Densetsu: Pretty Fighter X, featuring several of the same characters. It uses a simple three-button fighting system — punch, kick, and guard — and includes story and 2-player versus modes, plus an arcade mode in the PlayStation version, with eight total characters to play as. Unusual for a game of its time, there is also a character bio mode which lets the player rotate and view the in-game character models from any angle.

Both releases of the game include a bonus disc with an audio drama and two music tracks.

title: Flash Sega Saturn: Ochikadzuki-hen
aka_titles: フラッシュセガサターン おちかづき編
description:
Flash Sega Saturn: Ochikadzuki-hen (フラッシュセガサターン おちかづき編) is a Japanese Sega Saturn demo disc. Unlike other Flash Sega Saturn series, this disc was bundled with the Saturn hardware.

Playable Demos included:
• Saturn Bomberman

Videos included:
• Cyber Troopers Virtual-On
• Sakura Taisen
• Tengai Makyou: Daiyon no Mokushiroku

title: Formula Grand Prix: Team Unei Simulation
aka_titles: Formula Grand Prix: Team Un'ei Simulation
description:
Formula Grand Prix: Team Unei Simulation is a Formula One racing management simulation game. The player controls all the business aspects of running an F1 team, from hiring drivers and training the pit crew, negotiating with sponsors, and choosing parts and equipment for the team's car. The player manages their team through an annual series of 16-race seasons, with each race consisting of both a qualifier and a main race. Races are automated and not player-controlled but can be watched in real-time. Between races, the player can run tests to tune their equipment, train their pit crew to work faster, and use sponsor money toward developing better parts for their vehicle.

The PlayStation version of the game includes an official FOCA license and real names for many drivers and sponsors. The Saturn port lacks an official F1 license but adds the ability to customize the names. Both versions are otherwise nearly identical.

title: Formula Karts
description: Formula Karts is a semi-realistic racing title that attempts to capture the spirit of kart racing with it's low slung feeling of speed, and corner after corner of impressive handling (and inevitable sliding). The title supports both simulation and arcade modes, and features some effective race AI for non-player vehicles. Two player split screen is supported albeit with some slowdown.

title: Formula Karts: Special Edition
description: Formula Karts is a semi-realistic racing title that attempts to capture the spirit of kart racing with it's low slung feeling of speed, and corner after corner of impressive handling (and inevitable sliding). The title supports both simulation and arcade modes, and features some effective race AI for non-player vehicles. Two player split screen is supported albeit with some slowdown.

title: Frank Thomas Big Hurt Baseball
description:
Baseball player Frank Thomas licensed one of the first baseball games to use motion-captured 3D graphics and multiple camera angles. 28 stadia have been rendered in 3D, and each has its own visible and significant differences.

There are 6 distinct game modes, allowing for single exhibition matches as well as full seasons on the playoffs. There is also a Home Run Derby mode, allowing the player to pelt the ball out of the ground for points.

You can choose pitchers and batters, based on their statistics and form. Bowling options are set to define the delivery, with fastballs and curveballs as well as more precise setting of pace and height. Fielding is optional - it's best to leave this to the computer at first You can always alter the infield and outfield depth and shift.

title: Frankenstein: Through the Eyes of the Monster
aka_titles: Frankenstein: Através dos Olhos do Monstro
Frankenstein: Mit den Augen des Monsters
description:
This interactive movie puts a new twist on the Frankenstein tale: you are the monster! You have been falsely accused of murder and executed. However, the scientist Dr. Frankenstein (played by Tim Curry) has found a way to bring you back to life. You wake up in his laboratory, and your goal is to find out what exactly happened to you and what role Frankenstein played in your resurrection. Will you be able to return back to your former self?

The game plays entirely from first-person perspective. You wander around the huge laboratory, looking for clues and solving puzzles. Sometimes events will happen in the game, triggered by careful research of Frankenstein's notes and other clues. The game features live actors filmed over pre-rendered backgrounds.

title: Free Talk Studio: Mari no Kimama na Oshaberi
aka_titles: Free Talk Studio: Mari no Kimama na O-Shaberi
Free Talk Studio: Mari no Kimamana Oshaberi
description:
Free Talk Studio is an adventure-style game where the player takes the part of a radio talk show host interviewing various celebrities live on the air. Each week, the player has a choice of several guests such as an artist, a comedian, and a singer, and is presented with a short biography to review. At various points throughout the broadcast, the player must choose questions and responses from a list, which will affect the flow of the conversation and lead to different topics being discussed. The goal is to ask questions that will lead to the most interesting and engaging interview, and the player is graded at the end of each interview on the station's ratings for their show.

The Sega Saturn version of the game comes in two variants: the Red edition includes a behind-the-scenes booklet, while the Blue edition includes three trading cards featuring photos of the voice actresses. The PlayStation version of the game does not include either bonus item.

title: Freestyle Boardin' '99
description:
Phat Air Extreme Snowboarding is a 3D snowboarding game. The game comes with four game modes: championship, time competition, freestyle and head-to-head.

In championship mode you can choose between five boarders who all have different skills. During the championship you earn points, which can be used to improve the skills of your boarder in between races. There are 8 races in total, which cover all the disciplines. Disciplines include half pipes, downhill, straight jumps, freestyle jumps and slalom.

In the freestyle mode you pick a course and try to score as much points as possible through finishing fast and/or making tricks.

Time Competition is only about finishing first.

You can play the game in two player vertical split-screen mode.

title: Friends: Seishun no Kagayaki
description:
Friends: Seishun no Kagayaki is a console port of an adult visual novel Dousoukai for PC. Sega Saturn port was released 3 years after the PC version and has all the adult content removed but is fully voice-acted. A PlayStation 2 port came 5 years after the Sega Saturn release in two versions, first one marked with age 18 restriction and second one a year later with age 15 restriction. Both PS2 versions, however, do not feature adult CG event scenes, but are fully voiced and have a new opening animation whereas Sega Saturn version does not feature an opening animation.

This is the first game in the Dousoukai series and starts with you on your way to a nice resort to reunite with some of your classmates from high-school. In particular, your tennis team members. The game focuses on romance and features full map of the place you're staying at as well as the rural town and its surrounding area. The game occurs through one week time and lets you visit any location on the map during both daytime and nighttime, which advances the time. An icon of a character marks when someone is at some location, but not who the person is. This visual novel features typical static anime characters sprites with light animation such as talking animations, pasted over background images. CG event scenes occur with the right character at the right place and time. Your dialogue choices and actions affect how the story progresses and if you will end up with one of the heroines or help with the match-making for your friends.

title: From TV Animation Slam Dunk: I Love Basketball
aka_titles: 灌篮高手 我爱打篮球
description:
Slam Dunk is based on the popular manga/anime of the same title, created by Takehiko Inoue. The game follows the story of Sakuragi Hanamichi, a high school delinquent, as he joins a basketball team in an attempt to win the heart of a young woman. The story follows the same plot as the anime/manga and progresses between basketball matches as you progress through the story mode.

Also available is a versus mode, where two players can play against each other using the pre-set teams or by mixing and matching players into their own personal dream team.

title: Full Cowl Mini Yonku Super Factory
aka_titles: Fully Cowled Mini Yonku: Super Factory
Full Cowled Mini Yonku: Super Factory
description:
Full Cowl Mini Yonku Super Factory is a racing management simulation game based on the Mini Yonku (Mini 4WD) line of toy cars produced by Tamiya and featuring characters from the Bakusō Kyōdai Let's & Go!! manga and anime by Tetsuhiro Koshita. In the main race mode, one or more players selects a car and a track, tunes 14 parts of their car based on a wide range of options, and then watches the race play out between a field of five computer-controlled racers. There is no direct control over the vehicles by the player. Up to five players can compete at once, and the game also includes a track editor.

This Special Limited Edition is the only release of the game, and includes a Gunbluster XTO Metallic Blue car model body plus a "Special Mini Book".

title: Fully Cowled Mini Yonku: Super Factory (Special Limited Edition)
description:
Fully Cowled Mini Yonku: Super Factory is a racing management simulation game based on the Mini Yonku (Mini 4WD) line of toy cars produced by Tamiya and featuring characters from the Bakusō Kyōdai Let's & Go!! manga and anime by Tetsuhiro Koshita. In the main race mode, one or more players selects a car and a track, tunes 14 parts of their car based on a wide range of options, and then watches the race play out between a field of five computer-controlled racers. There is no direct control over the vehicles by the player. Up to five players can compete at once, and the game also includes a track editor.

This Special Limited Edition is the only release of the game, and includes a Gunbluster XTO Metallic Blue car model body plus a "Special Mini Book".

title: Funky Fantasy
description:
Somewhere in the distant reaches of space, there exists a society where magic and technology coexist. In this world, peace is maintained by four great cards representing human emotions — Joy, Anger, Grief, and Pleasure. However, the Kingdom of Yoshimole, which protects the Card of Joy, has suddenly come under attack by the Rokuna Empire, which holds the Card of Anger, and strange monsters have appeared all over! The Queen of Yoshimole, Bunny Bee, escapes with her two retainers Riki and Alter, and together they must fight back against the Rokuna Empire and save their homeland.

Funky Fantasy is a comedy-fantasy turn-based strategy RPG. Many of the characters and situations are parodies of popular contemporary games and media, and the cast consists of comedians and actors from Yoshimoto Kogyo, the largest comedy talent agency in Japan at the time. Gameplay is similar to titles like Tactics Ogre with the player controlling Bunny Bee and a team of fighters on grid-based maps against various opponents. Each turn consists of a Move phase, in which the player can position their units, followed by an Attack phase, where the player can attack enemy units or perform other actions.

A key feature is that Bunny Bee can summon monsters on the battlefield to fight for her, similar to Master of Monsters. Each chapter consists of several battle culminating in a boss encounter, and is strictly linear with each battle occurring in order as the often-bizarre story dictates.

title: Funky Head Boxers
description:
Funky Head Boxers is a slapstick boxing game adapted from the arcade game of the same title. This console conversion plays similar to the arcade version but includes significant changes and new content. Notably, the cast of boxers, originally consisting of Sega development staff, has largely been replaced with real-life comedians and actors represented by talent agency Yoshimoto Kogyo. This version includes a new "Champion Mode" in which the player selects a boxer and must train them to increase their stats by winning bouts. There is also a standard versus mode against either the computer or another player.

The Plus edition of the game, released several months later, includes the boss characters unlocked to play as by default and has various other minor polish but is otherwise identical to the original release.

title: Funky Head Boxers PLUS
description:
Funky Head Boxers is a slapstick boxing game adapted from the arcade game of the same title. This console conversion plays similar to the arcade version but includes significant changes and new content. Notably, the cast of boxers, originally consisting of Sega development staff, has largely been replaced with real-life comedians and actors represented by talent agency Yoshimoto Kogyo. This version includes a new "Champion Mode" in which the player selects a boxer and must train them to increase their stats by winning bouts. There is also a standard versus mode against either the computer or another player.

The Plus edition of the game, released several months later, includes the boss characters unlocked to play as by default and has various other minor polish but is otherwise identical to the original release.

title: Fushigi no Kuni no Angelique
description:
This game is a variation on the Angelique story: an ordinary school girl named Angelique becomes involved in a struggle to become the Queen of Cosmos, for which it is necessary to befriend the handsome and powerful Guardians of the Elements. The game features the same world and graphics as Angelique Special, with a slightly different story: Angelique falls asleep outside near a tree, and dreams that she fell through a rabbit hole (in an Alice in Wonderland fashion) into the magical land where she encounters her eternal rival Rosalia.

Unlike other Angelique games, Fushigi no Kuni no Angelique plays like a board game, with the kingdom divided into fields on which Angelique moves. There are no visible dice, but the amount of fields Angelique can walk on is determined randomly by clicking on the "move" button. Fields can either be empty, placed inside a location (like Angelique's own room), trigger events, conversations, etc. In some places it is possible to find items, which can then be used on another field to help Angelique advance more quickly, increasing her chances to become the queen.

title: Fuusui Sensei: Feng-Shui Master
description:
Feng Shui is a traditional Chinese practice which posits that the physical layout of a landscape or other space determines how spiritual energy moves through it, in turn affecting the health and prosperity of that place and the people within.

Feng-Shui Master is an abstract simulation game based on that practice. Each stage consists of a city which the player can move around in first-person, filled with buildings, roads, and other structures and objects. Objects can be moved and adjusted, demolished and rebuilt, and the goal is to rearrange each area in accordance with Feng Shui practice in order to improve the city's prosperity and earn a certain amount of money. The player has a limited amount of money to make changes, but improving the energy flow and prosperity will increase the income and allow for further changes to be made. There are a total of seven stages, and the game also includes in-game book and video resources that explain the basics of Feng Shui.

title: Gaia Breeder
description: Gaia Breeder is a life-simulation sandbox game where the player attempts to recreate a natural environment. In the 23rd century, a meteor has wiped out all wild animal life on Earth, and humanity has decided to attempt to restore it using science. Using a time machine and a curious pink creature called "Mupi", the player travels back in time to harvest the DNA of extinct animals, then can clone or combine them in the present day. The game is divided into a series of "Breeder Tournaments" where the goal is to build a balanced and sustainable natural environment that can be used as a blueprint for restoring nature.

title: Gakkō no Kaidan
description: Gakkō no Kaidan is an interactive movie with adventure elements, made to tie in with a Japanese ghost-themed film of the same name. Like some other Sega CD games with similar thematics, it features FMV sequences with interactive options. For example, escaping some of the enemies may require the player to press directional keys or the A/C buttons. The other element of the game is a point-and-click style set.

title: Gakkō no Kowai Uwasa: Hanako-San ga Kita!!
description: Gakkō no Kowai Uwasa: Hanako-San ga Kita!! is based on the anime series of the same name. A group of curious children explore their school in the dead of night to check out the rumors of ghosts lurking about. They are rescued from certain dangers by the ghost girl Hanako. The game has the player move around in a 3D environment, navigating rooms and areas, solving puzzles, obtaining items and playing mini-games.

title: Gal Jan
aka_titles: Yōen Denshi Mahjong Yūgi Gal Jan
description: Gal Jan is an arcade-style strip mahjong game. It is a standard 1-on-1 riichi mahjong game, and notably uses rotoscoped animation of real actresses for the opponents. The game features only a standard arcade mode where the player plays against each opponent in order. There are three opponents to face, who each progressively disrobe in animated sequences as the player wins matches against them. Gal Jan utilizes rotoscoping for its animation.

title: Galactic Attack
description:
Galactic Attack is a top-down shooter, there are seven levels to play, ranging from battles in the atmosphere of planets to battling over mountain ranges, each with their own standard huge bosses at the end of each of these levels. The player takes control of a starfighter called the RVA-818 X-LAY, out to destroy any opposing forces.

The story has the future of Earth governments gathering together to construct a massive super computer called Con-Human to help with the planet's environment, providing nutrients to the earth and caring for the ecosystem. However, a cloned human is linked with the system and makes Con-Human a sentient being. The system eventually becomes insane and starts to create natural disasters, wiping all nearly all of mankind and destroying the ecosystem, driving the survivors into space to develop colonies on other planets. Con-Human then makes Earth into a giant fortress and is assembling a massive armada to destroy the remaining survivors, but before it can attack, the survivors amass a first strike in order to reclaim the Earth.

The goal is to fly around in the level, using the primary laser weapon to destroy various enemies flying in and out of the screen. Players can upgrade this weapon by collecting "L" icons floating around when enough enemies are destroyed. There is also a secondary weapon, a lock-on missile launcher, that has the ability to fire upon eight different ground enemies at once.

title: Galaxy Fight
aka_titles: ギャラクシーファイト ユニバーサル・ウォリアーズ
description:
As the millennium nears in the far future, a being of ultimate power named Felden will make his appearance in the galaxy. It is unknown whether he comes to destroy all living beings or use his powers for good, but whatever the reason a group of skilled fighters from all corners of the universe have decided to beat each other up in order to face off against him and claim his power.

Enter Galaxy Fight, a one-on-one 2D fighter set in the far future and featuring sci-fi characters and settings. In the game itself, you have to select from 8 fighters, each with his unique moveset and stats, and then attempt to defeat the other character in 2 out of 3 matches using your special moves and attacks while avoiding your opponent's strikes.

Features single player and 2-player Vs. game modes, secret bosses and bonus rounds.

title: Galaxy Fight: Universal Warriors
description:
As the millennium nears in the far future, a being of ultimate power named Felden will make his appearance in the galaxy. It is unknown whether he comes to destroy all living beings or use his powers for good, but whatever the reason a group of skilled fighters from all corners of the universe have decided to beat each other up in order to face off against him and claim his power.

Enter Galaxy Fight, a one-on-one 2D fighter set in the far future and featuring sci-fi characters and settings. In the game itself, you have to select from 8 fighters, each with his unique moveset and stats, and then attempt to defeat the other character in 2 out of 3 matches using your special moves and attacks while avoiding your opponent's strikes.

Features single player and 2-player Vs. game modes, secret bosses and bonus rounds.

title: Galaxy Force II
description:
Galaxy Force II is an expanded version of Galaxy Force. It adds two additional levels, the old levels are revised (expanded and re-balanced) and the four missiles can be fired with a single button press.

You are strapped into a spaceship to take on six dangerous settings, ranging from a pleasant garden to hostile fire and tough ice. You will have to fly freely before cutting through tunnels and canyons, and finally destroying an alien base. Your energy read out starts at 1200 and decreases as shots hit you, or you make contact with a wall or blockage. You have infinite cannons and guided missiles to help you along. You can get regular energy recharges and power upgrades, by shooting and then collecting their carrier pods.

title: Gale Racer
description:
Gale Racer is a 1st-person racing game where the scenarios are 2D and all of them correspond to 20 zones across the United States. The only available camera is the one inside the car, from where you can see the wheel and indicators (again, in 2D). Also, the game features weather effects, like rain, fog and night, for which you should use either the headlights or the windscreen wiper to succeed in the race.

The Saturn version is similar to the Arcade version except that your rivals are fully polygonal cars. It also adds Full Motion Video sequences, as well as a CD soundtrack.

title: Gals Panic SS
description: Gals Panic SS is the first game in the Gals Panic series designed specifically for home consoles. That said, there is no nudity. It is very similar to Gals Panic 4 before it in that all the girls are drawn in an anime style, with no photographic models whatsoever. The gameplay is changed in this game. The same basic gameplay of uncovering a girl's picture with Qix-like gameplay is used, but you spend 5 rounds on each girl. After this, instead of moving on to the next girl, the game saves and ends. You then play another girl after starting the game again. There is a gallery where the unlocked CG can be viewed. There are a total 12 models in the game, the last two unlocked after beating all the available girls. Some of these girls are reused from Gals Panic 4.

title: Gambler Jiko Chuushinha: Tokyo Mahjongland
aka_titles: Gambler Jiko Chūshinha: Tokyo Mahjong Land
ぎゅわんぶらあ 自己中心派 トーキョーマージャンランド
description:
Gambler Jiko Chuushinha: Tokyo Mahjongland is a riichi mahjong game based on the manga by Masayuki Katayama, and a sequel to Katayama Masayuki no Mahjong Dōjō. The game includes three different modes: the main Story Mahjong mode lets the player select either Hideyuki or Dorao and follows their visit to a strange mahjong-themed amusement park; Date Mahjong Anniversary mode lets the player pick from one of nine male characters and attempt to win the heart of one of 18 female characters by playing mahjong; and Free Battle mode is a standard match play mode where any of the 51 characters can be freely selected for a regular match.

Saturn version features completely redone graphics and sound, and includes an additional 5 characters in the free battle mode, but is otherwise the same game.

title: Game Basic for SegaSaturn
description:
Game Basic for SegaSaturn is a game development and programming kit which uses a version of the BASIC programming language. It supports keyboard input directly, includes various tools such as a paint tool and a music sequencer, and is packaged with a communication cable and PC software for transferring programs to and from a Windows PC for easier development. Various premade sample graphical and sound assets are also included, notably including a selection of music tracks from Game Arts games.

There are a total of 43 sample programs included on the disc; while many of these are tools or simple demos, there are also 12 sample games of varying complexity. Sample games include a first-person 3D maze game, a 3D jetpack flight game, and even a complete conversion of the 1984 MSX game Theseus.

title: Game de Seishun
description:
Game de Seishun is a multiplayer party board game in the mold of The Game of Life, which follows each player's avatar through five stage of youth, from kindergarten through to graduating high school and starting a career. The focus is on building friendship and relationships with various characters, and living a full and satisfying youth, with the winners being decided by so-called "seishun points" which are accrued by deepening interpersonal relationships, earning money from jobs, exercising and studying to improve oneself, and going on dates.

Each player moves through the board by selecting from one of several numbers to determine the number of spaces to move. Various spaces have different effects: some cause good or bad events to occur, some cause random events to happen, and some allow the player to pick a specific activity for the day such as studying or going to work which will increase various stats that in turn affect future events. Once all players have reached the goal, points are tallied based on the game type selected and a winner is decided.

title: Game Nihonshi: Kakumeiji - Oda Nobunaga
description: Game Nihonshi: Kakumeiji - Oda Nobunaga is a historical simulation game with an emphasis on the "historical"; while similar to military strategy games such as Advance Wars, it is intended to teach real Japanese history through both the story and strategy gameplay. The game recreates 10 historical events of the life of Oda Nobunaga, from the battle of Iwakura Castle in 1558 through to his death in the Honnō-ji Incident in 1582, as turn-based strategy sequences in which the player controls Nobunaga and his troops, and must meet certain criteria to complete each mission. Animated sequences between each mission dramatize the events of the real historical figure's life.

title: Game no Tatsujin
description: Within Game no Tatsujin are four different classic Japanese board games made by different developers, which are Mahjong, Shogi, Go and Reversi. The board games can be played in three different modes including the Training Mode with five opponents, the Free Battle Mode with progressive levels of difficulty and World Mode with a total of 21 game masters to challenge with the ultimate goal beating them all and earning the award title "Master of the Game".

title: Game no Tatsujin 2
description: Game no Tatsujin 2 is a collection of digital conversions of seven board games popular in Japan: Shōgi, Igo, Renju, Mahjong, Chess, Reversi (called "Place" in this compilation), and Backgammon. Each game is a straightforward conversion of the real-world game, and includes a variety of configuration and difficulty options. All games other than Mahjong also include a two-player mode. In addition to the standard free mode, there is also a "Tatsujinsen" ("Master Battle") mode where the player can challenge masters of each game at the highest level of difficulty with a fixed set of rules.

title: Game no Tetsujin: The Shanghai
description:
Game no Tetsujin: The Shanghai is a collection of three puzzle games which each make use of mahjong tiles:

  • Shanghai, also called Solitaire Mahjong, in which the player must match tiles stacked in various grid patterns. Tiles can only be removed if they are fully visible (no tiles on top of them) and either the left or right edge is fully free.
  • Rong Rong, also called Shisen-Sho, in which the player must match tiles stacked in various grid patterns. Tiles can only be removed if the matching pair can be connected by a line, with no more than two bends, which does not pass through any other tile.
  • Shi-Kin-Joh, also called Forbidden City, a Sokoban-style block pushing game where the player must navigate a maze of oversized mahjong tiles to reach a goal. Pushing two matching tiles together will clear them from the board.

Each game can be freely played individually, and there is also a story mode where the player must complete specific puzzles in order to progress, as well as a Tetsujin ("iron man") mode where puzzles are randomly selected and must be cleared in order.

title: Game Tengoku: The Game Paradise!
description:
Game Tengoku is a conversion of the coin-op game of the same name. The game is a vertical scrolling comical shooter similar to Konami's Parodius series and Hudson's Star Parodier.

The game is playable in normal or time attack mode.

The playable characters are:

  • Jeynus Starmine, pilot of the Fighter-EX from Exerion
  • Seria, pilot of the ship from Plus Alpha
  • Z-DYNE MK II, the successor to the mech from Formation Z
  • Pig, from Okkotoshi Puzzle Tonjan!?
  • Momoko, from Momoko 120%
  • Miki and Misato, two young girls piloting the radar ship Genesis 3 from Field Combat

title: Game Tengoku: The Game Paradise! (Gokuraku Pack)
description: This deluxe release of Game Tengoku includes the game along with a VHS tape which contains an original animated short (16 minutes) and voice cast interviews (41 minutes).

title: Game-Ware
description:
Game-Ware is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the first release in the quarterly series of the same title. This first volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames:

  • Series of Dreams, a short branching text adventure where the player is a young man named Akira, who must make choices as he converses with two women: his girlfriend Shoko, and a mysterious girl named Megumi.

  • Pipit Boy no Daibōken, a puzzle game where the player must guide a boy to collect all the gems on each stage; the boy follows whatever path he walks along, and the player rotates tiles to direct him around the map.

  • Ejihon no Tantei Jimusho, a conversion of a "spot the different" style arcade game for up to four players where the player is shown an image filled with many kanji characters and must locate the one that does not match.

  • Telecom Town, a simple side-scrolling action game sponsored by Nihon Telecom in which a boy named Mamoru must collect stolen telephone cards to save the titular Telecom Town.

  • HG Cup, an action game sponsored by cosmetics company Shiseido in which the penguin Rocky must use hair gel and mousse to find all the checkpoints and clear the course as quickly as possible.

  • A playable demo of Digital Pinball: Last Gladiators which includes a single table, "Warlock".

Also included is a variety of multimedia content such as creator interviews, game previews, and an art gallery.

title: Game-Ware Vol. 1
description:
Game-Ware is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the first release in the quarterly series of the same title. This first volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames:

• Series of Dreams, a short branching text adventure where the player is a young man named Akira, who must make choices as he converses with two women: his girlfriend Shoko, and a mysterious girl named Megumi.
• Pipit Boy no Daibōken, a puzzle game where the player must guide a boy to collect all the gems on each stage; the boy follows whatever path he walks along, and the player rotates tiles to direct him around the map.
• Ejihon no Tantei Jimusho, a conversion of a "spot the different" style arcade game for up to four players where the player is shown an image filled with many kanji characters and must locate the one that does not match.
• Telecom Town, a simple side-scrolling action game sponsored by Nihon Telecom in which a boy named Mamoru must collect stolen telephone cards to save the titular Telecom Town.
• HG Cup, an action game sponsored by cosmetics company Shiseido in which the penguin Rocky must use hair gel and mousse to find all the checkpoints and clear the course as quickly as possible.
• A playable demo of Digital Pinball: Last Gladiators which includes a single table, "Warlock".

Also included is a variety of multimedia content such as creator interviews, game previews, and an art gallery.

title: Game-Ware Vol.2
description:
Game-Ware Vol.2 is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the second release in the quarterly series of the same title. This volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames:

  • Aoi Mizu no Naka, a suspense-horror adventure game with live-action video and photographs.

  • Pipit Boy no Daibōken 2, a sequel to the puzzle game in the first volume in which the player must guide a boy to collect all the bones on each stage; the boy follows whatever path he walks along, and the player rotates tiles to direct him around the map.

  • Telecom Town II, a simple side-scrolling shooter where the player shoots telephone cards as their projectile, and a sequel to the Nihon Telecom-sponsored game in the previous volume.

  • Cinderella Cruising, a top-down driving game sponsored by Mitsubishi in which the player, just married and on the way home from their wedding, must drive their wife home in their brand new Mitsubishi Challenger SUV within a time limit.

  • A playable demo of Layer Section.

Also included is a variety of multimedia content such as creator interviews, game previews, and an art gallery. This edition also includes the first chapter of the Virtua Fighter digital comic, "Legend of Sara".

title: Game-Ware Vol.3
description:
Game-Ware Vol.3 is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the third release in the quarterly series of the same title. As usual, this volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames:

  • Ejihon, a "spot the different" style game for one or two players which returns from the first volume with new puzzle pictures, where the player is shown an image filled with many kanji characters and must locate the one that does not match.

  • Onii-san, a simple point-and-click comedy adventure game.

  • Pipit Boy no Daibōken 3, a continuation of the puzzle games found in the previous releases; the goal is still to guide the boy to collect all the objects on the screen, but it is now a falling-block puzzle game where two players compete to build a path for the boy.

  • Protector Man: The King of Space, a simple Breakout-style game sponsored by razor company Schick.

Also included is a variety of multimedia content such as creator interviews, game previews, and an art gallery. This edition also includes the second chapter of the Virtua Fighter digital comic, "Legend of Sara".

title: Game-Ware Vol.4
description:
Game-Ware Vol.4 is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the fourth release in the quarterly series of the same title. This edition is the first to come on two discs rather than just one, and includes significantly more content than previous volumes. As usual, this volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames:

  • Pipit Boy no Daibōken 4, a continuation of the puzzle game series found in the previous volumes. This edition lets the player player Pipit Boy directly for the first time, as the game is now an auto-scrolling, top-down action game similar to Bump 'N' Jump, in which the player must collect small creatures to use as ammo while avoiding enemies and obstacles.

  • Ejihon, a "spot the difference"-style game for one or two players in which the player is shown an image filled with many kanji characters and must locate the one that does not match; this version continues the story and contains new picture puzzles.

  • Barbara Konomi's Sūsenjutsu, a numerology fortunetelling game.

  • Gondola-kun, a competitive window-washing game for one or two players where each player must avoid constant obstacles and be the first to wash all the windows on their building.

  • Otanoshimi Slot, a slot machine where the player can bet coins earned from viewing other contents on the disc; earning enough coins will give the player a password to enter a contest to win real-life prizes.

  • Yuppii no Puzzle Land, a competitive puzzle game in which two players try to match objects on the screen based on various criteria such as name or color.

  • Onii-san, a simple point-and-click comedy adventure game which returns for a second part to continue the story.

  • A playable demo of Digital Pinball: Necronomicon.

Also included is a variety of multimedia content such as game previews, and an art gallery, though the focus on these elements has been reduced in favor of interactive game content. This edition also includes the third and final chapter of the Virtua Fighter digital comic, "Legend of Sara".

title: Game-Ware Vol.5
description:
Game-Ware Vol.5 is a multimedia "digital magazine", and the fifth and final release in the quarterly series of the same title. As usual, this volume includes several playable game demos and original minigames, with many ongoing series reaching their conclusion:

  • Pipit Boy no Daibōken 5, the conclusion of the Pipit Boy series. This final edition takes the form of a simple action game where the player must target and reel in creatures and powerups while avoiding attacks, with the goal of reaching a quota before the other player.

  • Ejihon, a "spot the different" style game in which the player is shown an image filled with many kanji characters and must locate the one that does not match; as usual, this version includes numerous new picture puzzles.

  • The final chapter of Onii-san, a simple point-and-click comedy adventure game.

  • Barbara Konomi's Sūsenjutsu, a numerology fortunetelling game.

  • Toru Toru Marble, a puzzle game where the player must collect all objects on the field by only moving on the spaces where the items are contained, moving either one or two spaces forward at a time.

  • Otanoshimi Blackjack, a basic blackjack game where the player can bet coins earned from viewing other contents on the disc; earning enough coins will give the player a password to enter a contest to win real-life prizes.

  • Sekai Seifuku Kabushiki Gaisha ("World Conquest Corporation"), a simple strategy simulation game where the player must manage an army of monsters in order to conquer the world within the time limit.

  • A playable demo of Quovadis 2: Wakusei Kyōshū Ovan Rei.

Also included is a variety of multimedia content such as creator interviews, game previews, and an art gallery.

title: Garou Densetsu 3: Road to the Final Victory
aka_titles: 餓狼伝説３ ～遥かなる闘い～
description:
Fatal Fury 3 retains the format and controls of the previous game in the series, Fatal Fury Special. However, the two-plane battle stages have been revamped into a three plane format known as the Oversway System. The player fights primarily in the middle plane or the main plane, but can move or "oversway" into either of the sway lines at the background (LP+LK) or foreground (LK+HP). When the player performs an attack in a sway plane (or an Oversway Attack), their character will return to the main plane. Likewise, the player can attack an opponent who is in a Sway Plane with an Anti-Oversway Attack. The player can also do a "Quick Sway" to avoid an attack, leaving the opponent vulnerable to a regular attack.

Other new techniques introduced in this installment includes controlling the height of the character's jump, block an opponent's attack at mid-air (Air Guard), and a new type of combo techniques known as Combination Arts, allowing the player to cancel a specific series (which varies between characters) of regular attacks from one to the other. In addition to the regular Special Moves, and the Super Special Moves which can only be performed when the life gauge is flashing red, each character also has a "Hidden Ability", which is a stronger version of a Super Special Move. A Hidden Ability occurs once in every 1024 chances whenever the player inputs the command for the character's Super Special Move. A Hidden Ability can also be used by activating "Super Mode" before a match using a secret code. The player then enters a specific command for the Hidden Ability when the life gauge is flashing red. Unlike Super Special Moves, a Hidden Ability can only be used once per round.

Fatal Fury 3 also features a Fighting Level system when fighting against the computer. When the player completes a round, their performance is graded from D to SSS. The final opponents the player faces at the end of the Single Player Mode is determined then by the player's average.

title: GeGeGe no Kitarō: Gentō Kaikitan
description: GeGeGe no Kitarō: Gentō Kaikitan is a sound novel adventure game based on the long-running manga series originally created by Shigeru Mizuki. It's winter, and snow has started to fall in the forest where Kitarō and his friends live... but even during winter, snow never normally falls in their forest, and Kitarō worries about what this might mean. The game follows standard sound novel format, with unvoiced dialogue and narration over still images depicting the current scene, occasionally interrupted by choices which branch the story path. There are three main scenarios that can unfold — one in which Kitarō investigates the recent disappearance of bodies, one in which he investigates the source of the mysterious snow, and one in which a fake copy of Kitarō himself appears — each with multiple endings depending on the player's choices.

title: Gekiretsu Pachinkers
description: Gekiretsu Pachinkers is a gambling simulation game featuring both pachinko and pachi-slot (slot machine) games. It includes four playable machines of each type, which are original and not licensed from any specific real-life machines. The main story mode casts the player as an unemployed young man who decides to use the small amount of money he has left to take up gambling full-time and try to make it rich. The player sets either a time limit or money goal for the game and then must spend each day visiting the parlors and gambling to try to win as much money as possible. It's also possible to play the lottery, take out loans, and even go out in the evening looking for a date. In addition to the story mode there is also a practice mode where each of the eight machines can be freely practiced without any time or money restrictions.

title: Gekirindan
description:
In 3195, Hokuto Higara, Shario Vissen, and their comrades join together in a fight against Huge Boss who has plans to render the human race extinct. To do this, the heroes will need to travel through various time periods in the past chasing down Huge Boss, whose disrupting human history.

Gekirindan is a vertical scrolling shoot-em-up. Players can choose from three different ship types (biplane, helicopter, and space fighter) to pilot, each equipped with their own unique firepower.. The game consists of 5 stages where the heroes travel through time from 3195 to 1942, 1999, 2373 and finally to 4580.

Some of the development team who helped create the game came from the recently defunct at the time Toaplan, hence the game sharing similarities to that companies previous shoot-'em-up efforts.

title: Gekirindan: Time Travel Shooting
description:
In 3195, Hokuto Higara, Shario Vissen, and their comrades join together in a fight against Huge Boss who has plans to render the human race extinct. To do this, the heroes will need to travel through various time periods in the past chasing down Huge Boss, whose disrupting human history.

Gekirindan is a vertical scrolling shoot-em-up. Players can choose from three different ship types (biplane, helicopter, and space fighter) to pilot, each equipped with their own unique firepower.. The game consists of 5 stages where the heroes travel through time from 3195 to 1942, 1999, 2373 and finally to 4580.

Some of the development team who helped create the game came from the recently defunct at the time Toaplan, hence the game sharing similarities to that companies previous shoot-'em-up efforts.

title: Gekitotsu Koushien
description: Gekitotsu Koushien is a super deep high school baseball tournament simulator. Like the Little League World Series, in Japan Koshien is a huge tournament. With over 4000 teams involved (and all of that data put into this game!) it is a great place for scouts to find professional players, and the game is a great and totally unique baseball experience.

title: Gekka no Kishi: Ōryūsen
description: Gekka no Kishi: Ōryūsen is a digital conversion of the traditional Japanese board game shogi for one or two players, based on the manga series Gekka no Kishi by Junichi Nojo. The main story mode follows protagonist Shosuke Himuro as he battles through a shogi tournament against each of the other opponents. There are also practice and jōseki modes, as well as a free battle mode for one or two players where any of the characters can be selected. The practice and free battle modes include a range of rule configuration options.

title: Gensou Suikoden
description:
Loosely based on the classic medieval Chinese novel Water Margins, the game is a fantasy RPG set in an imaginary universe, its main theme being political struggle. The hero of the game is the young son of Theo McDohl, a general who serves the Scarlet Moon Empire, presently controlling the land of Toran. Through a series of events the hero becomes involved in a rebellion against the Empire, led by an organization known as the Liberation Army. Will the hero find a new home there, will he be able to tear himself away from everything that has been sacred to him, including his own father?

Suikoden is a Japanese-style role-playing game with several unusual additions. There are three kinds of combat in the game, the most common one being the traditional turn-based party combat (players can have up to six people in their active party). Magic runes can be equipped on the player's characters which allow limited usage of offensive and healing spells. There are also a few army battles, where the player must control whole units of fighters, archers, magicians, etc., and one-on-one fights (duels).

The game allows the player to build and customize a castle, which serves as their home base and fortress. 108 characters can be recruited in the game, a tribute to 108 Stars Of Destiny in "Water Margins". Many of those characters will be available as active party members and participate in battles, while others will act as strategy advisers, or enhance the castle itself in various ways.

title: Gex
description:
Gex is a single-player side-scrolling platform game.

Gex is a television-obsessed gecko living alone in his mansion when he is pulled into the Media Dimension by Rez, the ruler of that television-based world. Rez wants to turn Gex into his new network mascot, leaving Gex trapped inside a realm built from parodies of television and movie genres. To escape, Gex must travel through the Media Dimension, collect remote controls, open new television worlds, and eventually confront Rez.

The game is organized around a map of television sets that act as entrances to side-scrolling stages. Each world is based on a different genre or channel theme, including horror, cartoons, jungle adventures, martial arts films, and Rez’s own mechanical domain. Stages contain hidden and visible remotes, and collecting enough of them unlocks additional levels and routes through the Media Dimension. Progression depends on both reaching stage exits and searching for remotes placed away from the main path.

Gex has standard platforming abilities such as running, jumping, and attacking, but his gecko traits define much of the gameplay. He can strike enemies with his tail, launch a short-range fire attack after collecting firefly power-ups, and use his tongue to grab certain items from a distance. He can also cling to and climb along many walls and ceilings, allowing stages to include vertical routes, hidden alcoves, and platform layouts that require movement in more than one direction.

Enemies and hazards vary by world theme. The horror stages include monsters and haunted scenery, cartoon stages use exaggerated traps and animated enemies, jungle areas feature natural hazards, and martial arts stages include enemies and obstacles based on action film settings. Gex can defeat many enemies with his tail attack or fire breath, but he must also avoid spikes, pits, projectiles, crushing traps, and other environmental dangers. Losing all health costs a life, and losing all lives ends the current attempt.

Collectibles and power-ups support both survival and completion. Bugs restore health or provide temporary abilities, paw coins contribute toward extra lives, and remote controls serve as the main progression items. Some levels also contain hidden video tapes or portals leading to bonus stages. Bonus stages are separate timed challenges, and completing them perfectly can reward pieces of an additional remote tied to optional completion.

Progress can be preserved differently depending on the version. The original release includes save support, while other versions use passwords unlocked through boss completion or hidden items. Later digital releases preserve the same basic campaign and mechanics, although presentation, controls, display options, and save handling may vary by platform.

title: Ghen War
description:
Ghen War is a classic first-person shooter. The solar system is being attacked by an evil force of aliens known as Ghen. The player is a Lieutenant surface engineer in a hypersuit, and it is his task to boot these aliens out of your world in twenty levels. From the cockpit of this hypersuit, the character operates lasers, grenades, mines, missiles and more while making his way across planet surfaces and city environments protecting the human race. It also has a claw that can operate elements in the environment and can send out a decoy of itself to confuse opponents.

The game is also one of the first to feature deformable terrain. Explosions make craters and firing into the environment can make it wear away.

title: Ginga Eiyū Densetsu
description: Ginga Eiyū Densetsu is a strategy simulation game, and part of a long-running series based on Yoshiki Tanaka's Legend of the Galactic Heroes science fiction novels. This console version is most similar to Ginga Eiyū Densetsu III, with the player taking the role of a top general in either the Galactic Empire or the Free Planets Alliance, commanding an entire fleet of ships. The game is divided into two main sections. In the strategy sections, the player is shown a full-scale map of the conflict, showing planets and the locations of ships; here the player may direct ships to move or engage with enemies, as well as converse with their officers. When battle starts, the player controls their fleet from a top-down perspective in semi realtime; each vessel can be given orders which they will carry out as instructed, but the action can also be paused at any point to issue new orders.

title: Ginga Eiyū Densetsu Plus
description:
Ginga Eiyū Densetsu Plus is a revised and expanded edition of the previous Sega Saturn entry in the long-running franchise, featuring several changes and new additions:

  • A new scenario mode featuring four campaigns, smaller in scope than the main game
  • Additional story event scenes featuring the voice cast from the anime
  • Various tweaks to the game mechanics such as a more restricted ability to resupply ships, resulting in a generally more difficult game

title: Ginga Ojōsama Densetsu Yuna 3: Lightning Angel
aka_titles: Ginga Ojōsama Densetsu Yuna: Final Edition
description:
Yuna and her friends are enjoying a relaxing day shopping when suddenly an intergalactic army appears with plans of conquering the Earth. With the fate of the planet on the line, Yuna and her rivals must put aside their differences and fight back against this intergalactic menace.

Ginga Ojōsama Densetsu Yuna 3: Lightning Angel is the third mainline game in the Galaxy Fräulein Yuna series. Gameplay is very different from prior entries in the series; while story sequences are presented in the same digital-comic format as the previous games, this time the battle sequences take center stage and are presented as isometric turn-based strategy battles in the vein of Tactics Ogre. The player can control a team of up to eight characters depending on the scenario, and each character has their own abilities and special techniques. Choices made during the adventure sequences can also affect the particular conditions of the following battle.

The later PlayStation version of the game, dubbed Final Edition, adds a two-player battle mode and hidden trading cards to collect, but is otherwise the same game.

title: Ginga Ojōsama Densetsu Yuna Remix
description: Galaxy Fräulein Yuna Remix is a remake of the original PC Engine game. The gameplay and story are identical to the original release, but this version features completely redrawn graphics at a higher quality, newly-arranged music, and additional newly-recorded voiceovers. There is also some additional bonus content such as an illustration gallery. The package also includes a 1997 calendar featuring new artwork by series illustrator Mika Akitaka.

title: Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works
aka_titles: Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna: Akitaka Mika IllustWorks
Galaxy Fraulein Yuna: Mika Akitaka Illust Works
description:
Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works (銀河お嬢様伝説 ユナ あきたか みか イラストワークス) is an art gallery for the Sega Saturn.

It was followed by Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works 2.

title: Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna: Mika Akitaka Illust Works 2
aka_titles: Galaxy Fraulein Yuna: Mika Akitaka Illust Works 2
description: Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works 2 (銀河お嬢様伝説 ユナ あきたか みか イラストワークス 2) is an art gallery for the Sega Saturn and "sequel" to Ginga Ojousama Densetsu Yuna Mika Akitaka Illust Works.

title: Girl Doll Toy: Tamashii o Kudasai...
description:
Girl Doll Toy is a love adventure game centered around a female android. The protagonist is a young college student working part-time at a laboratory that develops humanoid androids. Following a failed experiment, he takes home an android slated for disposal, fixes and upgrades her back into working order, and gives her the name Erika. While at first Erika is only able to directly obey commands, with the player's help she will gradually learn independent thought, emotion, and eventually even love.

The game plays in standard Japanese-style adventure format, with voiced dialogue and limited interaction through simple commands like talk and move. In addition to Erika, there are also several other romantic interests to pursue. The original PC version of the game includes explicit sexual content; the later Sega Saturn version censors the adult content and includes redrawn illustrations. The PC "Premium Version" has higher-quality illustration graphics based on the Saturn version but is otherwise the same.

title: Go III Professional: Taikyoku Igo
description: Go III Professional: Taikyoku Igo is a digital conversion of the ancient Chinese board game Go, part of a series of such games produced by Oxford Softworks. Like the previous release, this version offers play against 12 different CPU skill levels or a second player, options for 9x9, 13x13, and 19x19 game boards, handicap options, Chinese or Japanese rule variations, and a variety of board graphic options. New in this version is the option to set turn time limits for each player.

title: Godzilla: Rettō Shinkan
description:
Godzilla: Rettō Shinkan is an isometric-view real-time strategy game based on the famous kaiju monster movie series created by Toho. The player controls the JSDF forces and must attempt to repel Godzilla and other monsters, protecting Japan from destruction.

Each mission contains a different map, scenario, and set of monsters to fight off. The player can select to various military vehicles and issue various commands to each, such as to move to a specific location or attack a particular target. Multiple monsters often appear on the same map, and may even fight against each other — not necessarily a good thing as they may cause immense collateral damage. To clear a stage, the player must defeat all monsters on the stage before either their forces are depleted or the city sustains too much damage.

The game includes a story scenario with 10 missions, as well as a free mission mode with an additional 10 missions.

title: Goiken Muyou: Anarchy in the Nippon
description:
Goiken Muyou: Anarchy in the Nippon is a 3D fighting game in the vein of Virtua Fighter. Thus, similarly to VF series, there's no fireballs or other special attacks of that kind. But, unlike VF, there's no jump button, even if there's the possibility to jump over opponents for additional damage when they're on the ground. Also, a side-step dodge through the L and R buttons can be done, showing that the game also uses a 3D gameplay.

The game features a cast of 13 characters, 4 of them being the programmers themselves. The game modes available are varied: the classical arcade mode, a 1-round survival mode, a tournament against the CPU or against human opponents, spectator mode, training mode and there's also a character customization mode.

All menu options, character names, etc. are in Japanese.

title: Golden Axe: The Duel
description:
This is a one-on-one fighting game in the vein of Street Fighter 2 and Samurai Shodown featuring the cast of Sega's Golden Axe games (actually their fictional descendants). The game's story is that Death Adder has been resurrected and stolen the legendary Golden Axe from Gilius Thunderhead's family. For some reason Death Adder decided to set up a Street Fighter-like tournament to give his enemies an opportunity to slay him and prevent the end of the world.

The game play formula follows Street Fighter 2 closely with several playable characters that are essentially the same as the cast of the original Golden Axe (for all extents and purposes).

It’s essentially an elimination tournament with each character having special moves similar to that of Street Fighter 2 characters. You can play against another player or against the computer. It does feature scaling backgrounds similar to Samurai Shodown.

title: Gotha: Ismailia Seneki
description: Taking inspirations from Yoshiki Tanaka's "Legend of the Galactic Heroes", the game consists of two divided human factions at war after an increasingly hostile colonization across the Milky Way. The player simply positions tactical units in airspace, configures their stats then assigns each unit specific commands. If decisions are done correctly, a successful strategy ensures a victory against all enemy units.

title: Gradius: Deluxe Pack
aka_titles: グラディウス ＤＥＬＵＸＥ ＰＡＣＫ
description:
This pack contains both the arcade classics Gradius I and II, ported to Windows 95, Sony Playstation and Sega Saturn.

Story: the Bacterians are attacking the planet Gradius, and in a state-of-the-art fighter ship you have to stop them. Both games have similar gameplay and graphics, with only different music and level layout setting them apart.

Each of these side-scrolling shooters has over a dozen levels each, all of which are completely unique. There are no enemy types that are re-used from level to level (except for the boss who is the same in every level). You can collect powerups that provide things like extra speed, laser shots, target-seeking missiles, shields, etc.

While there have been many small modernising touches made to the games, there is still no ability to save. Be prepared to set aside a considerable amount of time to finish in one go.

title: Graduation for Windows 95
description:
Graduation is a Japanese anime "life-sim" game. You take the role of a homeroom teacher who is given the responsibility of teaching five girls in their last year of high school. You determine their class schedules, do guidance counseling, interfere with their weekend plans, and occasionally take to the streets to make sure they're not getting into trouble. Each of the girls has their own individual personality and problems, and the choices you make will determine whether they graduate from high school, what they do with their lives afterward, and whether or not they wind up hating your guts. Get them all into top colleges and your boss will praise your genius. If they all flunk or wind up wanting to marry you, you'll obviously be fired.

Despite what common sense and knowledge of the Japanese psyche might lead you to believe, this is not an adult (or hentai) game and there's no nudity and only an average amount of anime sexploitation.

title: Grand Slam
description:
Grand Slam is a baseball game that mixes arcade play with some simulation elements. Players can choose exhibition, tournament, full season, or "quick start" modes.

During baseball matches the player gets to control batters and pitchers. Batting and pitching both use tiered difficulty systems: batting ranges from simple timing swings to advanced control of swing power and strike-zone placement, while pitching uses a “golf swing” style meter where precision and control matter.

The game also includes simple team management gameplay, with the ability to buy and sell players.

Other highlights amongst Grand Slam's feature set include:

  • A trade AI engine that would examine the needs of a team and decide if a proposed trade was in its best interest.

  • Catcher AI and pitch signals, helping a player learn how to pitch to each batter's strengths and weaknesses.

  • Attention to details and baseball flavor, such as players that would blow bubble gum bubbles during an at bat, light- hearted commentary, an All Star Break during season play (complete with a working voting ballot), and an in-game JumboTron scoreboard that would show animations after home runs.

Grand Slam was one of the early adopters of 3D accelerator card technology and also offered full 3D play in software alone. The Playstation and Saturn versions were 3D by default.

title: Grandia
description:
The ancient Angelou civilization has ceased to exist centuries ago, and technology in the world develops rapidly. General Baal, the head of the militaristic Garlyle Forces, organizes an excavation of ancient ruins, apparently for philanthropic reasons. Meanwhile, Justin, a young boy from the nearby town of Parm, decides to investigate the ruins in search of the Spirit Stone, an artefact that once belonged to his missing father. A mysterious holographic image tells him that he should travel to faraway lands to discover the stone's true power, and he embarks on the most dangerous adventure of his life without hesitation.

Grandia is a Japanese-style role-playing game. The characters are represented by 2D sprites which are moved around over 3D backgrounds in towns and dungeons. The game makes use of anime-style cutscenes to advance the story. Combat is initiated by coming into contact with enemies on the screen, rather than through random battles. Battles occur in pseudo-real-time, using an 'IP Gauge' to determine when a character takes action. Striking at the right time or with the right ability can even delay or cancel an enemy's turn.

The characters in the game gradually advance in level as they gain experience points for killing monsters. Characters also gain experience based on the weapon (e.g. sword, mace, whip, etc.) or magic (e.g. fire, water, etc.) that they use, powering up their spells and learning new ones from continuous usage. There are a large number of spells, weapons, and other items to use throughout the game.

title: Grandia: Digital Museum
description: Grandia: Digital Museum is a fan disc containing production materials and bonus content for the game Grandia. It is presented as a museum which the characters are visiting, and there is a dungeon which the player can explore to fight monsters and unlock additional materials for viewing in the museum portion. In addition to a gallery of production artwork, there is also a radio drama with a new scenario not in the main game, a bestiary, and a selection of save files which can be used in the main game to replay the game's most famous moments.

title: Grandia: Prelude
description: Grandia: Prelude is a preview demo disc for Sega Saturn.

title: Grandread
description:
In the distant future of the year UC 1715, Earth's solar system is suddenly attacked by an unknown alien force. A young cadet named Nagumo is on board one of the attacked ships, but the ship's crew are saved by a relic of a mysterious ancient civilization that had been hidden on Jupiter: the Grandread-class starship Dragonalis, which has a will of its own and recognizes Nagumo as its captain. The last hope for humanity now falls under the command of of this young man.

Grandread is a space opera hex-strategy game in which the player controls fleets of space battleships in turn-based combat. The player controls many ships at any given time, which each have varying capabilities and weaponry, and can even move multiple ships into a formation to control them as a single unit. There are multiple factions interacting in the story, and depending on the player's actions it is possible to ally with or even recruit many enemy units, and the game includes multiple endings and branching story paths.

title: Greatest Nine '96
description:
Greatest Nine '96 is a baseball game featuring featuring an NPB (Nippon Professional Baseball) license and all twelve teams and all players from the Central and Pacific Leagues of Japanese baseball for the 1996 season, and the second game in the series after Kanzen Chūkei Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine.

The game is once again presented in a realistic visual style using digitized photographs of the players. The major changes over the previous game are updated rosters for the new season, and the addition of licensed real-world stadiums instead of the fictional ones found in the first game. Game modes available are identical to the previous title: Exhibition, Pennant Race, Tournament, All-Star, and Home Run Contest, plus a full Team Edit mode and player database.

A modified version featuring American MLB teams and players was released worldwide as World Series Baseball II.

title: Gremlin Demo Disk
description: Gremlin Interactive Demo Disk, not to be confused with the similarly titled Gremlin Interactive Demo Disc, is a Sega Saturn demo disc containing demos of Loaded, UEFA Euro 96 England and Actua Golf; three games published by Gremlin Interactive. It was distributed in the United Kingdom alongside the first issue of Total Saturn.

title: Grid Runner
description: Aliens have captured you and you are forced to play a deadly game of what appears to be capture the flag combined with tag. Race your way around the area and capture the required number of flags before being touched by your opponent. If they do touch you, you must find and touch them before they capture the right number of flags. Who ever is "it" cannot capture flags until their opponent is tagged. There is a story and 2 player versus mode. Through the story, you face many different enemies with ranging speeds and firepower (gun fire only slows down the person shot, there is no health bar).

title: Groove on Fight: Gōketsuji Ichizoku 3
aka_titles: グルーヴオンファイト 豪血寺一族３
description:
Another entry in the Power Instinct series. Groove on Fight changes the entire atmosphere of the game and introduces several gameplay changes to the original formula.

The game is set once again around the fighting tournament organized to decide the fate of the Gouketsuji clan, but the action takes place decades after the last tournament in a dark retro-futuristic world. Additionally, the bloodlines of the Gouketsuji clan have grown thin and now the tournament has been opened to foreign families, thus resulting in a new cast of characters that all but replaces the original fighters.

Gameplay-wise Groove on Fight plays as a team-based 2-on-2 2D fighting game, with each player selecting two fighters and being able to tag freely between them at any point in the fights a la X-Men vs. Street Fighter. Your objective is to defeat all the challenger teams and then face of against your teammate to decide who gets to be the new head of the clan. Also a new dodge and knockout attack has been added to the basic controls, and the game features four player simultaneous play in Vs mode.

title: Groove on Fight: Gōketsuji Ichizoku 3 (Kakuchō RAM Cartridge Tsuki!)
description: This release of Groove on Fight includes the game along with a Sega Saturn 1MB RAM Expansion Cartridge.

title: GT24
description: GT24 is an arcade-style racing game and a modified port of the 1996 arcade game Super GT 24h. It features one new track for a total of three in both regular and reverse configurations, two new vehicles for a total of six, and five different pit crews. Three game modes are included: Time Trial, Grand Prix, and a 24-hour Endurance race mode (which can be configured as 12, 24, or 48 minutes real time) that includes a full day/night cycle that changes as the race progresses.

title: Guardian Force
description:
Guardian Force is a shoot-em-up where the player controls a tank that can fire in eight directions. While the body of the tank can be moved freely around the screen, each press of the outer buttons will rotate the tank's turret 45 degrees clockwise or counter-clockwise. The tank/screen will scroll vertically for much of the game, but will sometimes be reoriented midlevel to scroll horizontally or diagonally.

There are five unique weapons which can be used: a standard shmup spread shot (Tusk), a non-continuing laser (Feeler), what is essentially a giant yo-yo that can be launched and retracted (Fang), a short-ranged explosive attack (Horn), and a bevy of missiles (Beak). Each of them has a designated color (red, yellow, green, purple, and blue respectively) and special attack (bomb equivalent), and will increase in damage/ability as the tank's level increases. The tank also has a standard repeating shot that will always fire in the direction the screen is scrolling.

Regular play revolves around a number of onscreen collectibles. The standard weapon power-up will cycle through the aforementioned weapon colors before eventually going dark, floating or fading away. It will change the player's current weapon to the one of its color when picked up, or upgrade the tank's level if it matches the color of the player's current weapon. In addition, there are pink gems that drop from particular enemies that also upgrade the tank's level, a missile power-up that will add either homing or straight-shooting rockets to the player's current weapon, and a special attack refill (equivalent to one shot).

Certain enemies and destructible objects will also drop medals when destroyed. The first medal will always spawn at level I, worth 100 points. Once it's collected, the next medal spawned will increase in rank and double in score; this continues until medals reach level VIII/12,800 points. If a medal goes uncollected for whatever reason (it either disappears or is overtaken by the scrolling screen), the next medal spawned will reset to level I. Score bonuses can also be had from quickly killing a number of midbosses, as well as collecting the weapon power-up once it stops cycling through the weapon colors.

title: Guardian Heroes
description:
Ages ago, the spirits of Earth and Sky waged war on each other. Neither could win, and eventually the Sky Spirits bestowed some humans with their powers, turning them into wizards and allies in the war. The Earth Spirits were banished into darkness; but the Sky Spirits feared the human wizards and cast them underground as well.

Years have passed, and a powerful wizard named Kanon escaped from the gloomy prison and turned the human land into a puppet state trembling before his might. One legendary sword is said to bring an end to Kanon's reign. Four warriors - Han, Randy, Nicole and Ginjirou - retrieved the sword, but knights sent by Kanon are determined to take it away and destroy it at all costs. Aided by the renegade knight Serena, the four heroes must keep the world safe and protect themselves against the onslaught.

Guardian Heroes is a hybrid of a side-scrolling beat-em-up and a role-playing game. The four initial player characters are distinguished by their attributes and abilities: Han is a strong fighter who cannot use magic; Randy is a sorcerer who can cast attack spells but is physically more vulnerable; Ginjirou is a ninja-type, agile character; finally, Nicole has weak attacks but can cast healing spells.

The fighting mechanic is slightly deeper than in most other games of this type, with light and heavy attacks, special moves (executed the same way as usually in fighting games), magical attacks and the ability to block. Defeating enemies yields experience points, with which the player can upgrade the characters between levels, sharing them between various factors such as strength, speed, constitution and magic resistance.

The game has a branching storyline that develops according to the player's selection of stages. There is also a "Karma" system that evaluates the player's actions depending on how he or she treats enemies or innocent people in the game world.

Even in one-player mode there are always two controllable characters on screen - the player commands the other character by changing his "mood" - aggressive, cowardly etc. - of which there are six. On top of this, it is possible to play the game as a more traditional beat-em-up with up to six players (human or AI-controlled); in this mode it is possible to play as any character encountered during the main game mode.

title: Gun & Frontier
description:
Gun & Frontier is a 1990 arcade vertical shoot-'em-up. The setting of the series and purportedly of the game is an extraterrestrial American Wild West, with the player fighting to defend settlers from airborne pirates -- the game, though, actually looks to be an entirely standard military-themed shooter, with the player's jet fighter set against tanks and other airplanes. Guns and bombs are levelled-up and collected by dropped power-ups, which are money-themed, with the gun upgrades shown as American dimes and bombs as gold bars.

Gun & Frontier was ported to the Sega Saturn in 1997 and was later included in the cross-platform compilation Taito Legends 2 in 2006.

title: Gunbird
description:
Gunbird is a vertically scrolling shoot 'em up developed by Psikyo. It hit the Japanese arcade in 1994 and was followed by a Japanese release to the Saturn and the Playstation in the following year.

The game is set in a fantasy setting with steampunk elements. Lush forests and medieval castles meet steam trains and mech robots. Instead of piloting the genre-traditional space ships, Gunbird lets the player chose between five different characters (Ash, Marion, Valnus, Yuan Nang and Tetsu) who traverse the game world on broomstick, jet packs and pedal-powered helicopters on a quest to find the pieces of a magic mirror across seven stages.

Unorthodox vehicles aside, the gameplay follows traditional genre standards. The main goal is to dodge all bullets that fill the screen while collecting power-ups to make the character stronger. Gunbird features one power-up that incrementally increases the firepower of the standard weapon (P-items) as well as additional ammo for the screen-clearing special ability (B-items). Standard weapon and special ability differ from character to character. Where some characters excel in high firepower in a straight line others allow for a wider spread of bullets or additional homing missiles.

title: GunBlaze S
description:
GunBlaze S is a remake of GunBlaze.

The story remains the same as in the original game, and the dialogues almost the same, with a few minor omissions. The gameplay is also largely unchanged.

The main difference between the two versions is in the graphics. Many locations and cut scenes in GunBlaze S were re-drawn from scratch. Some of the locations have different layout. Generally, the graphics are clearly more detailed, even though they retain the simple 2D top-down style of the original. There are voice-overs for all story-related dialogues in this version.
