There is also another significant change: the original GunBlaze had scenes with nudity; GunBlaze S has none. The sexual innuendo is present in the dialogues, and there are scenes with scantily clad young girls; but the adult content is gone.

title: Gungriffon
description: Pilot an enormous walking mech to complete missions set all over the world in late 21st century warfare fighting other mechs, trucks and helicopters. The missions, set in different weathers and at different times of day, usually have specific objectives, be they search and destroy, protecting allies or killing everything. Four weapons are available: the main cannon; a weak machine gun that overheats with prolonged use; clusters of grenades and limited supplies of homing missiles. Damage repair and extra ammo is available from supply helicopters, but these are vulnerable to attack. Ally mechs can be useful, but it is the player who has to do most of the work by far, battling mechs that are sometimes faster and more agile, therefore a certain amount of strategy and planning is required.

title: Gungriffon II
description: Gungriffon II is 3D FPP mecha simulator, similar to Armored Core or Mechwarrior, continuation of Gungriffon, released only in Japan. The player is a pilot of giant humanoid looking, heavily armed robot. He must complete various missions (search & destroy, guard various objects, etc.), and fight against other robots and tanks. Various robots and equipment for combat can be selected. The game also has two additional game modes, a special virtual training mode, and survival mode. Gungriffon II supports up to 2 players on one machine and 4 with cable link for multiplayer.

title: Gungriffon II (Taisen Cable Dōkonban)
description: This bundle package includes Gungriffon II along with a serial Link Cable accessory.

title: Gussun Oyoyo-S
description: This port of Risky Challenge adds 34 more levels to the original 40. It also incorporates touched up cutscenes with voice-overs as well as intermission screens between levels.

title: GVector
description: GVector is a sci-fi chase-view rail shooter in the style of Panzer Dragoon. The player pilots a small fighter craft and must fight off an alien invasion of Earth. There are two weapons at the player's disposal: a standard foward shot, and a homing laser that can lock on to up to eight targets; the more targets locked and destroyed simultaneously, the greater the bonus points awarded. There are a total of six stages, each with an encounter with a large boss enemy at the end, and the game includes a standard story mode as well as a score attack mode where any stage previously completed can be played and practiced for high scores.

title: Gyuwambler Jiko Chūshinha 2: Gekitō! Tokyo Mahjongland-hen
description:
Gyuwambler Jiko Chūshinha 2: Gekitō! Tokyo Mahjongland-hen is a riichi mahjong game based on the manga by Masayuki Katayama, and a sequel to Katayama Masayuki no Mahjong Dōjō. The game includes three different modes: the main Story Mahjong mode lets the player select either Hideyuki or Dorao and follows their visit to a strange mahjong-themed amusement park; Date Mahjong Anniversary mode lets the player pick from one of nine male characters and attempt to win the heart of one of 18 female characters by playing mahjong; and Free Battle mode is a standard match play mode where any of the 51 characters can be freely selected for a regular match.

The later Sega Saturn version features completely redone graphics and sound, and includes an additional 5 characters in the free battle mode, but is otherwise the same game.

title: Habitat II
description:
Habitat II, later rebranded Habitat II: Elysium, is an online virtual world and a follow-up to Fujitsu Habitat, refreshing the experience with new graphics and events and bringing the service to home console for the first time. Players create a custom avatar and hang out in the city Elysium with other players. The focus is on social interaction with other players and avatar customization; one can chat with other players in the same area, and there are numerous shops around the game world where the new clothing and accessories can be acquired. There are also various simple minigames, such as a dice game for multiple players, and special events held by the service operators.

The computer versions of the game were distributed as a free download, while the Sega Saturn version was only available packaged together with the Saturn Keyboard peripheral, and never sold as a separate release. All versions required a monthly subscription and per-minute service fee, and players from all platforms could play together in the same game world. Service ended in August 1999.

title: Hanagumi Taisen Columns
aka_titles: 樱花大战 花组方块
description:
Hanagumi Taisen Columns is a Sakura Wars spinoff that crosses the series over with SEGA's classic puzzle game Columns. The core gameplay follows the classic Columns rules: players control falling columns of three blocks of assorted colours with the goal of creating horizontal, vertical, or diagonal sets of 3 pieces of the same colour. Unlike the original Columns, this game introduces a new Puyo Puyo-style competitive mechanic. As players perform combos, a super gauge fills, with longer combos rewarding progressively larger amounts of super meter. Each time the meter fills to a full level, players are given the option to keep charging or to perform an offensive or defensive special technique. Offensive attacks send garbage blocks to the opponent's side; these pieces have the same colours as normal pieces, but can't be used in a combo until a certain number of turns passes. Defensive techniques remove lines of blocks from the player's side. The longer the player charges up their super meter, the more powerful techniques become.

A visual novel story mode gives the player a traditional Sakura Wars-style story, complete with branching story paths using the series's trademark LIPS option-selection system. However, instead of mech battles, characters settle their differences with matches of Columns. The story follows the troupe's production of Cinderella, with each character vying for the best parts in the show.

title: Hang-On GP
description:
Hang-On GP features three tracks: Albatross Cliff Reef, Great Crimson Wall, and New Dwells. Each track contains an additional route that becomes available after a high placing. This makes a total of six possible races.

Players can choose from among ten motorcycles to use during a race as well as an automatic or manual transmission for each. Players can also decide how the bike should control, highside or power slide.

Placing in the top three on any of the first three tracks will release the additional routes. When players place in the top three on the additional routes an endurance mode will be available. In endurance mode players attempt to complete as many laps as they can in 10 minutes.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Hankou Shashin: Shibarareta Shōjotachi no Mita Mono wa?
aka_titles: The Photograph of a Crime: Hankou Shashin: Shibarareta Shoujo-tachi no Mita Mono wa
description:
An idol group known as Otomegumi (乙女組) is staying at the western-style boarding house in a spa resort in Izu (伊豆), Japan. You, Takeshi Gouda (郷田 武史), as a professional photographer came, along with your team which includes Ryouichi Akada (赤田 良一), your editor, and Takuya Sasaki (佐々木 拓也), your young assistant, to make a photo album of that very idol group. As you arrive at the boarding house you meet with Otomegumi idol group consisting of Rei, Maki, and Shouko, as well as with some other suspicious looking characters on the premise. Due to a sudden storm, you decide to wait it out and use that opportunity to get to know everyone a little better. But the evening doesn't go as well as expected and some unpleasant words are exchanged with Seiji Tashiro (田代 成治), an idol group manager. Ryouichi had to step in a couple of time to prevent things from escalating, but by the time everyone went to bed it all seemed to have quiet down.

Next morning, you, the idol group, Ryouichi, Takuya, and Chieko Naemura (苗村 千恵子) who is a stylist for Otomegumi idol group all went to hot springs for some photo session. The photos are going fine and things were about to wrap up when the distressing rumor about someone being dead back at the boarding house have reached you. You all pack your things and head back to the boarding house. There, you find the owners of the boarding house, Kyousuke Nakagawa (中川 京介) and his wife Reiko Nakagawa (中川 麗子), standing in front of a room of none other than Seiji Tashiro who was a troublemaker since the moment you met him. At closer inspection you soon realize it's a murder as he appears to have been stabbed with a knife. But who would have a reason to kill him? Suspects... motives... opportunities... anyone could be the killers, and to top it all, you cannot call the police as phone line appears to be dead. With the killer among you, what was to be a nice relaxing vacation is turning into a murder mystery that is far from being over.

The game plays like a straight visual novel consisting of text over current background which is comprised on many photo stills to match the dialogue and emotion of the scene in question. Occasionally the player is presented with dialogue choices which may affect the current situation but there is no real branching in the main story, just different reactions by the people addressing you. Voice-acting is almost non-present and appears only in key dialogues between the player and the idols, and usually for no more than a single short sentence. In photo session player can take a limited number of photos but does not control camera movement, instead, camera moves up and down once and the player has the chance to take a photo or keep the movie to use on the next pose. Limited bonus contained in a package is an envelope containing an actual photo from one of the photo sessions in the game.

title: Hansha de Spark!
description: Hansha de Spark! is a 2D top-down arcade game, similar in style to Bomberman, but instead of using bombs, players can shoot energy balls that receive power by bouncing off the special walls. They can collect bonuses to gain advantage. Game features both single-player mode where the player fights against zombie-like regular enemies and bosses, and a multi-player mode where you fights against other players or bots.

title: Harukaze Sentai V-Force
description:
Long ago, civilization flourished on Venus. The environmental protection agency Goa Del maintained the planet. However, in the name of self-defense, Goa Del began to develop weaponry against the wishes of the house of lords, El Doral, and eventually war broke out between the two groups. The queen of El Doral sent her young daughter Rabis on a shuttle to Earth, but in an attack, the shuttle was separated from the convoy and made an emergency landing on the moon. In a last-ditch effort, El Doral brought the way to an end with the "organic weapon" HN-01, and the defeated Goa Del fled into the reaches of space.

Two thousand years later, the descendants of Goa Del, now calling themselves the Baskille Empire, are rapidly expanding their power. One day, a bright light appears near Venus, and the Baskille Empire has appeared, returning to take back their planet. And now, three sisters living on Earth, distant descendants of El Doral, have gotten caught up in the fight.

Harukaze Sentai V-Force is an isometric strategy RPG similar to Front Mission or Super Robot Taisen. The game follows Natsuki, Mizuki, and Kagetsu, three sisters who are pilots in the Earth Defense Force. Each mission allows you to configure your character's weaponry, and as they fight, they will gain experience and level up. Before and after each mission, fully-animated cutscenes drive the plot forward, and sometimes they will appear at crucial points during a mission as well.

title: Hatsukoi Monogatari
description: Hatsukoi Monogatari is a life sim/love adventure game and a remake of the 1993 PC game of the same title. While the story and gameplay are largely identical to the original version, this remake adds a new character — the angel Liliana — along with new events and endings. The artwork has also been completely redone in a different style, with new character designs by a different artist than the original release.
publishers: Tokuma Shoten Co., Ltd. Intermedia Company

title: Hattrick Hero '95
description: Hattrick Hero S reminds us of the side-scrolling arcade soccer games in 2D that were popular in the coin-ops of the 90's, especially of the Super Sidekicks series. In this game we can choose among a large list of national teams (42 in total) from all the continents, and we can compete in either a friendly match, a championship, a world league or a penalty shoot out session. Each team counts with an "Ace" player (you can guess who he is by seeing "Ace" above his head during a match), or in other words, the man with the best skills in the team. The game also counts with a system that lets you execute special actions during a match, but these have to be "exchanged" for something called units (you start every match with 20 of them), so for example, if you want to execute an Hyper Shoot (the most effective shoot in the game) you will have 6 units less. These actions must be executed by your "Ace", and he can be as far as the area as he wants, because in all cases the shoot will still be almost unstoppable.

title: Hattrick Hero S
description: Hattrick Hero S reminds us of the side-scrolling arcade soccer games in 2D that were popular in the coin-ops of the 90's, especially of the Super Sidekicks series. In this game we can choose among a large list of national teams (42 in total) from all the continents, and we can compete in either a friendly match, a championship, a world league or a penalty shoot out session. Each team counts with an "Ace" player (you can guess who he is by seeing "Ace" above his head during a match), or in other words, the man with the best skills in the team. The game also counts with a system that lets you execute special actions during a match, but these have to be "exchanged" for something called units (you start every match with 20 of them), so for example, if you want to execute an Hyper Shoot (the most effective shoot in the game) you will have 6 units less. These actions must be executed by your "Ace", and he can be as far as the area as he wants, because in all cases the shoot will still be almost unstoppable.

title: Haunted Casino
description:
Haunted Casino is an adult-themed horror adventure gambling game. The player enters the titular "Haunted Casino", where a demon queen and her followers -- all of them attractive women -- lure in and trap unsuspecting men as their playthings. The player must explore the mansion-like casino in first person, avoiding traps and looking for helpful items, and eventually find each of the demons to challenge them to various gambling games such as roulette and blackjack. As the player wins coins, the demons will gradually remove their clothing until they are completely nude, at which point they can be sealed within a playing card. If the player loses, then their soul is lost for eternity to the demon queen.

There are seven demons throughout the casino to find, each of whom has a particular game they like best. After sealing a particular demon, the player can visit a viewing room and spend coins to view various nude scenes of that girl. The game is divided into three floors, and after sealing all the demons on a floor, the player will receive a key that leads to the next one. The ultimate goal is to seal the demon queen on the third floor.

title: Heartbeat Scramble
description:
Heartbeat Scramble is a love simulation game in the style of Tokimeki Memorial, in which the player takes the part of a high school student trying to keep up with his studies, a part-time job and, of course, a healthy social life. Unusual among such games, all the in-game characters and locations are portrayed using photographs of real-life actors, rather than the illustrated characters usually found in dating sims.

The game follows the main character through three years of high school life. The player can choose an activity for each day, such as studying or going to a part-time job to earn money, which affects their status and relationships with six potential romantic interests. The player can ask girls out on dates, and numerous events happen at fixed dates, such as school festivals, a ski resort trip, and ultimately graduation.

title: Hebereke's Popoitto
description: Hebereke's Popoitto is a Tetris variant. The goal in each level is to remove the blocks already on the playfield, representing characters from the franchise. Other blocks fall down from the top of the screen and have to be steered to the right place before touching the ground or another block. When four or more of the same blocks are together, they vanish. The catch of this variant is that the blocks which have to be removed move over the playfield. The player takes the role of the penguin Hebereke who wants to win a tournament against his friends.

title: Heim Waltz
description: Heim Waltz (ハイムワルツ) is a piece of Japanese Sega Saturn software, containing an interactive tour.

title: Heir of Zendor: The Legend and The Land
description:
Heir of Zendor: The Legend and The Land is a turn-based strategy game and a sequel to Gotha: Ismailia Seneki.

The game is set on Zendor, a planet with floating continents thanks to anti-gravity ore. The most important resource is water, which after the Great Wars still remained only in the continent named Terra Sancta. The player assumes the role of the Prince of Zendor, commander of the Zendorian Squadron of the Royal Alliance Expeditionary Forces and needs to defeat the "Five Kings".

As any strategy game, Heir of Zendor has objective driven stages called missions. Completing these objectives the player reaches new missions. The player needs to deploy ships, arm them, move each unit individually or as a complete formation, and when the player's units are close enough to attack the enemies, command their in battle (that consists in: select a weapon, select a target and shoot). Turn ends when all player's units moved or attacked an enemy.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Heisei Tensai Bakabon: Susume! Bakabons
description:
Heisei Tensai Bakabon: Susume! Bakabons is a competitive falling-block puzzle game based on the 1990 animated series Heisei Tensai Bakabon. Pairs of blocks in four colors drop from the top of the screen, and the goal is to line up two or more blocks of the same color, with another pair of a different matching color at either end. Any blocks on top of the ones cleared will fall into the open space, potentially comboing together into chains. Clearing multiple sets of blocks in a combo or chain will send garbage blocks to the opponent's playfield, and also charge up a super move that triggers automatically at a certain threshold which can clear a large number of blocks from the playfield.

The game has a single-player story mode in which Bakabon's dad, refusing to wake up in the morning, gets sucked up by his wife's vacuum cleaner and sent to a strange puzzle world where he must defeat the other characters from the show in puzzle battles. There is also a two-player versus mode with nine playable characters.

title: Heiwa Pachinko Sōshingeki
description: Heiwa Pachinko Sōshingeki is a pachinko simulation game featuring recreations of four real-life pachinko machines licensed from pachinko manufacturer Heiwa: CD Meiga, CD Ryujin, Daisangen, and Hayabusa. The main game mode has the player visiting various pachinko parlors to play each of the machines and attempt to win as much as possible. The game also includes two customization modes: the first lets the player adjust the arrangement of the pins on each board, while the second lets the player combine various layouts and background graphics to create a custom machine.

title: Herc's Adventures
description:
Ahhh...ancient Greece. A fertile land, full of wine, women, and some of the best gyros you'll ever taste. Thanks to Persephone, the Greek goddess of spring and fertility, Greece is a wonderful paradise. But now the lord of the Underworld, Hades, has gone and kidnapped Persephone, causing the land to slowly wither away! Zeus, the King of the Gods, needs help in saving her, so who do you call? None other than three of the greatest warriors in the land!

You can choose from the big 'n' buff Herc, the super swift Atlanta, or the young and street-smart Jason, each of whom have their own weapons and strengths. The game's 40 levels include many further variations and pastiches of Greek mythology and legend.

It's all up to you to rescue Persephone and give Hades a beatdown he'll never forget!

title: Hexen: Beyond Heretic
description:
Hexen is the sequel to Heretic. While the Heretic was destroying D'Sparil, the other two Serpent Riders have come to your dimension and slaughtered everyone. Or so they thought. Three humans have managed to escape with their lives and now seek vengeance against the Serpent Rider Korax who remains in their world.

Like Heretic, Hexen is a fantasy game based on an enhanced Doom engine. All of Heretic's innovations like vertical looking, flying, and the inventory system have been carried over. The new major changes this time around are three characters for the player to choose from and the level hub system. The characters are the Fighter, the Cleric, and the Mage. Each one has four unique weapons and different levels of speed and armor.

The hub system steps away from the traditional "single levels stringed along into episodes" system which had been carried over into the FPS genre from sidescrollers and made popular by Wolfenstein 3D. In Hexen's hub system each episode is still made up of interconnected levels, but most of the levels are connected to a single "hub" level through portals. There are also portals between some of the "spoke" levels. Many of the puzzles in Hexen require travel back and forth between different levels.

Other innovations in Hexen include weather effects, jumping, earth-quakes, and destructible objects such as trees and vases. The game also includes scripted sequences created with a language called ACS, allowing for much more complex puzzles and dramatic scenes.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Hi-Octane
description:
A futuristic racing game with hover cars, in the same line as Wipeout, using a modified version of the Magic Carpet 2 engine.

Gameplay takes a straightforward approach, with the directional keys controlling the steering and throttle, and three keys to fire the minigun, missiles or charge the booster. While the minigun has unlimited ammo, both fuel, armour and missiles must be replenished by passing through some marked areas or picking up powerups in the track or by left destroyed opponents. While the vehicles float on the track they are still influenced by the ground material: they slow down on dirt and even more on water. Each track has a number of shortcuts or alternate routes that offer powerups, and some tracks feature gates and ramps that open or close randomly.

Includes 9 tracks and several game modes (for Saturn owners and PC players with the 1.2 patch installed) such as single race mode (with option to change the number of laps), a Championship mode, Split Screen, Clone Race (beating the ghost of the best race time), Death Match (Where instead of finishing first what matters is finish alive and with the most kills) and Hot Seat, where up to eight players can compete in the same race by taking turns, with the computer taking control of the players' vehicles waiting for their turn. There are six hover cars to choose from: the fast Flexiwing and Outrider, the balanced KD-1 Speeder and Vampyr and the slow but armed to the teeth Berserker and Jugga. In addition to the natural capacity of each, their Minigun, Missle and Booster capacities can be upgraded by picking up powerups during the race. There are Eight teams to choose from, which change the colour of the vehicle: Mad Medicine (white), Bullfrog (aqua green), Storm Riders (purple), Fire Phreaks (orange), DethFest (blue), Foo Fighters (yellow), Gorehounds (red) and Assassins Anonymous (black).

title: Hi-Octane: The Track Fights Back!
description:

title: Hideyoshi Nobunaga Set
description:
This bundle packages two of Koei's Japanese-history simulation games together at a budget price:

  • Taikō Risshiden II
  • Nobunaga no Yabō: Tenshōki

title: High Velocity: Mountain Racing Challenge
description:
High Velocity is an arcade-style racing game that allows the player to drive sports cars on twisty roads around Japanese mountain tops. There are 3 tracks on which to drive, each with forward and reverse routes. The player may choose from one of 6 different cars, each with different driving characteristics. There are three different game modes:

  • King Battle: The player competes in one of 6 head-to-head races against the computer on each of the tracks. Win all the races and be declared King of the Mountain.
  • VS. Battle: The player competes head to head against another player.
  • Time Trial: The player races for the best time around a course.

title: Highschool Terra Story
description:
Highschool Terra Story is a visual novel-style love adventure game. The protagonist is a second-year high school student at Satsuki Academy, who has learned that he'll be moving in three months and decides to pursue romance with his classmates before then. The game is a simulation-style game in the vein of Tokimeki Memorial, with the player's actions affecting three different stats — intelligence, athletics, and creativity — which in turn determine which of the six romantic interests will show interest in the main character.

The original PC version of the game includes explicit sexual content; the later Saturn port is still suggestive but censors the explicit content. The Saturn version also adds the option to view each girl's daily schedule, and includes some minor scenario additions.

title: Highway 2000
description: Highway 2000 is a racing game that offers five racing tracks and three cars (Mad Viper, Dark Nebula and Rapid Fire) with different statistics based on speed, acceleration, handling and grip. The game has several modes like the tournament mode in which you race against AI-controlled opponents and a time trial mode. There is also a two-player race mode in where you race another player in split-screen.

title: Himitsu Sentai Metamor V
description:
Fourth-grader Sakie Shinjō has just transferred to a new elementary school at the start of the semester, but any hopes she may have had for a normal school life have been quickly dashed. She's run into a strange woman in the hall cosplaying as a nurse, gotten involved in a battle on the playground with Baron Dandy of the Adonis Empire, and finally been recruited by Space Detective Shatner, the leader of the transforming justice squad Metamor V, as the second-generation Metamor Red.

Himitsu Sentai Metamor V is a visual novel-style adventure game starring a cast of transforming magical girls. The game is divided into chapters and follows the five members of the Metamor V squad, all of them elementary school students and classmates of Sakie's. Much of the game consists of conversation sequences with other characters; the player's reactions and choices will affect Sakie's trust level with her squadmates, and through conversations the player will also learn different key words. Both of these are important during the battle sequences, in which the player must combine words in order to create the most effective special attacks. There is no lose condition, but the player is graded on how quickly they defeat opponents, which affects trust levels and ultimately the game's ending.

The later PlayStation "Deluxe" version includes an extra bonus side scenario and additional voice acting, but is otherwise the same game.

title: Hissatsu Pachinko Collection
description:
Hissatsu Pachinko Collection is a pachinko simulation game featuring recreations of six real-life pachinko machines licensed from pachinko manufacturers Daiichi and Fuji: Dance Dance 2, Arejin, CR Big Slotter 2, Sunrise, Excite, and Arrange Man.

The main game mode is a simulation mode where the player visits various pachinko parlors which each have their own operating hours and sets of machines. In addition to playing various machines with the goal of winning as much as possible, the player can also return home to rest or play a round of mahjong against the computer. In addition, there is also a free play mode where the player can practice on any specific machine with a variety of options, as well as an online competition mode where the player enters a password from a (now-discontinued) online service to compete with other players.

title: Hissatsu!
description:
Hissatsu! is an action game set in Japan during the Edo period, inspired by the popular Hissatsu historical drama series.

The game has a similar gameplay to the Shinobi series. At the start of each level, players are given a choice of playing as 2 characters out of the available 4 (Including Nakamura Mondo from the aforementioned series) and the game features 5 levels in total. The story is told through cutscenes and a gory cutscene depicting how the protagonist dealt the finishing blow to the enemy is shown after defeating each boss. Each protagonist has their own weapons which can be short range or long range, as well as a special attack that deals extra damage to their foes. Both players and the enemies can block each other's attacks. Players may also swap their characters at any time to allow one of the protagonists to regain their special attack gauge.

title: Hiyake no Omoide + Himekuri: Girls in Motion Puzzle - Vol.1
aka_titles: Girls in Motion Puzzle Vol. 1: Hiyake no Omoide & Himekuri
Girls in Motion Puzzle Vol. 1: Hiyake no Omoide + Himekuri
description:
Hiyake no Omoide (日灼けの思い出) is a jigsaw puzzle game for one or two players featuring photo stills and live videos. The puzzle pieces portray stills and videos featuring five different girls, namely Ayumi (桜井 亜弓), Mami (長谷川 真美), Kyoko (藤本 恭子), Miwako (工藤 美和子), and Chiyoko (山室 千代子).

The game feature three gameplay modes. Movie Puzzle mode features countdown mode where player races against time to assemble the animated jigsaw puzzle. Animated thumbnail video can be scrolled over to get the better preview. Upon completing the puzzle, the player is rewarded with fullscreen video of the girl in question, and the next jigsaw puzzle video gets unlocked. VP Puzzle mode lets you play against other player or CPU where photo is displayed only for a brief moment before the game starts. During the battle, puzzles set in place by each of the player are marked with the player's color on the grid map. But the battle isn't just about who can put the right piece at the right place faster, instead, there are several different traps and weapons of a sort that one player can use against the other player such as having a character hunt down the puzzle piece the player is carrying and take it off, or mess up the player controls to make everything reverse. The last mode is called Himekuri and is a single-player mode for assembling the jigsaw puzzle of a still image.

Options, which are accessible via main menu, feature movie and photo viewers which let you watch all the videos and photo still you have unlocked during your gameplay. Unlike the majority of Sega Saturn jewel case packages, the game comes in a sleeve which contains jewel case sized cardboard digipak with CD slot and manuals which are made as part of the digipak.

title: Hokuto no Ken
description:
Hokuto no Ken is based on the anime series First of the North Star, continuing its plot. The story begins when Burt and Lynn are about to marry and Lynn is kidnapped by Jado (which resembles Jagger of the first series of Hokuto no Ken), a disciple of the "Dark Hokuto" The Dark Fist of Deceased Light, using a technique called Hokuto Mumyo Ken, a technique older than Hokuto Shinken itself. Then Ken (who is retired in a cave) is attacked by an henchmen of this martial arts school. After defeating him, Ken decides to investigate.

The player watches the development of plot in long anime-like cutscenes and takes an active role only during the simple turn-based battles. The player chooses his actions from a menu. A time bar marks the flow of the turns. When the battle is won, another cutscene starts, etc. The game is divided in levels and a password is given after beating each of those.

title: Hōma Hunter Lime: Perfect Collection
description:
This collection contains:

  • Hōma Hunter Lime: Special Collection Vol. 1
  • Hōma Hunter Lime: Special Collection Vol. 2

The player can only access the first episode directly from the main menu, and must complete each episode before being able to play the next one.

title: Honkaku 4-nin Uchi Geinōjin Taikyoku Mahjong: The Wareme de Pon
description:
Honkaku 4-nin Uchi Geinōjin Taikyoku Mahjong: The Wareme de Pon is a 4-way riichi mahjong game based on a series of television specials which aired between 1995 and 2008 on Fuji TV. The show featured many actors, athletes, and other celebrities playing mahjong, with commentary provided by professional mahjong players. This game version includes a tournament story mode, a free battle mode, and a watch mode, along with detailed player records and rule setting options.

The game features the likenesses of 10 contemporary celebrities to play against: music producer Yasushi Akimoto, actress Miyoko Asada, manga author Yoshikazu Ebisu, actor Morio Kazama, actor Shinobu Sakagami, comedian Akira Shimizu, baseball player Masayuki Dobashi, singer Akira Nishikino, actor Daijiro Harada, and actress Shigeru Muroi.

title: Honkaku Hanafuda
description: Honkaku Hanafuda is a digital version of three popular two-player card games played with Japanese hanafuda cards: Koi-Koi, Hana-Awase, and Oicho-Kabu. The game includes a story mode where the player meets different characters and must defeat them at the various games, and a free battle mode where the player can select any game type and play against the computer. There are eight different computer opponent characters, and a variety of game rule settings for each game type, as well as a basic tutorial that explains how each of the included games are played.

title: Honkaku Mahjong: Tetsuman Special
description:
Tetsuman Special is a 4-way riichi mahjong game featuring the endorsement of the Japan Professional Mahjong League and the likenesses of 14 professional mahjong players (15 in the Saturn version). It is the third title in Naxat Soft's Tetsuman mahjong game series.

There are two main play modes: Title Conquest mode tasks the player with winning against the pros to increase their rank and earn a total of 48 different professional titles; Free Game lets the player set up a more relaxed exhibition game against any set of opponents. The game also keeps detailed records on the player's performance which can be reviewed at any time.

title: Honkaku Shōgi Shinan: Wakamatsu Shōgi Juku
aka_titles: Honkaku Shōgi Shinan: Wakamatsu Shōgi Juku
description: Honkaku Shōgi Shinan: Wakamatsu Shōgi Juku is a shogi game featuring the endorsement of professional shogi player Masakazu Wakamatsu. In addition to a standard play mode for one or two players, it includes a variety of features and modes designed to help beginner shogi players improve their skills. There is a "cram school" mode where the player's skills are first measured, and then the game provides advice and challenges meant to help the player practice their weakest points. There is also a "tsumeshogi" shogi puzzle mode with three levels of difficulty, a "3-on-1" mode where the player must defeat three different opponents under specific restrictions, and even a "blind shogi" mode the player is only shown moves as they are made, and must remember the layout of the board.

title: Hop Step Idol
description:
Hop Step Idol is a management simulation game in the vein of Graduation, where the player is the producer of a new boys idol group and must lead them to success. The game starts with the player recruiting each of the band members by visiting various locations around Tokyo; once the group is assembled, the simulation gameplay starts. The player must decide on each member's practice and work schedule for each week, keeping in mind their strengths and energy levels.

There are 10 different kinds of training, which each affect the eight parameters in various ways, and it's also important to keep drama between band members in check as their personalities will tend to clash. Different parameters improve skill at different jobs, including recording, concerts, and interviews. It is also possible to ask the boys out on dates, which can dramatically improve their motivation levels but may cause drama with their bandmates.

title: Horror Tour
description:
Long ago, Rodvydel Castle fell into the evil grasp of Zeddas, who worked his foul spells upon the place to hide it from mortal eyes. Now you must walk these same haunted halls, trying to undo the harm this demon has wrought. Can you restore the castle? You must pit your own cunning against the fiend's treachery to unravel the sinister mysteries of this place. But beware - the King of Demons keeps a warm place ready for those who would meddle in his affairs!

Horror Tour is a first-person adventure game with pre-rendered backgrounds. The game is set entirely in the castle, which is a maze-like location that must be explored as the player searches for clues. The game's puzzles are predominantly logic-based; reading books in the library is often required to receive clues for their solutions.

title: Houkago Renai Club: Koi no Etude
aka_titles: Hōkago Renai Club: Koi no Etude
description:
Renichi Amagi is an average high-school student who has just joined the Afterschool Romance Club, where young romantic hopefuls meet up to get to know each other. Each afternoon, the club meets at a nearby restaurant, and Renichi can have conversations with up to three of the twelve girls in the club, learning more about them and potentially furthering a relationship with them.

Houkago Renai Club is an adult dating simulation game. Most of the gameplay consists of text conversations with the various girls, with the player occasionally making dialogue choices in response to the girls' questions. The player also has access to a notebook where they can keep notes on each girl, such as their likes and schedules. If the relationship with a particular girl has progressed far enough, the player can ask that girl out on a date, which might lead to an even deeper relationship.

The original PC version of the game includes explicit sexual content, and no voice acting in the original release; an accessory pack which included voiceovers for the main cast was released at a later date. The Sega Saturn version of the game removes the explicit content, adds animated cutscenes and newly-drawn CG illustrations, and includes re-recorded voice acting for the event scenes with a different cast; the story content is otherwise the same as the original PC release. An English/Japanese bilingual version was later released as Casual Romance Club which includes some redrawn graphics.

title: Hudson Soft: New Soft Line Up for Sega Saturn
aka_titles: ハドソン 新作 プレビュー
description:
Hudson Soft New Soft Line Up for Sega Saturn, also called Hudson Shinsaku Preview (ハドソン 新作 プレビュー), is a demo disc published by Hudson Soft for the Sega Saturn containing demos of five Hudson games:

• Bulk Slash
• Willy Wombat
• Virus
• Koden Koureijutsu Hyaku Monogatari: Hontoni Atta Kowai Hanashi
• Momotarou Douchuuki

title: hyper 3-D Pinball
description: hyper 3-D Pinball is a pinball game. It contains 6 pinball tables, that can be played in a 3D view (full table or scrolling) or in a 2D scrolling view. The themes of the tables are Science Fiction (Star Quest), Horror (Monster), Racing (Road King), Underworld (Gangster), Fantasy (Myst & Majik) and Fair (Funfair). Every pinball table has multi-ball gaming, animations (esp. ball-locks) during the game and intermezzos in the scoring field.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Hyper 3D Taisen Battle Gebockers
description: Hyper 3D Taisen Battle Gebockers is a simplistic 3D shooting game. You choose one out of a cast of several cartoon characters to duel the others one by one in a 3D environment. The goal is simply to diminish your opponents health by using your standard and special weapons.

title: Hyper 3D Taisen Battle Gebockers (Taisen Cable-tsuki Gentei Pack)
description: This limited-edition package includes Hyper 3D Taisen Battle Gebockers along with a serial Link Cable accessory.

title: Hyper Duel
description: Hyper Duel is a 2D side-scrolling space shooter. The player controls one of three "Buster Gears” pilots: Keith Spader, Lisa Rowling, or Dr. B. Lloyd, and must destroy alien forces. "Buster Gears” look like normal spaceships from other games but have two modes - spaceship and robot - with different fire modes. The ships can also acquire additional helper units (similar to option from Gradius but more independent) by collecting either the T or G items. The weapon can be upgraded by collecting P items. There are eight stages.

title: Hyper Reverthion
description: Eight warriors seek "Sentien", to obtain the ultimate power of creation and the title of "Reverthion". Reverthion is a third-person arena-based action game that pits two mechanized creatures against one another. It plays very similarly to Sega's contemporary hit Virtual On, and includes eight playable characters each with their own unique move set and abilities. There is a single-player campaign with unique endings for each character, as well as a 2-player split screen versus mode; the Saturn version, Hyper Reverthion, adds system link support for two-player matches between two consoles.

title: Hyper Securities S
description:
In the the near future, in response to rising crime rates and dwindling public funding, the Japanese government has just passed a bill to privatize the country's police force. The first city selected to test this new approach to law enforcement is the former capital city of Tokyo, with numerous security companies setting up shop there for the three-year trial period.

Hyper Securities S is a life simulation game similar to Graduation, in which the player must manage the schedules of three young police cadets in order to both train them into outstanding officers, as well as maintain the safety of Tokyo while keeping the company's budget under control. Each girl's schedule is decided weekly, with the player deciding whether each day is dedicated to training, working, or rest; numerous kinds of training and work can be selected, which will affect that character's status and skills. The girls can also encounter criminals while out on patrol; encounters take the form of a turn-based card battle, with the suspect being arrested if the player wins.

The Sega Saturn release has enhanced graphics and adds voice acting for the game's dialogue, but is otherwise the same game.

title: Hyper Securities: Kinmirai Bishōjo Police Nisshi
description:
In the the near future, in response to rising crime rates and dwindling public funding, the Japanese government has just passed a bill to privatize the country's police force. The first city selected to test this new approach to law enforcement is the former capital city of Tokyo, with numerous security companies setting up shop there for the three-year trial period.

Hyper Securities is a life simulation game similar to Graduation, in which the player must manage the schedules of three young police cadets in order to both train them into outstanding officers, as well as maintain the safety of Tokyo while keeping the company's budget under control. Each girl's schedule is decided weekly, with the player deciding whether each day is dedicated to training, working, or rest; numerous kinds of training and work can be selected, which will affect that character's status and skills. The girls can also encounter criminals while out on patrol; encounters take the form of a turn-based card battle, with the suspect being arrested if the player wins.

The Sega Saturn release has enhanced graphics and adds voice acting for the game's dialogue, but is otherwise the same game.

title: Ide Yōsuke Meijin no Shin Jissen Mahjong
description: A group of shifty gangsters, cops and other groups gather together to compete in a Mahjong tournament. Before starting the game, the player configures the game settings and bets, then choose the characters. There are a total of 16 different opponents to choose from. The order of players' turns is determined by a dice-roll. Then the traditional rules of Mahjong apply with the goal being to beat the other three opponents.

title: Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai II
description:
The third installment in the Suchie-Pai series of mahjong games. More beautiful girls are ready to be your opponent in a game of strip mahjong.

A girl named Shiho Katagiri has been kidnapped, and it's up to Suchie-Pai to save her. Suchie-Pai will need to beat several opponents in mahjong in order to progress. The strip scenes are animated this time. You are also joined by some of your opponents, who can transform into heroes themselves.

The PlayStation version is a censored port and doesn't feature the adult content.

title: Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Mecha Genteiban: Hatsubai 5 Shūnen Toku Package
description:
A nudity-free compilation from the Suchie-Pai series, this four-disc set includes the following:

  • Disk 1: A non-nude version of Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Special.
  • Disk 2: A non-nude version of Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai II.
  • Disk 3: A new Adventure game, similar to Suchie-Pai Adventure: Doki Doki Nightmare, in which the Pai team sets out to find a ghost in the school. Also contains extras, such as a replica of Jaleco's then-current site's voice actress page.
  • Disk 4: A mini audio CD.

title: Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Remix
description:
Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Special is an arcade follow-up to the Super Famicom game Bishōjo Janshi Suchie-Pai that was later ported to several home systems. Like the original, it features Misaki Kyoko's alter ego, the superheroine Suchie-Pai, as she plays mahjong against various young, attractive female opponents. However, this game contains stripping.

Saturn "Remix" version removes some censorship and changes some music compared to the first Saturn release.

title: Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Secret Album
description: Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Secret Album, as the title might suggest, is an album of sorts, in more ways than one. There are two discs, The second disc is an audio CD, also known as an album. The first disc, however, is more of a traditional album. It is a digital scrapbook of the Suchie-Pai series so far, compiled in the form of an internet browser-like interface (known as Suchie-Explorer 4.7). From here you can access a video interview with character designer Kenichi Sonoda, galleries of art from previous games in the series, galleries of various other promotional art, figures, flyers, posters, and cards, the Suchie Dictionary, and the Waku Waku chat. There are also a couple mini-games. First there is the Lilim quiz, a harder version of the quiz game from Suchie-Pai Adventure: Doki Doki Nightmare. There is also "Milk no Usagi-chan Panic," a shooter where you try to prevent hordes of rabbits from making off with the carrots at the bottom of the screen.

title: Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Special
description:
Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Special is an arcade follow-up to the Super Famicom game Bishōjo Janshi Suchie-Pai that was later ported to several home systems. Like the original, it features Misaki Kyoko's alter ego, the superheroine Suchie-Pai, as she plays mahjong against various young, attractive female opponents. However, this game contains stripping.

The PlayStation version is a censored port and doesn't feature the adult content. The Saturn "Remix" version removes some censorship and changes some music compared to the first Saturn release.

title: Idol Mahjong: Final Romance 2
description: Idol Mahjong: Final Romance 2 is the second game in the Final Romance series and the first to feature anime-style girls instead of digitized photos of real models. It is also the first to be ported to home systems. Like the first, you play strip mahjong against various girls. You can use your score to purchase various cheating methods.

title: Idol Mahjong: Final Romance 4
description: Idol Mahjong: Final Romance 4 is the fourth game in the Final Romance series. You play strip mahjong against various female opponents. If you win, you get animated strip scenes. Between girls, you can use your points to buy cheating devices to increase your chances of a winning hand or look at your opponent's tiles.

title: Idol Mahjong: Final Romance R
description:
This limited-edition release of Idol-Mahjong Final Romance R includes the game along with two bonus items:

• A "dress-up" game disc which lets the player dress each up each of the girls in various outfits, including new voice lines.
• A booklet of concept and production artwork.

The dress-up disc was also given out as a separate promotional item, but the art book is unique to this release.

title: Idol-Mahjong Final Romance R (Premium Package)
description:
This limited-edition release of Idol-Mahjong Final Romance R includes the game along with two bonus items:

  • A "dress-up" game disc which lets the player dress each up each of the girls in various outfits, including new voice lines.
  • A booklet of concept and production artwork.

The dress-up disc was also given out as a separate promotional item, but the art book is unique to this release.

title: Ieyasu Senki
description: Ieyasu Senki (titled Tenga-Seiha on consoles) is a historical simulation game set in the Warring States period of Japanese history, which chronicles the life and rise to power of shogun Ieyasu Tokugawa. The game is divided into two main sections: adventure segments and battle segments. In the adventure segments, the player can speak with advisors and villagers to gather information. The battle segments play out in real-time with the player giving basic orders to units, such as to move to a specific location or to launch an attack. The game includes recreations of 26 real-life battles, and numerous story branch points where the scenario can diverge significantly from historical fact.

title: Image Fight & X Multiply
description: Part of the Arcade Gears series, this compilation features two old Irem scrollers: ImageFight and X Multiply.

title: Impact Racing
description:
With disregard for a background story, Funcom Dublin offers a Wipeout-esque mix of racing and driving at a very fast pace. Completing laps within the allotted time does not suffice, you also need to destroy a certain amount of vehicles. Contrary to the aforementioned title, you drive ordinary racing cars, if you count out the mounted weapons. These include mines, concussion missiles, smart bombs, heat-seeking missiles, lasers and firewalls. Some are provided by taking out enemies, but power-ups, time bonuses, energy, armor and a handicap that turns the screen upside-down, can also be collected.

Five cars are available, with different statistics and built-in weapons. The initially weak weapon is soon replaced when you collect upgrade icons. To activate these, you have to complete a bonus stage after which you can also save your game. To add to the game's length, each of the twelve tracks, based on the settings "city", "mountain" or "space", has three variations: reverse, at night or the combination of the two. Other features include a small diagram showing approaching cars to time your mines, and pumping electronic tracks to match the game's pace.

title: In the Hunt
description:
A 2D side scrolling shooter in which you take control of a small attack submarine and engage in underwater combat. The Dark Anarchy Society's forces threaten to destroy the earth's most important cities and only you can get past their defenses and destroy their secret underwater lair.

In the Hunt follows the classic template for 2D shooters, with the added feature of being able to control scrolling speed. Includes seven levels of underwater action (and keep an eye out for threats from above the surface), upgradeable weapons, and two player cooperative gameplay.

title: Independence Day
description:
This arcade game is based loosely on the 1996 blockbuster movie "Independence Day." Interspersed with cutscenes lifted from the film, the game consists of flying a jet through various missions in order to take down the gargantuan, city-destroying spaceships. This entails flying around the 3D level and taking out targets such as: communication uplinks, shield generators, the occasional alien fighter craft, and ultimately bringing down the major alien ship via a strike on its main cannon. Powerups are plentiful, such as medical packs that heal your jetcraft, bonus weapons, bonus planes, and an item that freezes enemy planes for a brief time.

Mission settings include the Grand Canyon, Washington D.C., and New York City. There are other missions that are provided on a need-to-know basis (as stated in the manual). The game also features 2-player head-to-head action via a network or null modem link.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Ippatsu Gyakuten: Gamble King e no Michi
aka_titles: Ippatsu Gyakuten: Gambling King e no Michi
description:
Ippatsu Gyakuten is a gambling simulation game with a strong story element. A young man whose father was a famous gambler dreams of following the same path, and decides to become the greatest gambler in Japan. To that end, the player can bet on horse, boat, and cycling races, as well as play pachinko and pachislot (slot machines), with the ultimate goal of earning 1 billion yen in winnings. In addition to gambling, the player can also take part-time jobs to earn some extra cash, and even meet girls and go on dates.

In addition to the main story mode, there is also a free mode where each of the gambling activities can be played without any of the time or money restrictions of the story mode. The later PlayStation version has a different title and removes pachinko from the available games, but is otherwise the same game.

title: Irem Arcade Classics
description:
Irem Arcade Classics is a compilation featuring direct conversions of three early Irem arcade games:

  • 10-Yard Fight
  • Zippy Race (AKA MotoRace USA)
  • Spartan X (AKA Kung-Fu Master)

Each game includes a variety of configuration options, and a choice between original and arranged music. A superplay video of Spartan X is also included as a bonus.

title: Iron Man / X-O Manowar in Heavy Metal
description:
This game is a linear beat 'em up Final Fight type game with the choice to play as one of two comic book heroes: Iron Man or X-O Manowar. The game follows the pattern of sidescrolling action in each level with a comic book boss at the end of each.

Levels are as follows:1. Nuclear Plant Siege with bosses Mr. Hyde and the Melter. 2. Stark Enterprises with bosses Titania, Yellowjacket and Goliath. 3. Retake New York City with bosses Vizier and Mistress Crescendo. 4. Dromak Base Assault with bosses Absorbing Man and Dromak Gladiator. 5. Assault on Zola's Castle with bosses Arnim Zola and Mistress Crescendo. 6. Alien Dig: The Cosmic Cube with bosses Baron Zemo and Mistress Crescendo. 7. Board Dromak Ship with Final Boss General Krytos.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Iron Storm
aka_titles: World Advanced Daisenryaku: Kōtetsu no Senpū
World Advanced Daisenryaku: Koutetsu no Senpuu
description:
Iron Storm is a traditional turn-based strategy game. The original Japanese release was the second entry in Sega's Advanced Daisenryaku series, with gameplay very similar to that of it's 16-bit predecessor, changing some details and using 3D animations for the combat cutscenes. The game uses a hex-based map and features fog-of-war, weather, unit experience, unit upgrading, supply, and other common strategy wargame features.

Unlike the previous game, three campaigns are available instead of one. Japanese, as well as United States forces can be commanded now in addition to German units. The scenarios that are played during a campaign can change depending on the battle results - a successful player may invade North America for example. There are also ten scenarios with pre-set forces separately available for selection in Standard Mode, during which the control of all involved armies can be switched to a human player.

title: Ishin Kaikoku
description:
Ishin Kaikoku (titled Sakamoto Ryōma: Ishin Kaikoku on consoles) is a historical simulation game set in the Bakumatsu period of Japanese history. It centers around real-life political figure Ryoma Sakamoto, who was instrumental in ending a 250-year period of Japanese isolationism and restoring the Emperor of Japan to power over the shogunate. The player selects one of over 500 possible characters, from the famous Sakamoto himself, down to simple traders and scholars. The ultimate goal of the game is to unify the ideology of the Japanese people and bring about the Meiji Restoration.

The game primarily consists of meeting with people in the many villages in order to convince them to join your cause, looking for those who may be sympathetic. This is accomplished through a menu-based conversation mini-game where the player must choose their words and approach in order to align the other character's feelings with their own. Once the player's influence has sufficiently grown, they can hold faction meetings and delegate various tasks to their followers, including recruiting more people or attempting to assassinate threats. The player's faction can also be attacked, and so care must be taken not to arouse too much attention from the shogunate. The game includes over 150 real-life historical events that can occur.

title: Ishin no Arashi
description:
Ishin no Arashi is set during Bakumatsu period (around 1850 until the Meiji Restoration of 1867), the final stretch of the Japanese Edo period, which was a turbulent time, a time of great struggle between the supporters of the feudal shoguns, the rulers of the country, and the adherents of the Emperor, which eventually won and carried through the Meiji Restoration, turning Japan into a modern, powerful state. In Ishin no Arashi the player can choose one of the three major battles of Bakumastu period, and decide which leader will eventually propel Japan towards the Meiji era.

This strategy game is somewhat similar to the better-known Romance of the Three Kingdoms series and other historical simulation games by the same company, but also differs from them by having much less complex diplomacy options and focusing the gameplay on navigation and individual encounters. Before beginning, the player chooses a general and customizes his parameters (stamina, attack power, charisma, knowledge). The player then controls the general with soldiers of his choice, navigating him on grids representing towns and countryside of Japan in turn-based fashion. The grids can be occupied by shops, schools (to train the general), friendly and hostile characters and groups. Battles, as well as negotiations and diplomatic procedures, are carried out automatically, and their outcome depends on the characters' statistics.

title: Isto é Zico: Zico no Kangaeru Soccer
aka_titles: Isto e Zico: Zico no Kangaeru Soccer
description: Isto é Zico: Zico no Kangaeru Soccer (イスト・エ・ジーコ ジーコの 考えるサッカー) is an interactive movie for the Sega Saturn endorsed by Brazillian football player Arthur Antunes Coimbra, otherwise known as Zico.

title: J. League Jikkyō Honō no Striker
description: Soccer game for the SEGA Saturn by Konami, essentially a version of their International Superstar Soccer franchise that was well known on the N64 and PlayStation.
developers: Konami Computer Entertainment Sapporo Co., Ltd

title: J.B. Harold: Blue Chicago Blues
description:
J.B. Harold: Blue Chicago Blues is a single-player live-action detective adventure game.

The game follows private investigator J.B. Harold, who travels to Chicago after a murder case becomes connected to people from his past. A woman in a red dress is found dead, and soon afterward Catherine White, a detective from the Liberty Town Police Department, is also killed at the same location. Her death is staged to look like a suicide, but the circumstances suggest a larger crime.

Harold arrives in Chicago to work with the local police and uncover the truth behind both deaths. The investigation takes him through police offices, hotels, bars, streets, and other city locations as he follows leads, questions witnesses, and searches for contradictions in the official version of events. The story is built around a noir-style murder mystery rather than action scenes or puzzle rooms.

Gameplay is structured as an interactive movie and detective investigation. Most scenes are presented with live-action video footage using actors and real-world locations. At key points, the video stops and the player chooses where Harold should go, whom he should question, or which investigative action to take next. These choices determine how the investigation proceeds.

Time management is central to play. Many actions advance the in-game clock, so the player cannot simply exhaust every option without consequence. Visiting locations, interviewing people, and following leads must be planned carefully, since wasting time can prevent the player from solving the case successfully. The challenge comes from deciding which clues matter and when to pursue them.

Interviews provide much of the evidence. The player speaks with police officers, suspects, witnesses, and people connected to the victim or the city’s criminal world. Information gathered from one person may open new questions for another, reveal a location, or expose inconsistencies in someone’s statement. The player must connect testimony, evidence, and timing to move closer to the solution.

The presentation emphasizes filmed drama, voice performances, city atmosphere, and detective-story pacing. The live-action footage gives each conversation and location a cinematic style, while the interface keeps the player focused on choices, leads, and the passage of time. The game’s connection to earlier J.B. Harold mysteries provides background for the protagonist, but the case itself is presented as a self-contained Chicago investigation.

title: J.League Go Go Goal!
description: J.League Go Go Goal! is a soccer game licensed by the Japanese J.League organization and featuring all 17 clubs and full stats for the 1997 season. It includes standard league and exhibition modes and supports up to four simultaneous players. A notable feature of the game is the ability to create custom player formations, and the option to switch between multiple different play strategies on the fly during a match.

title: J.League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurō!
aka_titles: J.League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurō!
J-League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurou!
description: J.League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurō! is a football (soccer) management simulation game and the first game in Sega's long-running management sim series. The player takes the role of the owner of a new Japanese football club and must build it from the ground up into a competitive team, with the ultimate goal of the club being admitted to the top league in the country, the prestigious J.League. With only a limited amount of funds available per year, the player must hire staff and scout players, manage sponsorships and publicity, schedule matches and training, and even chose the team's hometown and uniform colors.

title: J.League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurō! 2
aka_titles: J.League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurō! 2
J-League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurou! 2
description: J.League Pro Soccer Club o Tsukurō! 2 is a football (soccer) management simulation game and the sequel to the first game in Sega's long-running series. The player takes the part of the owner of an upcoming club that is just about to join the prestigious J.League soccer league. As in the previous game, the player manages staff hiring and player scouting, sponsorships and publicity, match and training scheduling, and of course choose the team's hometown and uniforms. New in this entry are the ability to create up to three custom players for the team, additional options for post-match publicity and commentary, and a completely revamped in-game match display system that lets the player watch each match in a much more realistic style.

title: J.League Victory Goal
description:
It was Team Aquila's first creation as a sub-department of Sega CS1, and the first in the Victory Goal series. Being released in 1995, it also stands as one of the first 3D football games, though the players are represented as 2D sprites.
Victory Goal was announced alongside the Saturn in early 1994, under the working title of Virtua Soccer. However, it is only assumed Virtua Soccer became Victory Goal - in this early incarnation, only simple demo footage was shown (as was the case for Clockwork Knight, Daytona USA and Panzer Dragoon - only Virtua Fighter was partially playable), with no specific details on the team listings.
Contrary to popular belief, Victory Goal was a Japanese exclusive, featuring teams from the Japanese J. League. Its engine would be adapted and J. League teams replaced with international teams in Sega International Victory Goal. Victory Goal is hence sometimes referred to as J. League Victory Goal to make the distinction.

title: J.League Victory Goal '96
description:
Victory Goal '96, the direct sequel to Victory Goal (not to be mistaken for International Victory Goal, which unlike the game in question was distributed for all regions), is the game that set the bases further development of Sega Worldwide Soccer 97 and the sequels.

From the previous games of the series this soccer game just kept the title, because the game engine, music, video scenes and almost everything else, all had the same ingredients that in the West could be seen for first time with the later Worldwide Soccer 97. Also, just as its predecessor, this game includes all the teams of the Japanese J.League (of which it had an official license), but on the other hand, it does not include any international teams. The game features commentary tracks by two of Japan's most famous commentators.

title: J.League Victory Goal '97
aka_titles: Japan Professional Football League: Victory Goal '97
description:
Victory Goal '97 can be considered Sega Worldwide Soccer 97 but with 17 of the teams of the Japanese Professional Football League. Just like the previous Victory Goal games it does not include any international teams, but instead the updated club teams and player names for the 1997 season.

The first in the series not developed by Team Aquila but this time adapted by SIMS, it became the last of the series dedicated exclusively to the Japanese league, and also the last of SEGA games to carry "Victory Goal". Further releases would use the title "Worldwide Soccer", also in Japan.

title: Jantei: Battle Cos-Player
description:
Jantei: Battle Cos-Player is a 4-way riichi mahjong game featuring a science-fiction story and a combination of live-action and animated opponents. Set in a futuristic city where the greatest treasures are the costumes of a previous era, the player and their partner Yuko Saionji challenge a series of opponents to mahjong matches in order to collect as many costumes as possible and become the "Jantei", or Mahjong Emperor. Defeating opponents will award their costume, which Yuko can wear and show off in animated or live-action videos depending on which type of costume it is.

In addition to the main story mode, there is also a free battle mode. There is also a "making-of" disc included in the package, which contains a photo gallery and cast interview videos.

title: Japan Super Bass Classic '96
description: Japan Super Bass Classic '96 is a bass fishing game endorsed by pro bass fisher Katsutaka Imae. The player is tasked with winning various tournaments on order to win professional titles; winnings can be used to buy and upgrade equipment, with the player's rod, reel, line and lure all being customizable. The game also includes a practice mode to try out equipment before participating in a tournament.

title: Jewels of the Oracle
aka_titles: Oracle no Houseki: Jewels of the Oracle
description:
Jewels of the Oracle is a stationary puzzle game with no real story line or plot. A total of 24 ingenious puzzles must be solved, each independent of the others. Most of them can be played in two difficulty levels (Easy or Hard), and the Oracle provides clues to help along the way.

The graphics for the puzzles are designed in an Egyptian or Mesopotamian style. Music plays in the background to provide atmosphere, but it can be turned off, if it gets repetitive. The basic layout is a hexagon around an Oracle's well. There are three doors on the outside of the hexagon, and the first one is where you begin the game. In each room is a puzzle you have to solve to get a jewel which must be taken back to the Oracle's well.

The puzzles in this game can be compared to those found in The 7th Guest. The Chinese Checkers puzzle in Shivers rivals many of the ones contained in Jewels of the Oracle.

title: Jikkyō Oshaberi Parodius
aka_titles: Jikkyou Oshaberi Parodius: Forever With Me
description:
Jikkyō Oshaberi Parodius is the third in the Parodius series. It retains the same gameplay and humorous elements that substantiated the first two games. Gameplay itself is a parody of Konami's famous Gradius series; the screen scrolls from left to right (most times) and the player manoeuvres a flying character around the screen destroying waves of enemies and avoiding obstacles. Unlike previous Parodius titles, this game contains a difficulty adjustment option, allowing the player to make things easier or harder. Also unique to this installment are bits of digital voice acting. Survival throughout the level leads the player to a boss fight, which frequently includes some of the strangest characters in the game.

Power-ups include, besides the standard version (red, used to upgrade weapons), the shield power-up (blue) and a variety of different coloured bells. Green Bells will make the protagonist huge on the screen; Yellow Bells are worth points (points in turn are worth extra lives); Blue Bells are "big bombs" that clear the screen of enemies and can be saved until you need them; White Bells will give the player character a megaphone that will shout out phrases that damage enemies; Red Bells stockpiles the hero with three point-defense lasers, only one of which can be activated at a time and disappears after a short while; Purple Bells will clear the screen of all but the strongest enemies, turning them into power-ups.

This time around there are sixteen different characters to chose from, each with unique power-ups and weapons. These include familiar faces from earlier games as well as new ones: Vic Viper, the "gradius ship" equipped with its traditional Gradius weapons; Pentaro from Penguin Adventure, whose Potion weapon may now hit multiple enemies and his normal weapon shots explode against obstacles; Soitsu, a green stickman surfing aboard a paper airplane, whose laser weapon is able to charge up to deliver more power and who drops little stickmen onto the ground which occasionally dance around rather than attacking; Mike, a cute little kitten who happens to to have a very powerful wave weapon which can travel through obstacles and enemies, as well as a multiple bomb ability which requires his "upgrade ability"; Memim, a flying fairy in bikini who carries missile weapons whose direction is determined by her current location on the screen when fired; Tako, the flying octopus wearing a baseball cap; Upa, the flying baby with a Mega Crush ability that destroys all enemies on screen, and others.

title: Jikkyō Powerful Pro Yakyū '95 Kaimakuban
description:
Jikkyō Powerful Pro Yakyū '95 Kaimakuban is a baseball simulation game. It is an updated version of Jikkyō Powerful Pro Yakyū '95, and also the first in the Powerful Pro Yakyū series to appear on the Sega Saturn. It features a full NPB license and thus all teams and players from the Japanese Pacific and Central leagues, with rosters up-to-date as of the end of the 1995 pre-season.

In addition to the updated roster, this version features a new set of 12 Scenario mode challenges based on recent games in the 1995 season. The Camp mode, which allows the player to practice the various actions of the game such as batting and pitching, also returns after being absent from the prior release. Also new in this iteration are various assist options to make pitching and batting easier.

title: Jikkyō Powerful Pro Yakyū '97 Kaimakuban
description:
Jikkyō Powerful Pro Yakyū '97 Kaimakuban is a baseball simulation game and part of the long-running Powerful Pro Yakyū series. It is the third release in the series for the PlayStation, and the second and final to appear on the Saturn. It features a full NPB license and thus all teams and players from the Japanese Pacific and Central leagues, with rosters up-to-date as of the end of the 1997 pre-season.

New in this entry for the 32-bit versions are the addition of Success mode and League mode, which were both introduced in Jikkyō Powerful Pro Yakyū 3. Success mode is an in-depth training and story mode where the player creates a new recruit and has three years to make it to the starting lineup; Success mode players can be saved with passwords compatible with several other titles in the franchise, allowing a player to be moved between games. League mode is a tournament mode for up to six players/teams. Other returning modes include the Battle (Exhibition) mode, Pennant mode, and Practice mode. There is also a team editor called Arrange mode.
developers: Konami Computer Entertainment Osaka Co., Ltd.

title: Jikkyou Oshaberi Parodius: Forever With Me
description:
This game is the third game in the series of parody shooters produced by Konami and was released only in Japan. The gameplay is stylistically very similar to the Gradius series, but the graphics and music are intentionally absurd. The game, as its name would suggest (translated: "Chatting Parodius Live"), contains a large amount of Japanese voice samples shouted out in a style similar to that of a game show host.

Unlike the previous titles, this game was not created originally as an Arcade game. Instead, it was originally released on the Japanese Super Famicom and this port is an upgraded version of that one, featuring not only improved graphics and sound from the Super Famicom game, but some altered levels and bosses, including a cheat to replace "Tokimeki People's Dance" with an enhanced version, "Days Of The Dream's Memories". Also added were several "Omake" stages and an unlockable Dracula-kun and Kid Dracula as a playable character. In a two-player game, both players can now choose to play simultaneously instead of just alternately in the Super Famicom game.

This game was also released on the Sony PlayStation with little differences compared to this version.

title: Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu S
description:
Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu S is a baseball simulation game and part of the long-running Powerful Pro Yakyuu series. It is the second and final game in the series to appear on the Saturn. It features a full NPB license and thus all teams and players from the Japanese Pacific and Central leagues, with rosters up-to-date as of the end of the 1997 pre-season.

New in this entry are the addition of Success mode and League mode, which were both introduced in Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu 3. Success mode is an in-depth training and story mode where the player creates a new recruit and has three years to make it to the starting lineup; Success mode players can be saved with passwords compatible with several other titles in the franchise, allowing a player to be moved between games. League mode is a tournament mode for up to six players/teams. Other returning modes include the Battle (Exhibition) mode, Pennant mode, and Practice mode. There is also a team editor called Arrange mode.

title: Jikū Tantei DD: Maboroshi no Lorelei
aka_titles: Jikū Tantei Dracula Detective: Maboroshi no Lorelei
Jikuu Tantei Dracula Detective: Maboroshi no Lorelei
description: Jikuu Tantei DD is a detective noir adventure game with a futuristic setting. The game is one big cinematic drama which plays as an interactive movie (think Cyberia). The story takes place aboard a zeppelin ship Lorelei. In 2238 human race got the freedom to use the ability to travel back in time, which eventually led to the emergence of crime. You are a Raizou Narukami, a detective who runs an agency that specializes in space-time crimes. Womanizer at first glance, you are very skilled at what you do, namely in power of observation, reasoning and deduction. You are known as DD (short for Dracula Detective) because your are a direct descendant of legendary Dracula. Due to your genes, you also exert some superhuman powers and abilities.

title: Jissen Mahjong
description: Jissen Mahjong is a 4-player riichi mahjong game that offers both 2D and full-3D visuals of the mahjong table. The game includes three modes: Challenge Mode tasks the player with defeating various opponents to increase their rank; while Free Battle Mode and Party Mode let the player choose any three of the 10 available opponents and play a regular match with various options. There are also a wide range of configuration options for adjusting the game rules.

title: Jissen Pachi-Slot Hisshōhō! 3
description:
Jissen Pachi-Slot Hisshōhō! 3 is a pachi-slot (Japanese slot machine) simulation game and part of Sammy's long-running series of gambling sims. It features a faithful recreation of five different real-life slot machines from various manufacturers: Aladdin Master by Sammy, Divers XX by Yamasa, Flipper 3 by Universal, Play Girl Queen 2 by Olympia, and Any 7 A by Takasago.

The main game mode is the "Real Battle" mode, in which the player selects one of five characters who each have different income and hours they are able to play, and must conquer a series of gambling halls by successfully earning enough winnings within a certain time limit. There is also the "Strategy" mode which lets the player select any configuration of any of the five featured machines, and practice without any time or money limits. Both modes include detailed progression and stat tracking.

title: Jissen Pachinko Hisshōhō! Twin
description:
Jissen Pachinko Hisshōhō! Twin is a pachinko simulation game in Sammy's long-running series of gambling sims. This particular release features faithful recreations of two contemporary real-life pachinko machines made by Sammy:

  • CR Gao Gao Kids 4, a dinosaur-themed machine
  • CR Kudamonobatake, a fruit-themed machine

The game includes two play modes.
