Similar to other titles in the series, the goal of the game is to clear the screen of constantly advancing objects called 'drops'. The player character, stuck at the bottom of the screen, has a grapple which can be used to pull down a single drop, change its colour and put it back in line. Drops disappear when a line of three or more drops of the same colour is created.

There are several game modes: endless mode, story mode, two-player mode, and puzzle mode.

title: Magical Drop 2
description: Magical Drop is played in a style and gameplay similar to Compile's (now Sega's) Puyo Puyo and Taito's Puzzle Bobble franchises; a "stack" of random colored bubbles descend from the top, and a player is defeated when a bubble hits the bottom. Bubbles can be picked up and dropped by the player's "clown" at the bottom, and are destroyed when three or more of the same color are put together on a single column. "Chains" are formed either when a single drop caused a chain reaction, or when more than one group of bubbles is destroyed in quick succession. The game is normally played with two players (one may be a computer opponent), and chains cause the opponent's stack to descend faster.

title: Magical Drop II
description:
In Magical Drop II, you control a clown that can grab and throw balloons. You have to match three balloons of the same colour or more vertically to pop them and clear the screen. You can hold multiple balloons of the same colour at once and cause consecutive collisions. There are special balloons that cannot be removed that easily and power-ups that clear entire rows or provide additional help.

Depending of the originating country, there are different game modes:

  • Survival: Play as long as you can - an endless flow of balloons appears at a rapidly increasing speed while you move up levels.

  • Puzzle: You have a limited time to clear a fixed set of balloons before time runs out.

  • VS Mode: Fight the CPU or a fellow player in a direct split-screen duel. Each character has specific item balloons during gameplay.

title: Magical Drop III
description:
This is the third installment in the puzzle frenzy series Magical Drop. In the game you control a clown who throws marbles up on the screen into the cluster of multi-colored marbles, rocks and crystals. The goal is to get three or more of the same color to remove marbles, but you can also grab more than one at the time to create long chain combos and gain better "special" blocks at the top of the screen.

You can play the game in single player modes or versus a friend in versus mode. In versus mode you get to pick your character, much like in a fighting game, each with their own counter attacks and abilities.

For the PSX version, the first Magical Drop was included on a separate disc.

title: Magical Drop III: Toretate Zoukangou!
description:
This is the third installment in the puzzle frenzy series Magical Drop. In the game you control a clown who throws marbles up on the screen into the cluster of multi-colored marbles, rocks and crystals. The goal is to get three or more of the same color to remove marbles, but you can also grab more than one at the time to create long chain combos and gain better "special" blocks at the top of the screen.

You can play the game in single player modes or versus a friend in versus mode. In versus mode you get to pick your character, much like in a fighting game, each with their own counter attacks and abilities.

title: Magical Night Dreams: Cotton 2
aka_titles: Magical Night Dreams: Cotton 2 - Saturn Tribute
description:
The true sequel to Cotton, Cotton 2 introduces Cotton's rival Appli for 2-player support for the first time and the story this time deals with the disappearance of the magic "Bluewater Willow" from the Kingdom's treasury. Cotton and Appli must now search the lands for the magic willow battling all the enemies they encounter in the way before its too late.

The game follows in the 2D-side scrolling shooter roots of the original with new spells, different elemental weapons that can be upgraded with experience crystals and a new energy bar that allows you to take a few hits before going down.

There are also new "command" shots that are triggered by specific controller moves as well as a hit-combo system that allows you to earn more power-ups and items. The Saturn version also has a "Saturn" mode which changes the enemy arrangement and makes some changes to the game balance.

title: Magical Night Dreams: Cotton Boomerang
aka_titles: Magical Night Dreams: Cotton Boomerang - Saturn Tribute
description:
Cotton Boomerang is sort of an expanded edition of Cotton 2, with remixed levels and enemies.

The only real differences are in the gameplay mechanics, which aim to make the game more action-oriented by removing the health bar and the restrictions for weapon upgrading. Now that the health bar is gone, you get to select 3 different characters from a group of 8 that act as your "lifes" but each has distinct shooting patterns and abilities to enhance the gameplay. Additionally you can switch between characters at will (as long as they are alive) which triggers a bomb-like effect.

Also includes an art gallery featuring Cotton 2 and Cotton Boomerang material, additional difficulty modes and controller configuration options that allow you to map the command-shots.

title: Mahjong Angel Kiss
description: Mahjong Angel Kiss is an arcade-style strip mahjong game featuring characters designed by noted illustrator Satoshi Urushihara. It is a standard 2-player riichi-style mahjong game; winning matches against the opponent will earn points, and enough points will earn the player an animated scene where said opponent removes an article of clothing until they are eventually topless. There are three girls to play against, and the only game mode is a standard arcade mode where each girl is played in order.

title: Mahjong Dōkyūsei Special
description: Mahjong Dōkyūsei Special is a follow-up to Mahjong Dōkyūsei, once again a strip mahjong game based on the Dōkyūsei series of adult adventure games. This edition is again a 2-player riichi mahjong game, but features improved cel animation and a new cast of ladies to disrobe. There are six opponents in total, two of whom return from the previous edition: Hiromi Machida, Satomi Kurokawa, Mako Saito, Natsuko Masaki, Yoshiko Serizawa, and the main heroine Mai Sakuragi. As in the original version, there are no game options, only a straightforward arcade story mode where each opponent is played in order.

title: Mahjong Dōkyūsei Special (Portrait CG-tsuki Shokai Genteiban)
description: This limited-edition release of Mahjong Dōkyūsei Special includes a bonus disc with a gallery of production artwork.

title: Mahjong Gakuensai
description:
Mahjong Gakuensai is a strip-mahjong game featuring a high school festival theme. The player is cast as the president of the school photography club, who wants to get some photos of his female classmates for upcoming school festival. The player can move around the school and nearby area to meet up with various characters; either female students who may offer to pose for a photo when defeated, or male students who will offer a salacious photo of one of the girls when defeated. The game is standard one-on-one riichi mahjong, though a notable feature is the "Mecha-Moe" system, whereby winning with higher-ranking hands will increase a gauge, which determines which of several photos the player will see upon defeating a girl at mahjong.

The Sega Saturn port censors the nudity, and adds an additional free battle mode as well as game rule option settings.

title: Mahjong Gakuensai (Shokai Genteiban)
description: This limited-edition release of Mahjong Gakuensai includes the game along with a bonus disc containing interviews with the voice cast.

title: Mahjong Gakuensai DX: Zenjitsu ni Matsuwaru Funsenki
description: Mahjong Gakuensai DX is a strip-mahjong game with a high school festival theme, and part of the Mahjong Gakuensai series. It is a remixed conversion of the first and second arcade releases, including a mix of opponents and locations found in both prior games. It is set on the day before the school festival, and the player is once again cast as a student hoping to get photos of his female classmates. Gameplay is the same as every other entry in the series, with the player visiting locations around campus and challenging other students in hopes of getting saucy photos of them. More impressive mahjong hands will raise a girl's "Mecha-Moe" gauge, resulting in more revealing photos the higher it gets, though this console version is censored and does not include any actual nudity. This version also includes a free-battle mode, various game rule options, and new animated opening and ending cutscenes.

title: Mahjong Ganryūjima
description:
Mahjong Ganryūjima is a 4-player riichi mahjong game that offers two different modes with different sets of opponents to play against. The Kengo Mahjong mode features 16 famous swordsmen of the Edo era of Japanese history such as Kojiro Sasaki and Jubei Yagyu, with the goal being to work through their ranks and ultimately defeat Musashi Miyamoto. The Modern Mahjong mode features a mostly-fictional cast along with several real-life players including manga artist Fujio Akatsuki and jazz singer Martha Miyake.

Other than a practice option in Kengo Mahjong that lets the player pick specific opponents, all match opponents are fixed and there are no game configuration options.

title: Mahjong Gokū Tenjiku
description: Mahjong Gokū Tenjiku is a mahjong tournament between characters from Xi You Ji ("Journey to the West"), the classic Chinese novel. The player can choose to play as either of the four "good" characters from Xi You Ji: the Buddhist monk Xuan Zang, the famous monkey Sun Wukong, the pig Bajie, and Xuan Zang's pupil Wujing. They compete against a variety of Xi You Ji villains. The player can choose a location to set the mahjong game in and can configure most of the mahjong rules to their own preference in a special menu.

title: Mahjong Hyper Reaction R
description:
Mahjong Hyper Reaction R is a one-on-one strip mahjong game and a home conversion of Mahjong Hyper Reaction. This version is significantly expanded over the original arcade game and includes new content and features:

  • A new opponent, Yuka, has been added for a total of three girls to play against.
  • New animated opening and ending sequences.
  • A new "Free Battle" mode where the player can unlock newly-drawn illustrations of each girl.

title: Mahjong Kaigan Monogatari: Mahjong Kyō Jidai Sexy Idol Hen
description: Mahjong Kyō Jidai Sexy Idol Hen is one of several games in Micronet's series of strip mahjong games featuring video footage of real-life models. This particular entry features video clips of three fashionable young idols, who progressively undress down to either their underwear or a swimsuit -- though no further -- as the player wins matches. The unlocked videos of each girl can be freely rewatched from the menu.

title: Mahjong Kyō Jidai: Cebu Island '96
description: Mahjong Kyō Jidai: Cebu Island '96 is one of several games in Micronet's series of strip mahjong games featuring video footage of real-life models. This particular entry features video clips of three young ladies shot on the beaches of the Philippine island of Cebu. Winning mahjong matches against the girls will unlock videos of each girl in various swimsuits, which can be freely rewatched from the menu.

title: Mahjong Kyō Jidai: Cogal Hōkago Hen
description: The player challenges three young socialites to a game of Mahjong. Beating the opponents in the game rewards the player with live-action clips of the ladies stripping and posing nude for amusement.

title: Mahjong Taikai II Special
description: Mahjong Taikai II Special is an enhanced remake of Mahjong Taikai II. The game plays much the same as the original version, allowing you to play mahjong against 23 famous historical and fictional figures, including Toyotomi Hideyoshi, Abraham Lincoln, Joan of Arc, and Sherlock Holmes. This remake includes full 3D graphics and voice clips for each character.

title: Mahjong Tenshi Angel Lips
description: Mahjong Tenshi Angel Lips is an arcade-style strip mahjong game featuring characters designed by noted illustrator Satoshi Urushihara. It is a standard 2-player riichi-style mahjong game; winning matches against the opponent will earn points, and enough points will earn the player an animated scene where said opponent removes an article of clothing until they are eventually topless. There are three girls to play against, and the only game mode is a standard arcade mode where each girl is played in order.

title: Mahjong Yonshimai: Wakakusa Monogatari
description: Mahjong Yonshimai: Wakakusa Monogatari is an arcade-style strip mahjong game featuring four sisters as the opponents. It is a standard 2-player riichi-style mahjong game; winning matches against the opponent will earn points, and enough points will earn the player an animated scene where said opponent removes an article of clothing until they are eventually topless. The only game mode is a standard arcade mode where each opponent is played in order, from the youngest (Hikaru) to the eldest (Haruka). At certain points in the game, there is also a slot-machine mini-game in which the player can win a bonus advantage for the next round.

title: Mahō Gakuen Lunar!
description:
This prequel to Lunar: The Silver Star begins in the same town of Burg hundreds of years earlier. Two teenage girls, Elie and Lena, set out to join the Magic School of Ien. There they meet new friends and go on lighthearted adventures around the world.

Lunar is a traditional Japanese RPG, featuring random battles and turn-based combat. Compared to the original Game Gear version, this remake features battles more in tune with the other Lunar games along with an expanded plot, CD audio soundtrack, and animated cutscenes.

title: Mahō no Janshi: Poe Poe Poemy
description: Mahō no Janshi: Poe Poe Poemy is a 1-on-1 riichi mahjong game with a magical-girl anime theme. Various villains are causing trouble, and the magical girl Poemy must put a stop to their wicked ways by defeating them at strip mahjong. The game includes a story mode with anime cutscenes where defeating each opponent causes them to be disrobed – defeat them three times and they'll be left in only their underwear – as well as a free battle mode against any of the first three story opponents.

title: Mahō Shōjo Pretty Sammy: "Osorubeshi Shintai Sokutei! Kakubakuhatsu 5-byō Mae!!"
aka_titles: Mahō Shōjo Pretty Sammy: "Osorubeshi Shintai Sokutei! Kakubakuhatsu 5-byō Mae!!"
description:
Mahō Shōjo Pretty Sammy: "Osorubeshi Shintai Sokutei! Kakubakuhatsu 5-byō Mae!!" is a visual novel style adventure game based on the Magical Girl Pretty Sammy anime series. A mysterious woman named Shizuka has appeared as the new nurse at Sasami's school, and when a new Love-Love Monster appears during the school's annual student health exam, it's up to Pretty Sammy to stop it and save the day. The bulk of the gameplay consists of voiced story sequences over still images; the player is occasionally given a choice of which action to take in a scene, which will affect how the rest of the scene plays out but not the overall story as a whole.

Also included in the package is an audio mini-CD containing three music tracks.

title: Mahō Shōjo Pretty Sammy: Heart no Kimochi
aka_titles: Mahō Shōjo Pretty Sammy: Heart no Kimochi
description: Mahō Shōjo Pretty Sammy: Heart no Kimochi is a visual novel style adventure game based on the Magical Girl Pretty Sammy anime series. It includes two new original story episodes: the first involves a mysterious group creating a new kind of super-weapon, while the second revolves around the cast preparing chocolates for Valentine's Day. Gameplay is identical to the previous title: voiced dialogue sequences over still images drive the story, and the player is occasionally given a choice of which action to take in a scene; these choices will affect how the rest of the scene plays out but not the overall story progression.

title: Mahōtsukai ni Naru Hōhō
description: Mahoutsukai ni Naru Houhou is a Simulation/Action Role-playing game taking place on an island. Players take the role of a wizard's apprentice who's aspiring to become a mage and players are given 3 girls to choose from (Lime, Berry or Nut). To become a mage, players must study how they can make scrolls and collect the ingredients necessary to make them. The game features a first person perspective while players are at home and switches to a top-down 2D view when they go outside (The Saturn and Playstation releases render areas in 3D). There are 102 days in a year in this game and 5 seasons during which different materials can be found on the island. The game has 70 kinds of scrolls and around 150 kinds of materials to collect.

title: Mainichi Kawaru Quiz Bangumi: Quiz 365
description:
Mainichi Kawaru Quiz Bangumi: Quiz 365 (roughly, "The Quiz Show that Changes Every Day: Quiz 365") is a quiz game themed like a daily television variety show. It features different sets of themed questions depending on the date when playing, including trivia questions specific to the current date or day of the week, and includes various themed sections imitating TV show segments as the player progresses. The game includes numerous types of questions, including regular multiple-choice questions, questions based on illustrations of photographs, and even logic deduction challenges based on various situations. There are also several minigames that can appear throughout the game.

The original arcade release is for one or two players, while the Sega Saturn version adds an additional multiplayer mode for up to six players. The Saturn version also adds a handful of additional quiz question types.

title: Manx TT SuperBike
description: Race motorcycles in this arcade port based on the real-life Isle of Man Trophy Race. There are two courses to race with the usual reversed and mirrored variations on the tracks. Also provided is a short and long version of the main course. Play modes include arcade (standard tracks), PC mode (added variations), time trial, and network games with up to eight people.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Maria: Kimitachi ga Umareta Wake
description:
In this game, you play as a young psychiatrist named Takano. One day a new patient is brought into the hospital you work in - Maria, a young woman who has attempted suicide. She suffers from amnesia, and you try to find out more about her, visiting her and talking to her. Before long you discover that Maria has schizophrenia - a split personality. Her "other self" appears to be evil and threatens to take over her. The fight for Maria's sanity begins.

The game plays like an interactive novel or movie: you read text and from time to time make a choice from two or more available ones. Instead of the standard 2D animé-style graphics the game utilizes semi-realistic CG pre-rendered backgrounds and characters. There are also CG animated movies in the game.

title: Marica: Shinjitsu no Sekai
description:
Shinjitsu no Sekai means real world in Japanese - and indeed, the game is set in modern-day Tokyo. The protagonist is an ordinary (at least in the beginning) girl named Marica, who lives together with her parents and her little sister. One day a dog steals a piece of meat she bought in a store. Following the dog, Marica encounters a strange, scary-looking man, who turns out to be a former terrorist on the run from his even scarier comrades, who are involved in supernatural activities. Marica becomes the sole owner of information that is vitally important to the terrorist organization, and has to protect her life with her newly discovered paranormal skills.

Despite the unusual (for an RPG) setting, the gameplay system of Marica is similar to other Japanese RPGs. There are no random enemies, but initiating contact with a hostile character on screen leads to a turn-based battle, viewed from first-person perspective. Marica and the two other girls who join the party later in the game can attack with equipped weapons or execute their special moves. Those attacks are displayed as anime-style still shots. The story is advanced mostly through extensive dialogue (no subtitles) between characters, with large anime-style portraits super-imposed on the background.

title: Mario Mushano no Chō Shōgi Juku
aka_titles: Mario Mushano no Chō Shōgi Juku
description: Mario Mushano no Chō Shōgi Juku (Mario Mushano's Hyper Shogi School) is a shogi training game featuring the endorsement and likeness of professional shogi player Katsumi "Mario" Mushano. It includes over 200 shogi problems arranged to teach various techniques, a skill tracker mode that measures various aspects of a player's shogi skills and advises on ways to improve, and a ranking test that allows players to see if they have the skill to obtain shodan ranking, the first official ranking for shogi.

title: Marvel Super Heroes
aka_titles: マーヴル・スーパーヒーローズ
description:
Marvel Super Heroes is a 2D fighting game and the second Capcom title to feature characters from the Marvel comic universe. The gameplay is very similar to X-Men: Children of the Atom, but with a simplified Super Combo gauge and the addition of infinity gems. Each character starts with a set of gems. These can be activated during a fight to improve speed, power and defence, or provide special abilities to create crushing stone walls, open up a rift in space, or reverse the opponent's controls. The use of the gems is inspired by the The Infinity Gauntlet comic book series.

There are ten playable characters. The heroes are Captain America, The Incredible Hulk, Iron Man, Psylocke, Spider-Man and Wolverine. The villains are Blackheart, Juggernaut, Magneto and Shuma-Gorath. Anita from the Darkstalkers series is a hidden character in the Japanese version. The bosses are Doctor Doom and Thanos. During the boss fight Thanos steals all the player's gems (except for mind) and uses them with new effects.

title: Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter
aka_titles: Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter EX Edition
description:
Marvel Super Heroes Vs. Street Fighter is a 2D fighting game and the first to combine characters from Capcom's Street Fighter series with those of the Marvel comic universe. It is also the first in Capcom's games to introduce a tag team style of combat where the player can call for another character during a fight.

Matches consists of two-on-two battles where the player can only control one character at a time. The other character can be called in regularly or while doing an attack. The off-screen one also regains some health while waiting. Both opposing characters need to be defeated to win the match, and when one dies the other is called in automatically. The tag team options introduces Variable Attack, Variable Counter and Variable Combination where the two characters team up to attack, counter of perform a special move.

Most of the X-Men characters were already present in X-Men: Children of the Atom and Marvel Super Heroes: Cyclops, Storm, Juggernaut, Magneto and Wolverine, with the addition of Rogue, Gambit and Sabretooth. The Street Fighter characters are gathered from Street Fighter Alpha 2: Ryu, Ken, Cammy/Chun-Li, Charlie, Zangief, Dhalsim, M. Bison and Akuma. The final boss of the game is Apocalypse.

The PlayStation version does not include the tag team feature and relies on the more traditional best-two-of-three round setup.

title: Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter (Kakuchō RAM Cartridge 4MB Fuzoku)
description: This release of Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter includes the game along with a Sega Saturn 4MB RAM Expansion Cartridge.

title: Mass Destruction
aka_titles: Mass Destruction: Otousan ni mo Dekiru Soft
description: Mass Destruction puts players behind the controls of a one-man tank. The environments range from arctic to desert to urban. The player can blow up trees, buildings, walls - whatever you don't like the look. Enemies will come at you in tanks, planes, helicopters, and on foot. Each of the different weapons available to the player works best on a specific enemy. The player can use guided missiles for the helicopters and run over infantry men with the tank.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Master of Monsters: Neo Generations
description:
Master of Monsters: Neo Generations is a fantasy-themed, turn-based hex strategy game and part of SystemSoft's Master of Monsters series. Like previous games in the series, each player controls a Master who can summon various creatures onto the battlefield to fight for them. These creatures can be upgraded and fused to increase their power and evolve them into more advanced forms, are consistent across maps once summoned, and are gone permanently if killed. The goal of each battle is to defeat the opposing master; if a master is killed, all their creatures vanish from the map and they lose the battle.

In the main story mode, the player selects one of six masters each with different abilities, backstory, and pool of available summon creatures. Over a series of battles on varied maps the player must defeat the other five masters and, ultimately, Gaia himself to claim his throne. There is also a map-select mode where any map can be played outside the story mode, a vs mode for two players, and a map-edit mode.

A heavily revised PlayStation port which replaces the master characters with more anime-style designs, adds an in-depth story component, and redesigns some of the maps was released the following year as Master of Monsters: Disciples of Gaia.

title: Masters: Harukanaru Augusta 3
description:
Masters: Haruka Naru Augusta 3 is a sequel to Masters: Haruka Naru Augusta 2 golf game and in that relation very similar to its predecessor. This game also features the Augusta National golf course and is licensed by Augusta National Golf Club. The game plays from the third-person perspective, showing your golfer sideways with a mini-map of the current hole on the right side of the screen. Several modes are accessible from the main menu, including Masters, Tournament, Stroke Play, Match, and Training.

Much like its predecessors, the game uses live-action golfers and caddies over 3D golf course terrain. During the rotation of the terrain, the game removes the texture details to moves more smoothly. Camera rotation lets you gain altitude on your current position, check the area around the hole immediately, or use your cart car to drive across the terrain and examine it in more detail before starting.

When playing a game you can select among four different golfers and four different caddies. Each golfer has its own advantages and disadvantages when playing such as the swinging gauge may be harder or easier to accurately select depending on the type of terrain of the golf club your golfer uses. The terrain level can be checked in more detail even while you're not on the green near the hole, and though it gives little help to use at those places it's still available. The course supports both members and masters tee plays and also includes a detailed guide for every hole. Various records for every hole are saved and can be checked along with other statistics.

title: Matsukata Hiroki no World Fishing
description: Matsukata Hiroki no World Fishing is a fishing game featuring the endorsement and likeness of Japanese actor Hiroki Matsukata. The game uses digitized photos of Matsukata to represent the player, and includes many live-action video clips of him as various events play out in-game. It includes two types of fishing: billfish trawling (ocean fishing) and black bass fishing (lake fishing), which despite the title are both set in Australia. Each type of fishing includes introduction and basics videos for beginners, a free fishing practice mode, and a tournament mode.

title: Maximum Force
description:
Maximum Force is the follow up to Area 51, however, this time around instead of shooting up aliens, the player goes up against a terrorist organization.

The gameplay is similar to other first-person shooter gun games where the player can use a light gun or a controller to shoot at bad guys popping up from behind objects or coming off from the side of the screen. If a player gets shot by a bad guy, they will loose a bar of health or can also loose health by accidentally shooting innocent bystanders.

There are also power-ups scattered throughout the stage that can restore health, upgrade their weapons power among many others. There are three levels in all and 35 secret rooms scattered throughout the stages. It also supports a second player simultaneously.

title: Mechanical Violator Hakaider: Last Judgement
description:
Mechanical Violator Hakaider: Last Judgement is a light-gun rail shooter with light adventure elements based on the 1995 tokusatsu film Mechanical Violator Hakaider. Set 10 years after the events of the film, the player controls the titular anti-hero android Hakaider as he returns to Jesus Town in order to defeat Professor Gil and recover the arm that he lost in a battle against Waruda.

Each mission consists of one or more first-person shooting gallery-style segments against either waves of enemies or a boss character, in which the player must shoot down targets and projectiles without taking too much damage. The player has several different weapons to choose from, which have different effectiveness and ammo limits. Certain segments also take the form of a simplified first-person adventure, where the player can explore environments and talk to characters, and there are occasional choices for the player to make which may affect the following action sequence.

title: MechWarrior 2: 31st Century Combat
aka_titles: MechWarrior 2: 31st Century Combat - Arcade Combat Edition
MechWarrior 2: Combat au 31'eme Siecle - Arcade Combat Edition
MechWarrior 2: Kampfspiel des 31. Jahrhunderts - Arcade Combat Edition
description:
You are the genetically engineered Clan Mechwarrior. The Clans are invading the Inner Sphere. Join either the Wolf Clan or the Jade Falcon Clan as they pursue their own agenda against the Inner Sphere and other Clans. Take your advanced Omnimechs into battle against all comers. Win high warrior ratings (by using less mechs or smaller mechs than needed, completing secondary objectives, etc.) and you'll get chance at a promotion trial where you face superior odds in an arena. If you win, you advance in rank. If you are very successful, you can make it all the way up to Khan, leader of the Clan.

Mechwarrior II was developed in-house by Activision as the successor to their original Mechwarrior. While this time there are no dynamic campaign and mercenary actions, the Clan culture is integrated into the two campaigns. Different clans have different mechs and different rules, even different weapons. You can customize your mechs in order to use less than the "par" force in order to get a higher rating. The game features full 3D environments. The addition of NetMech allowed users to fight each other online.

When 3D cards came along, special versions of the game were created to take advantage of 3D texturing.

The console ports made some changes to the game to make the game more action heavy. Alot of the mechs core mechanics are sped up, the maps are smaller so running into enemies is more of a factor, the enemies are weaker but that is made up by the fact there are more of them, and there are now power-ups scattered around. The mech lab has been removed and 16 new missions have been added.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: MechWarrior 2: 31st Century Combat: Arcade Combat Edition
aka_titles: MechWarrior 2: 31st Century Combat: Arcade Combat Edition
description:
You are the genetically engineered Clan Mechwarrior. The Clans are invading the Inner Sphere. Join either the Wolf Clan or the Jade Falcon Clan as they pursue their own agenda against the Inner Sphere and other Clans. Take your advanced Omnimechs into battle against all comers. Win high warrior ratings (by using less mechs or smaller mechs than needed, completing secondary objectives, etc.) and you'll get chance at a promotion trial where you face superior odds in an arena. If you win, you advance in rank. If you are very successfully, you can make it all the way up to Khan, leader of the Clan!

Mechwarrior II was developed in-house by Activision as the successor to their original Mechwarrior. While this time there are no dynamic campaign and mercenary actions, the Clan culture is integrated into the two campaigns. Different clans have different mechs and different rules, even different weapons. You can customize your mechs in order to use less than the "par" force in order to get a higher rating. The full 3D environment wasn't pretty as this was before the 3D accelerators made their debut, but it's still better than anything that came before. Let addition of NetMech allowed users to fight each other online. When 3D cards came along, special versions were created to take advantage of 3D texturing. While not QUITE as replayable as Mechwarrior, it's nonetheless a classic.

title: mediaROMancer: Daisuke Asakura
description: mediaROMancer Daisuke Asakura is a multimedia fan disc for Japanese musician Daisuke Asakura. It includes a discography, interview clips, a breakdown of his studio equipment, and a plethora of photographs, video clips, and other information about him. In addition, there is also a game mode in which Asakura's manager has been kidnapped by a bandit, and Asakura must save him by hitting a specified number of targets in a whack-a-mole style minigame. Clearing stages in this minigame unlocks additional bonus video clips.

title: Mega Man 8: Anniversary Collector's Edition
aka_titles: ロックマン８ メタルヒーローズ
description:
The Blue Bomber returns! The evil Dr. Wily discovers the remains of a strange robot that evidently came from space, and discovers a source of unbelieveablely powerful energy that could allow him to control the world with an army of unstoppable Robot Masters!

It's up to Mega Man to stop Wily once again! Now joined by a new ally, Duo, Mega Man takes off on his greatest mission yet!

title: Mega Man 8: Anniversary Edition
description:
The Blue Bomber returns! The evil Dr. Wily discovers the remains of a strange robot that evidently came from space, and discovers a source of unbelieveablely powerful energy that could allow him to control the world with an army of unstoppable Robot Masters!

It's up to Mega Man to stop Wily once again! Now joined by a new ally, Duo, Mega Man takes off on his greatest mission yet!

title: Mega Man X3
description:
A Reploid scientist named Dr. Doppler begins creation of a new city for Reploids, which will bring a new era of peace to the Reploids and humans. But something goes terribly wrong, and now Mavericks have begun to appear everywhere! It's up to X and Zero to find out who is behind this Maverick revolt and bring them down for good!

For the first time in the series, players can play use X's friend, Zero. However, he is pretty much restricted to only about one third of each level, and has only one life (i.e when he loses all his energy, he is put out of the fight for the rest of the game).

title: Mega Man X4
description: Mega Man X, the reploid leader of the 17th unit Maverick Hunters, and his best friend Zero have to stop a reploid rebellion. Each of them gets involved in a different way and you can play as either character through the parallel stories.

title: MeltyLancer: Ginga Shōjo Keisatsu 2086
description:
MeltyLancer: Ginga Shōjo Keisatsu 2086 is a life simulation game and an expanded port of the PC game The Melting Pot Police: MeltyLancer. The game plays generally the same: the player determines the weekly schedules of six young Lancers; when they patrol and which days they have off, and what kinds of training they do to sharpen their skills. Battles can occur during patrols or special missions but are largely automated, with the player only having limited control such as ordering a Lancer to retreat.

The console versions of the game contain significantly revised simulation mechanics and story compared with the original PC version, with additional story events and full voice acting as well as completely revamped graphics and sound. The later Sega Saturn version additionally includes even more new scenario events, though is otherwise the same game as the PlayStation version.

title: MeltyLancer: Ginga Shōjo Keisatsu 2086 (Special Edition)
description:
This limited-edition release of MeltyLancer: Ginga Shōjo Keisatsu 2086 includes the game along with several bonus items:

  • A 12-track audio CD containing music, drama tracks, and answering machine messages
  • A MeltyLancer-branded CD wallet
  • A 1997 calendar featuring MeltyLancer artwork

title: MeltyLancer: Re-inforce
description:
This Sega Saturn version of MeltyLancer: Re-inforce was released five months after the original PlayStation version of the game, and includes numerous changes and additions:

  • Battles have been redesigned in a turn-based tactical format rather than the semi-real-time format of the original.
  • New events have been added to the game, including several which make use of the Saturn's real time clock.
  • Several mini-games have been changed or replaced.

title: MeltyLancer: Re-inforce (Special Edition)
description: This special edition release of MeltyLancer: Re-inforce includes the game along with an audio drama CD.

title: Message Navi
description: A highly collectable Saturn title that is more like a digital magazine with horoscopes, guides to popular spots such as restaurants, a cosplay market with digitized photos, fashions from the streets etc.

title: Message Navi Vol. 2
description: Message Navi Vol. 2 (メッセージ・ナビ ＶＯＬ．２) is a game for the Sega Saturn.

title: Metal Black
description:
Metal Black is an arcade 2D side-scrolling shoot'em up, made as continuation of Gun Frontier and the Darius series.
Aliens (called Nemesis) invaded Earth, won the war, and took most of the raw materials and the player, piloting a spaceship, fights against those aliens. His vehicle is the CF-345 Black Fly, and he must "fly right, and shoot enemies". He has only 1 weapon, and collects special pickups to increase firepower (and activate power-beam). The game has 6 levels & 2 bonus levels, each with their own song.

title: Metal Fighter Miku
description:
In the year 2061, technological advancements have allowed humans to surpass the limits of the weak human body. A new form of entertainment called Neo Pro Wrestling, which allows combatants to use powered armor and other enhancements, is rapidly gaining in popularity. The Pretty Four are a team of teenage wrestlers/pop idols, riding high after their newest member, Miku, snatched a world championship victory. Suddenly, a new tournament is announced by a mysterious new group called The Lion's Den, and Miku and the Pretty Four decide to take on the challenge.

Metal Fighter Miku is a Japanese-style adventure/simulation game based on the 1994 animated series of the same name. It features a new scenario in six chapters set six months after the events of the show, essentially functioning as a sequel. The player controls Miku and must develop her abilities and ultimately win each match as the story progresses.

The game is divided into two main sections. Most of the story plays out in standard visual novel-style dialogue sequences, with occasional choices that affect the flow of the conversation. Wrestling matches play out as real-time sequences where the player must select actions from a menu; available actions and current fighter status are shown at the bottom of the screen, while the top of the screen shows large illustrations of the match in action. Matches can be decided by pinfall, count out, or submission.

title: Metal Slug
description:
Metal Slug, originally released on the Neo Geo, is a side-scrolling shoot'em'up.
The player(s) takes the role of a soldier (or two) and fights a gigantic army. Every level consists of running forward blasting anything that moves, while collecting power-ups along the way (there's also a wide selection of weaponry in the game). In the end of each level the player goes up against one gigantic boss.

title: Metal Slug (Okaidoku Set)
description: This release of Metal Slug includes the game along with a Sega Saturn 1MB RAM Expansion Cartridge.

title: Metal Slug: Super Vehicle - 001
aka_titles: Arcade Archives: Neo Geo - Metal Slug
description:
Metal Slug, originally released on the Neo Geo, is a side-scrolling shoot'em'up.

The player(s) takes the role of a soldier (or two) and fights a gigantic army. Every level consists of running forward blasting anything that moves, while collecting power-ups along the way (there's also a wide selection of weaponry in the game). In the end of each level the player goes up against one gigantic boss.

The PlayStation port introduces some extra features: there is a combat school where the player may fight with other players for the best time on each level and an art gallery.

title: Mezase Idol Star!! Natsuiro Memories: Mahjong-hen
description:
A television station is holding tryouts to find a new pop idol to represent the company. After several rounds of auditions, only eight young women remain in the running. The final test, to determine both their intelligence and luck, is a mahjong tournament! Whoever wins the tournament also wins the audition, and the competition is fierce.

Mezase Idol Star!! is a 1-on-1 mahjong game featuring a cast of aspiring young idols, each portrayed by a real-life actress. The player takes the part of a manager and selects a girl to represent in the tournament; to win the audition, the player must defeat all seven of the other girls at mahjong. The game also includes profiles and a photo gallery of each girl, and additional swimsuit photos are unlocked after clearing each girl's scenario.

title: Midway Presents Arcade's Greatest Hits
description:
Midway Presents Arcade's Greatest Hits is a compilation that includes the following games:

• Bubbles
• Defender
• Defender II
• Joust
• Robotron: 2084
• Sinistar

title: Mighty Hits
description:
Mighty Hits is a shooting gallery game and the gameplay and stages are very similar to Point Blank in theme and presentation. The game has a cartoony wild west theme throughout the cut scenes and menu screens.

One or two players compete in a series of mini games, which last about 20 or 30 seconds each. The rules of the mini games are displayed before each round. In general players have complete objectives and puzzles by shooting at targets. After each round a results screen shows if the objectives were completed or failed. Failing a round and the player loses a life feather, lose all feathers and the game is over.

There are 3 courses to select from, represented by a blue, green and yellow tin can. There is Easy (6 mini-games), Medium (9 mini-games) and Hard (15 mini-games) and completing hard mode unlocks a black tin can for Very Hard with 18 mini-games. The game is played in sets of 3 stages, the player has to shoot 3 cards to select the stages. The cards are quickly flipping randomly through mini-games. After 3 stages the player draws a bonus card and moves onto the next 3 stages. A bonus card might contain "2 stage select" where 2 of the stage cards will flip more slowly allowing the player to purposefully select a stage.

There are many mini games, including shooting away parts to complete a doll, a Three Shell type game, shoot ice to free a penguin, shoot colored bells to recreate a melody, throwing balls into cups, shoot the object in the room that has changed, and in general shooting at various targets like fish, bees, lights, eggs, floating lanterns, toppling pictures frames and other targets.

title: Minakata Hakudō Tōjō
description: Minakata Hakudō Tōjō is mystery adventure game with a faux claymation visual style. The player takes the role of an assistant to the titular Inspector Minakata, reviewing footage of crime scenes to look for anything suspicious. The bulk of the player's interaction involves clicking on objects, which will trigger dialogue descriptions of the object and ultimately lead to the solution of each case. The game includes two short tutorial cases and two longer main story cases.

title: Minami no Shima ni Buta ga Ita: Lucas no Daibōken
aka_titles: Minami no Shima ni Buta ga Ita: Lucas no Daibōken
description:
While searching for food for his village, the pig Lucas climbed a huge tree in hopes of stealing the eggs from a giant bird's nest. However, when he reached the nest, the mother bird saw him and chased him away. Upon returning to his village in defeat, Lucas finds all the homes ransacked and everyone gone but one young piglet, who is snatched away by a bird right before his eyes. Lucas sets out to rescue the piglets, and his journey will take him all across the island.

Minami no Shima ni Buta ga Ita: Lucas no Daibōken ("There was a Pig on the South Island: Lucas' Great Adventure") is a puzzle game featuring an assortment of logic puzzles. The game is divided into six themed worlds, and each world is divided into six levels in two types. Even-numbered stages are simple platform action sequences where Lucas can jump and use a whip to attack, avoiding enemies and looking for piglets to rescue. Odd-numbered stages take the form of various logic puzzles similar to those one might find in a puzzle magazine, such as arranging numbers to have them all add up to a certain sum, or rolling dice around so that they all show the same image on their face. These puzzles can be skipped, but clearing them will rescue a larger number of piglets.

title: Minnesota Fats: Pool Legend
description: Minnesota Fats: Pool Legend is a pool game where the player can participate in a story mode and play against a set of pros in six different pool halls in an attempt to face off against Minnesota Fats himself. There are seven different variations of pool to play: Eight-Ball, Nine-Ball, Rotation, 14-1 rack, Three ball, Cut Throat & One Pocket. There is also a Versus Mode to let players take on any opponent of their choice including a two-player option to take on a friend and a Tournament Mode. Players can also try out the Trick Mode that has the player try to compete 16 different trick shots.

title: Minton Keibu no Sōsa File: Dōkeshi Satsujin Jiken
aka_titles: ミントン警部の捜査ファイル 道化師殺人事件
Minton Keibu no Sōsa File: Dōkeshi Satsujin Jiken
description:
Minton Keibu no Sōsa File: Dōkeshi Satsujin Jiken is a murder mystery adventure game, and a full remake of Thinking Rabbit's 1985 release Dōkeshi Satsujin Jiken. The game is set in Brighton, England in 1932 at a traveling circus; the protagonist, Detective Frank C. Minton, is sent from London to investigate after a clown is found dead. The player, as Detective Minton, must explore the circus and nearby town searching for evidence and questioning suspects. Of particular note is that the player can change the tone of questioning with suspects, choosing to be gentle, firm, or harsh depending on the circumstance.

Compared with the original game, there are numerous changes and upgrades. Notably, the text parser interface has been replaced with a simplified command menu. All environments are pre-rendered in full 3D, while characters are presented as 2D illustrations with full voice acting.

title: Mizubaku Daibouken
description:
In Mizubaku Daibouken, you play Hipopo the Hippopotamus who must venture through a large number of enemy-packed levels in search for his missing girlfriend, as well as rescuing other hippo-like creatures along the way. The game features moving platforms, collapsible floors, boats, water-wheels, and plants that can be watered, causing them to grow and allowing you to reach much higher platforms.

Hipopo is supplied with magical water globes, which can be thrown at enemies to freeze them. Once frozen, the enemies can be kicked and destroyed completely. If idle for a few seconds, enemies will unfreeze themselves and continue their business. Every two levels is a boss that needs to be defeated in order to proceed to the next one.

title: Mizuki Shigeru no Yōkai Zukan: Sōshū-hen
aka_titles: Mizuki Shigeru no Yōkai Zukan: Sōshū-hen
水木しげるの妖怪図鑑 総集編
description:
Mizuki Shigeru no Yōkai Zukan: Sōshū-hen is a Japanese-style adventure game plus a multimedia database of yōkai (spirits and ghosts of Japanese folklore) featuring illustrations and commentary by yōkai scholar and GeGeGe no Kitarō creator Shigeru Mizuki. The database portion collects together the contents of three prior PC releases with information on a total of over 950 different yōkai.

In the game section, the player has come to Mizuki-sensei's home to become his disciple, but he has gone missing. The player visits various locations to search for the missing professor, and encounters many different yōkai in combat along the way. Combat is non-traditional; rather than attacking them directly, the player must use their knowledge of the various spirits to select the correct action or response to safely ward them off.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam
description:
Mobile Suit Gundam is a side-scrolling action game based on the popular 1979 animated series of the same title and its three film adaptations, casting the player as the series' main character, the young pilot Amuro Ray. The story generally follows the plot of the films with only minor changes, and includes new animation from the original animation studio Sunrise that remakes famous scenes from the original.

The player pilots the titular RX-78-2 Gundam in both ground-based run-and-gun and space-based flight stages, using various weapons to destroy enemies; Radio chatter from other characters plays throughout each stage, and it is often necessary to destroy all enemies in an area to advance the story. As missions are completed, additional weapons become available and the player can customize their equipment loadout before each stage. Of special note is the Newtype Attack, which when charged and locked on will deal instant damage to targeted enemies, including enemies in the foreground and background outside the range of normal attacks.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story I: Senritsu no Blue
aka_titles: Kidō Senshi Gundam Gaiden I: Senritsu no Blue
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story I: Blue Fear
Kidou Senshi Gundam Gaiden I: Senritsu no Blue
機動戦士ガンダム外伝Ⅰ 戦慄のブルー
description:
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story I: Senritsu no Blue is a first-person action shooting game based on the popular Mobile Suit Gundam media franchise. Relatively unique among Gundam games, it tells an original story not adapted from another media, and is the first in a three-part trilogy. It is set during the One Year War, shortly after Operation Odessa; the player controls Earth Federation pilot Yuu Kajima, who alongside his teammates Philip Hughes and Summona Fulis are sent on missions with experimental Mobile Suits in order to collect data for production. The team encounters a mysterious blue Mobile Suit that seems bent on eradicating Yuu's team, and which seems to show up without warning.

The game is divided into five missions, each of which has specific objectives such as destroying a particular target or defending a specific structure or character. The story is told through radio communications during gameplay, and objectives may change as the mission progresses. There are no branching story paths or loadout customization, though the player is ranked at the end of each mission which has an effect on the overall ending. Save data can be carried over into the sequel.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story I: Senritsu no Blue (Shokai Press Tokushu Package Shiyō)
description: This limited-edition release of Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story I: Senritsu no Blue includes the game along with a limited-edition pin, packaged in a cardboard digipak.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story II: Ao o Uketsugu Mono
aka_titles: Kidō Senshi Gundam Gaiden II: Ao o Uketsugu Mono
Kidou Senshi Gundam Gaiden II: Ao wo Uketsugu Mono
機動戦士ガンダム外伝Ⅱ 蒼を受け継ぐ者
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story II: Ao o Uketsugu Mono
description:
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story II: Ao o Uketsugu Mono is a first-person action shooting game based on the popular Mobile Suit Gundam media franchise. Relatively unique among Gundam games, it tells an original story not adapted from another media, and is second entry in a three-part trilogy, following after Senritsu no Blue. It once again casts the player as pilot Yuu Kajima, with the identity of the mysterious blue MS starting to be revealed.

The game is again divided into five missions, each of which has specific objectives such as destroying a particular target or defending a specific structure or character. The story is told through radio communications during gameplay, and objectives may change as the mission progresses. There are no branching story paths or loadout customization, though the player is ranked at the end of each mission which has an effect on the overall ending. Save data can be carried over from the first game, and into the third after completing all missions.

Two releases of the game exist: a standard edition in a jewel case and a limited edition in a cardboard digipak. Other than the packaging, the two releases are identical and there is no bonus content or extra items in the limited edition.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story III: Sabakareshi Mono
aka_titles: Kidō Senshi Gundam Gaiden III: Sabakareshi Mono
Kidou Senshi Gundam Gaiden III: Sabakareshi Mono
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story III: Those Who Are Judged
機動戦士ガンダム外伝Ⅲ 裁かれし者
description:
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story III: Sabakareshi Mono is a first-person action shooting game based on the popular Mobile Suit Gundam media franchise. Relatively unique among Gundam games, it tells an original story not adapted from another media, and is third and final entry in a three-part trilogy, following after Ao o Uketsugu Mono. This concluding chapter once again has the player controlling pilot Yuu Kajima. Two machines remain with the experimental EXAM System, designed to mechanize the abilities of Newtypes and allow human pilots to have the same capabilities: one has been stolen, purportedly by the pilot of the mysterious blue MS, Efreet; the other has been assigned to Yuu.

The game is again divided into five missions, each of which has specific objectives such as destroying a particular target or defending a specific structure or character. The story is told through radio communications during gameplay, and objectives may change as the mission progresses. There are no branching story paths or loadout customization, though the player is ranked at the end of each mission which has an effect on the overall ending. Save data can be carried over from the previous games, and the game's ending changes depending on the player's rank throughout the full campaign.

Two releases of the game exist: a standard edition in a jewel case and a limited edition in a cardboard digipak. Other than the packaging, the two releases are identical and there is no bonus content or extra items in the limited edition.

title: Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story: The Blue Destiny
aka_titles: Kidō Senshi Gundam Gaiden: The Blue Destiny
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story: Optional Guide
description:
Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story: The Blue Destiny collects together all three Saturn Gundam Side Story releases in a single package:

  • Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story I: Senritsu no Blue
  • Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story II: Ao o Uketsugu Mono
  • Mobile Suit Gundam Side Story III: Sabakareshi Mono

Also included is a bonus "Optional Guide" disc which includes an illustration gallery and play videos of each mission, as well as a set of trading cards.

title: Mōjya
description:
Take Money Puzzle Exchanger, sprinkle on some Puyo Puyo, and what do you get? Hey presto, it's Mōjya! Players control falling pairs of yen coins, in assorted denominations from 1 through 500. Making change by combining coins into the amount of a higher denominations combines the set of coins into one coin of the larger size, and combining two 500 yen coins makes them disappear. Efficient coin placement can lead to making large combos by letting transformed coins fall into place to make change for a higher denomination.

This rendition of Mōjya gives the original game a bright and colourful makeover and replaces the cast with cute cats.

title: Momotarō Dōchūki
description: Momotarō Dōchūki is a multiplayer board-game and a spinoff of Hudson's Momotarō Dentetsu series. It features many of the same characters and gameplay elements as the main series games, but with a new setting in the Edo period of Japanese history. As with other Momotetsu games, players take turns moving around the board via dice rolls, acquiring property to earn money, trying to avoid giving money to other players, and encountering a wide variety of random (and often comical) events that can grant each player various benefits or handicaps.

title: Momotarou Douchuuki
description: Momotarou Douchuuki is a multiplayer board-game and a spinoff of Hudson's Momotarou Dentetsu series. It features many of the same characters and gameplay elements as the main series games, but with a new setting in the Edo period of Japanese history. As with other Momotetsu games, players take turns moving around the board via dice rolls, acquiring property to earn money, trying to avoid giving money to other players, and encountering a wide variety of random (and often comical) events that can grant each player various benefits or handicaps.

title: Monster Slider
aka_titles: モンスタースライダー
description:
Monster Slider is a falling-block puzzle game similar to Columns or Puyo Puyo. Colored blocks fall in pairs from the top of the screen and must be arranged to match 3 or more of the same color together. Uniquely the entire playfield is at a tilt, causing blocks to slide to one side to fill gaps when they are placed or after clearing other blocks; the player can reverse the tilt at any time, causing blocks to slide in the opposite direction. Combos will launch garbage blocks at the opposing player, and if the blocks reach the top of the well that player loses the round. Each character also has a unique special ability.

The main single-player story mode casts the player as a young woman named Nina whose sister has been kidnapped by Count Dracula; she must defeat each of Dracula's minions and eventually Dracula himself in order to rescue her. There is also a two-player versus mode and a single-player endless mode.

title: Moon Cradle
aka_titles: Īda Jōji Nightmare Interactive: Moon Cradle
description: Moon Cradle is a mystery adventure game which uses live-action video for cut-scenes and fixed isometric perspective during actual gameplay. The player controls the character directly while actions such as "search", "talk" or "use" are presented in a menu-selected manner.

title: Mōri Motonari: Chikai no Sanshi
aka_titles: 毛利元就 誓いの三矢
description:
Mōri Motonari: Chikai no Sanshi is a tactical RPG in the vein of Shining Force. It is a historical drama based on the life of 16th-century daimyo Mōri Motonari, and the third entry in Koei's Eiketsuden series of historical RPGs. The story opens in 1517 with Motonari forced to take the reins of his clan following the deaths of both his father and elder brother.

The game is split into 27 chapters which each opens with a story event, then allows the player to speak with advisors and villagers as well as to prepare for the next battle. Villagers may have various requests, which when completed will reward the player with equipment or new recruits for battle. Additionally, equipment can be upgraded and soldiers can be trained at this time. Battles take the form of a top-down turn-based tactical format, with individual units engaging 1-on-1. Each battle has specific win conditions, and the story is linear with no branches.

title: Mortal Kombat II
description:
Mortal Kombat II is a single-player and multiplayer fighting game.

The story continues from the original tournament on Earth, Mortal Kombat. After Shang Tsung’s defeat, he persuades Emperor Shao Kahn to host a new contest in the realm of Outworld. Fighters from Earthrealm are invited to compete once again, unaware that the tournament is a trap designed to ensure their destruction and allow Outworld to invade. The player chooses from a roster of warriors, each with their own motivations for entering the deadly competition, and battles through a series of one-on-one matches to reach the final confrontation with Shao Kahn himself.

The gameplay builds on the foundation of the first Mortal Kombat. Players engage in side-view, best-of-three-round duels using a combination of punches, kicks, blocks, and jump maneuvers. Every character has unique special moves that can be executed with precise button inputs, such as fireballs, teleportations, or rapid multi-hit attacks. Common maneuvers like uppercuts, sweeps, and flying kicks remain vital, while throws and roundhouse kicks add further tactical options.

A defining feature of the franchise, finishing moves known as “Fatalities,” return with even more elaborate executions. Each fighter has at least one unique Fatality that can be performed after winning the final round of a match. These violent finishers became a hallmark of the series, and Mortal Kombat II expands the concept with multiple Fatalities per character, as well as hidden finishing moves like Friendships and Babalities in later revisions. Stage-specific Fatalities allow players to use the environment to eliminate their opponent, such as knocking them into spikes or acid pits.

The roster is significantly expanded compared to the original. Returning fighters include Liu Kang, Johnny Cage, Scorpion, Sub-Zero, Raiden, and Shang Tsung, now rejuvenated and able to morph into any character. New challengers include Kitana, Mileena, Jax, Kung Lao, Baraka, and Reptile as a fully playable character. Boss encounters escalate the challenge: after defeating the other fighters, players face Shang Tsung, the towering Kintaro, and ultimately Shao Kahn, whose overwhelming strength tests mastery of the mechanics.

Several modes and settings enhance replay value. The arcade version supports up to two players alternating or fighting head-to-head, including mirror matches between identical characters. Early home versions across platforms such as the Super Nintendo, Sega Genesis, Game Boy, and later compilations maintained the core structure, though censorship or graphical adjustments sometimes altered blood, violence, or speed. Later re-releases aimed to preserve the arcade experience more faithfully.

title: Mortal Kombat Trilogy
description:
All the characters from the first three Mortal Kombat games return for the ultimate battle. You can play as Kano, Reptile, Mileena, Kung Lao, Shang Tsung, Sindel, Sektor, Stryker, Nightwolf, Sheeva, Kitana, Scorpion, Sonya, Smoke (Cyber Ninja), Rain, Jade, Baraka, Johnny Cage, Ermac, Noob Saibot, Sub-Zero (Unmasked), Sub-Zero (Classic), Jax, Rayden, Cyrax, Liu Kang, Smoke (Human), Kabal, Goro, Kintaro, Motaro, or Shao Kahn.

This game is one-on-one martial arts fighting. The player can choose from over thirty different characters, all with their own fighting style and their own special moves. Trilogy differs from the other games in that you can play combinations of people that otherwise isn't possible, such as old Liu Kang vs. new Liu Kang, etc.

Mortal Kombat Trilogy also allows you to challenge a friend to a fight through a Windows IPX network connection.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Motteke Tamago with Ganbare! Kamonohashi
aka_titles: もってけたまご with がんばれ！かものはし
description: Motteke Tamago with Ganbare! Kamonohashi is a top-down Bomberman-style multiplayer arcade action game, and an enhanced port of the PC Engine game Motteke Tamago. This version includes the same arcade mode as the original release, and also adds a single-player story mode with multiple stages and new creatures to play as other than ducks, such as frogs and platypus.

title: Moujiya
description:
Take Money Puzzle Exchanger, sprinkle on some Puyo Puyo, and what do you get? Hey presto, it's Moujya! Players control falling pairs of yen coins, in assorted denominations from 1 through 500. Making change by combining coins into the amount of a higher denominations combines the set of coins into one coin of the larger size, and combining two 500 yen coins makes them disappear. Efficient coin placement can lead to making large combos by letting transformed coins fall into place to make change for a higher denomination.

This rendition of Moujya gives the original game a bright and colourful makeover and replaces the cast with cute cats.

title: Mr. Bones
description:
A philosopher named DaGoulian came up with a dubious doctrine: he believes that the only way to ensure the survival of the good is by making the world more evil. He invented a special set of drums using science and alchemy, allowing him to control a power called "skeletism". By using this power, DaGoulian reanimates the dead, raising people's skeletons from their graves and building a fearsome army to fulfill his mad plan. However, one of these skeletons had been a person of a particularly pure heart, and instead of being afflicted with the red (evil) skeletism, he is reanimated with its blue version, allowing him to retain his free will and refuse the madman's orders. DaGoulian orders his minions to get rid of this rebel, who has to fight for his life and eventually figure a way to stop the insanity.

Mr. Bones is an action game that consists of numerous stages. With the exception of a few, each stage has a different goal and introduces unique gameplay style. The stages also vary greatly in length, some being extended platform levels and others consisting of short timed sequences. Many of the stages involve avoiding hazards or enemies, as well as tasks that must be completed within a certain time limit. Mr. Bones, the skeletal protagonist of the game, usually has no offensive arsenal. When damaged, he begins to lose limbs and bones, which affects his manoeuvrability and speed; he may even end up with nothing but a head and a neck hopping on the ground.

Some of the stages are simple one-screen arcade levels, while others may deviate from the action-oriented gameplay (e.g. a stage during which the player has to combine sentences into jokes to get past guards). A few stages involve music exercises, for example a level that requires Mr. Bones to play blues guitar to impress a skeleton crowd. Another stage is a paddle game variant in which a small Mr. Bones bounces off a giant head of himself, trying to collect his own bones. In another level the hero must protect a village of tiny people against enemy assault.

The story is advanced by video cutscenes displayed between the levels. Some of these are computer-generated, while others utilize footage of live actors, or a mixture of both.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Mujintō Monogatari R: Survival Life in the Uninhabited Region
aka_titles: Mujintō Monogatari R: Futari no Love Love Island
description:
Mujintō Monogatari R is a survival simulation with love adventure elements, and part of the Mujintō Monogatari series. The protagonist is on a Hawaii vacation, but winds up stranded on a deserted island with five other vacationers: four female and one male from a total of 10 possible, with the specific companions selected by the player's choices in the introduction. The player must guide their group to work together to survive, and ultimately figure out a way off the island within three months, while also pursuing a romantic relationship with one of their companions.

The player's group is divided into three pairs, and the player can give each group instructions for both the morning and afternoon of each day, including to explore or investigate locations looking for resources, prepare food, or to rest. The protagonist can also use a turn to spend personal time with their partner, increasing their affection and eventually allowing them to be asked on a date. It is even possible to pursue a relationship with the other male companion, though he will pursue one of the other girls on his own if left alone. Each character has seven stats — health, trust, strength, focus, mood, cooking, and affection — which determine their effectiveness at particular tasks and their relationship with the protagonist, and which will change depending on what they're asked to do.

title: Mujintou Monogatari R: Futari no Love Love Island
aka_titles: 無人島物語R ふたりのラブラブ愛ランド
description:

title: Murakoshi Seikai no Bakuchō Nihon Rettō
aka_titles: Murakoshi Seikai no Bakuchō Nihon Rettō
村越正海の爆釣日本列島
description:
Murakoshi Seikai no Bakuchō Nihon Rettō is a fishing game featuring professional fisherman and author Seikai Murakoshi. The game includes a total of 11 locations from all across Japan to fish at, and each location has a specific target fish and quota to meet. Completing a stage will move on to the next, with the final stage being a 1-on-1 challenge against Murakoshi himself. Between stages, the player can use points earned from catching fish to obtain new rods and lures. There are also advice videos featuring Murakoshi giving beginner and intermediate fishing advice for the player.

The later PlayStation TsuriCon Taiō-ban release adds support for the ASCII "TsuriCon" fishing controller but is otherwise identical.

title: My Best Friends: St. Andrew Jogakuen-hen
aka_titles: My Best Friends: St. Andrew Jogakuin Hen
マイ・ベスト・フレンズ St.アンドリュー女学園編
description: My Best Friends: St. Andrew Jogakuen-hen is a anime-style jigsaw puzzle game with mild erotic content. The player meets up with various pretty young ladies at their school, attempting to woo them with jigsaw puzzle prowess. Each of the eight girls has multiple snapshots that appear as a puzzle, and completing the puzzle will reward the player with an animated scene of that girl; if the player can complete the puzzle quickly enough, the animated scene will show the girl topless, and the player will also get that girl's phone number to view the scene again. After gathering all eight phone numbers, an additional topless puzzle image is unlocked for each of the girls.

title: My Dream: On Air ga Matenakute
aka_titles: マイ・ドリーム オンエンが待てなくて
description:
My Dream is an simulation game focusing on the world of voice-actors. There are eight different heroines in the game, and each has been voiced by three different actresses. Voice actress for each heroine can be set up at the beginning of a new game, right after entering the player's name. The game doesn't feature default name for the player, and other characters will address you by the name you enter (both Japanese and Latin letters are available during name creation). The player focuses on a single heroine and by setting up a weekly schedule for her, the game advances as a visual novel with selectable dialogue and action choices at certain locations and during certain conversations. The weekly schedule is set by selecting locations on the map you wish to visit, one location per day. Different location offer different actions and participation in various events and meeting and talking to other characters. Each heroine has a default set of attributes which change over time, such as physical strength, self-confidence, stress, speaking skill, and other. During gameplay, static character images with mild animations such as talking, are glued over blurred real-life photos which are used as backgrounds.

Heroines with selectable voice-actresses include:

  • Nao Utsumi (voiced by Naoko Takano, Nao, or Miki Nagasawa)
  • Haruka Kudou (voiced by Tarako, Rika Matsumoto, or Kotono Mitsuishi)
  • Izumi Watanabe (voiced by Mayumi Tanaka, Noriko Hidaka, or Chisa Yokoyama)
  • Reika Shirouchi (voiced by Ai Orikasa, Naoko Matsui, or Rika Matsumoto)
  • Miyuki Yoshizawa (voiced by Kikuko Inoue, Miwako Hatayama, or Yuriko Fuchizaki)
  • Aya Takai (voiced by Mayumi Tanaka, Aya Hisakawa, or Akiko Hiramatsu)
  • Kurumi Kawai (voiced by Tarako, Yuriko Fuchizaki, or Yuuko Miyamura)
  • Erina Saitoh (voiced by Mika Nakai, Manami Komori, or Naoko Matsui)

title: Myst
description:
Myst is a single-player first-person point-and-click adventure game.

The player controls an unnamed traveler who discovers an unusual book titled Myst. The book contains a detailed description of an island, and touching its final page transports the traveler into the place described within it. With no immediate explanation and no visible way home, the player begins on Myst Island and must explore its buildings, machines, and hidden chambers to understand where they are and what happened there.

Myst Island serves as the central hub of the game. The island appears almost deserted, but traces of its former inhabitants remain in journals, mechanical devices, messages, and linking books. In the library, the player encounters red and blue books containing fragmented video messages from Sirrus and Achenar, two trapped brothers who each ask for help. Their messages are incomplete at first, and the player must recover missing pages from other Ages to learn more about them and decide how to proceed.

The game is presented from a first-person viewpoint using a simple cursor interface. The player moves between fixed viewpoints by clicking paths, doors, stairs, ladders, and other visible destinations. Interaction is handled by clicking or dragging objects in the environment, such as switches, levers, wheels, buttons, drawers, pages, doors, and control panels. There are no enemies, combat sequences, health meters, or conventional death states. Progress depends on observation, note-taking, and understanding how the island’s mechanisms connect to one another.

Puzzles are based largely on logic, spatial reasoning, sound, symbols, numbers, and environmental clues. Rather than collecting a large inventory of objects and using them on other objects, the player studies journals, diagrams, map markers, sounds, machinery, and visual patterns to determine how devices work. Many puzzles require information found in one location to be applied elsewhere, such as matching constellations, tuning sounds, setting mechanical controls, restoring power, or interpreting notes left behind by the island’s inhabitants.

As the player solves major puzzles on Myst Island, additional linking books become accessible. These books transport the player to other Ages, self-contained worlds with their own locations, devices, and puzzle chains. The main Ages include the Mechanical Age, Stoneship Age, Channelwood Age, and Selenitic Age. Each Age contains red and blue pages that can be returned to the corresponding books in the Myst library. Each Age also contains its own route back to Myst Island, usually locked behind another puzzle or sequence of mechanisms.

Different releases of Myst preserve the same central structure of solitary exploration, linking books, and puzzle-solving, although interface and presentation details may vary between platforms. The original version is built around fixed screens and point-and-click navigation, while other editions and remakes may alter movement or visual presentation. In all forms, the core game remains focused on exploring an uninhabited island, deciphering its Ages, and resolving the mystery behind the trapped figures in the library.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Nanatsu Kaze no Shima Monogatari
description:
The player takes the role of the dragon Garpu, who finds himself trapped on a mysterious island, where he is required to learn to harness the power of the seven winds.

The gameplay consists of trekking across platforms, interacting with characters, finding various objects to use where needed, and completing set tasks. Talking to characters reveals vital information to progress in the game. The power of the seven winds can be used to bypass obstacles.

title: Nanatsu no Hikan
description: In this mystery adventure game, a young man called Ippei has been given the key to the seven mansions his uncle wants to restore and turn into a resort. But these mansions were never fully explored and his uncle suspects a great treasure to be hiding somewhere on the premise, and Ippei is tasked to look into it. However, he is warned that there may be dangerous people lurking around. The game uses 3D graphics and a first-person perspective to let the player full explore the mansion up close. The more Ippei explores the mansion, the more he will find out about his family's history. Ippei can pick up and use various items, talk to other characters or simply think out loud to give clues to the player. While there are no action elements, the protagonist has a health bar which can be decreased if he is not careful and activates various traps that lie hidden throughout the mansions.

title: NASCAR 98
description: With top-of-the-line racing simulation NASCAR 98 allows you to race with 24 drivers including legend Dale Earnhardt and 10 official tracks and extra 6 fantasy tracks. This NASCAR game allows you to hear all screeching burnouts, oiled skids, and emergency vehicles, or listen to provided music. This includes the modes season, Arcade, and new custom racing(control opponents,laps,gas gauge, and just about anything.).

title: NBA Action
description:
TAKE IT TO THE HOLE!

• All 29 NBA teams
• Over 400 NBA players
• Monster surround sound
• Sweet 360° camera angles
• Radical playing views
• Season stat-tracking
• In-depth playbooks for offensive and defensive plays
• User records
• Player attributes in more than 20 categories
• Full instant replay options
• Create-a-player, Create-a-roster
• Custom playoffs
• Player trades
• Season-ending awards

title: NBA Action 98
description: Sega's first attempt at Basketball on the PC includes plenty of neat visuals; realistic AI and motion capture work; official licenses of the NBA including players, teams and courts; practice mode to help you get used to your team; and a multiplayer mode (for up to 5 players on one computer). You can also create your own team and players in the edit mode, in case you don't like what the NBA offers.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: NBA Jam Extreme
description:
"Takes the NBA Jam game and puts into an all new 3d engine with lifelike player movement. All the real basketball action is bundled with extreme moves. Zany sound fx, commentary and victory dances by the players."

Basketball with altered gameplay. Features two players on each team with a huge number of special dunks and moves. There is an inclusion of a new extreme button for added excitement. Commentary by Marv Albert.

title: NBA Jam Tournament Edition
description:
This game lets you play two-on-two arcade basketball with players from all the NBA teams. Gameplay is fast and action-packed, with few rules, no fouls, and deliberately unrealistic jamming. Players are rated on eight ability categories, from steals and blocks, to dunks and 3-pointers.

Up to four human players can take part, each always controlling a single player for their team, and AI for missing players. This allows for four players to face each other in teams of two, or for two players to team up against a third player with a CPU team-mate.
