After work, it's time to choose which girl to talk to. There are also many events that prompt the player to choose an action or a conversation option.

All these actions influence Yusuke's statistics, ultimately making him more (or less) attractive to the various girls he meets on his path. Depending on the way the player shapes and schedules the activities of the main character, he will follow one of the many different narratives, meet different people, and eventually - if the player is persistent enough - win the heart of the girl he loves.

The computer and the PC-FX versions feature scenes with explicit nudity and sexual situations.

title: Pia Carrot e Yōkoso!! 2
aka_titles: Pia♥キャロットへようこそ!! 2
description: This Sega Saturn port of Pia Carrot e Yōkoso!! 2 adds one new romance option (Tomomi Aizawa) and significant new scenario content compared to the original PC release. This version also censors the explicit sexual content.

title: Pict Flash Dondon
description: Pict Flash Dondon (ピクトフラッシュどんどん) is an educational software for the Sega Saturn for children of ages 1 to 6 years old.

title: Pinball Graffiti
aka_titles: ピンボールグラフィティ
description:
This pinball game has a 3D orientation in which the camera pans vertically wherever the ball moves or sometimes shows a closeup of the ball in rails and sinkholes. There are three different pinball tables:

  • Basketball Legend - Has the theme of a basketball court with coach-styled messages.
  • Card Master - Based on a casino theme, featuring poker and roulette.
  • Circus Fantasia - Displays a circus-styled theme with scoring for stunts.

The two modes in the game are the pinball mode, which feature only the pinball tables for the highest score or the story mode. In the story mode, a crippled basketball college student goes to a bar where he is inspired to become the best pinball champion player in the United States. The career-styled gameplay requires the player to make use of limited funds to make purchases, travel between cities and resting to stay healthy. Money is earned by beating opponents' scores in pinball or by winning a basketball mini-game.

title: Planet Joker
description: Planet Joker is a vertically-scrolling shoot-em-up with a strong story presentation. A mysterious army has invaded Tokyo, and it's up to a special crack team of JSDF mech pilots to defeat the invaders. The player chooses from one of seven different mech suits, each of which has different stats and a different set of attack abilities. In addition to regular shots and bombs, there is also a charged shot, and three different weapon types which can be swapped and upgraded by collecting items throughout each of the seven stages. There are also two competition modes: a time-attack mode to reach a set score as quickly as possible, and a caravan-style score attack mode with a time limit.

title: Playboy Karaoke Collection Volume 1
aka_titles: プレイボーイカラオケVol.1
description: Playboy Karaoke Collection Volume 1 (プレイボーイカラオケVol.1) is a 1996 compilation of karaoke music videos with Playboy models in the background released by VIC Tokai for the Sega Saturn exclusively in Japan. A second volume was also made.

title: Playboy Karaoke Collection Volume 2
aka_titles: プレイボーイカラオケvol.2
description: Playboy Karaoke Collection Volume 2 (プレイボーイカラオケvol.2) is a 1996 compilation of karaoke music videos with Playboy models in the background released by VIC Tokai for the Sega Saturn exclusively in Japan. A first volume was also made.

title: Pocket Fighter
description:
Pocket Fighter is a single-player and multiplayer 2D fighting game. It features characters from Capcom’s major series, such as Street Fighter and Darkstalkers, reimagined in super-deformed chibi style. There is no overarching story tying the roster together, but each fighter has short humorous cutscenes and rival interactions that parody their parent franchises. Players step into the role of one of these pint-sized brawlers and fight through a series of matches filled with slapstick comedy and exaggerated transformations.

Combat uses simplified controls compared to traditional fighting games. Instead of complex inputs, most attacks are mapped to straightforward button presses, making the game accessible to casual players. Standard punches and kicks can be chained into combo strings, which often trigger comedic costume changes or visual gags. These transformations briefly dress characters in outfits drawn from other Capcom games before delivering their next strike, emphasizing the parody style.

A central mechanic is the collection of colored gems. When a character is struck, gems spill out onto the stage, which can then be picked up by either player. Each color corresponds to a different attack type - red for punches, blue for kicks, and yellow for special moves. Gathering gems upgrades those categories, increasing both the power and variety of available techniques. The gem system introduces a layer of strategy, as managing offense and defense directly impacts a character’s move set during the match.

Super moves and special abilities play a large role. Each character retains signature attacks from their original series, though presented in exaggerated fashion. For example, Ryu still throws Hadokens, but with over-the-top animations, while Morrigan’s attacks are delivered with comedic flourishes. Characters also have unique “Flash Combo” sequences, which are extended chains that automatically launch when the player performs a specific input, often accompanied by elaborate costume gags.

The game includes multiple modes. The single-player arcade mode pits a character against a ladder of opponents, ending with a short comical ending sequence. Versus mode allows competitive matches between two players. Additional features such as training options and survival challenges appear in certain ports.

title: Policenauts
description:
In the year 2010 mankind has built its first space colony, Beyond Coast. Three years later the founders of the colony felt it needed to be protected, and chose five best policemen from Earth to do that: Gates Becker from Scotland Yard, the Japanese Sadaoki Tokugawa, Salvatore Toscanini from New York, and two policemen from Los Angeles: Jonathan Ingram and his best friend Ed Brown. During a routine patrol on Beyond Coast, something happened to Jonathan's spacesuit. He was sucked into space and presumed dead. Twenty-five years later, he is miraculously discovered in his life pod, alive. He still looks like a young man, but in reality, he is fifty-five years old.

Trying to forget his past, Jonathan opens an investigation agency on Earth. One day, his ex-wife unexpectedly pays him a visit. She has re-married during Jonathan's prolonged absence and asks him to find her missing husband. When she leaves the office, her car explodes, and she dies. Determined to fulfill her final request, Jonathan prepares to re-visit Beyond Coast.

Policenauts is a Japanese-style adventure with action elements, similar in many ways to Snatcher. The player interacts with the environment in a point-and-click fashion: positioning a cursor over an object allows the player character to examine it or perform other context-dependent actions. There are a few puzzles in the game, but most of the time the story is advanced by visiting various locations, examining objects, and talking to characters. Conversations usually include a selection of topics.

Action sequences are similar to those of Snatcher, but are more numerous and varied. The player must rapidly shoot enemies moving within a one-screen area viewed from a first-person perspective, reloading the gun manually and trying to eliminate the enemy before Jonathan's health bar is depleted.

title: Power Drift
description:
Ever wanted to race dune buggies at high speed on a variety of tracks? Power Drift is an arcade racer that gives you the chance to do just that.

There are 5 tracks to choose from, each with 5 stages. The stages range from cities, to deserts to tracks over water. There are also 12 drivers to pick from, from businessmen to skinheads and mohicans.

Your buggy has 2 gears, high and low. Once the light goes green, just keep the pedal to the metal. You’ll need to place third or higher to continue to the next stage. Be careful not to bump into other buggies or objects next to the road. While your buggy can take a pounding, crashing will slow you down.

Finish all 5 stages in a level and you’ll be presented with a bonus level.

title: Powerslave
description:
In this first-person shooter, you're an armed forces specialist sent to investigate strange happenings at the ancient Egyptian city of Karnak.

Soon you learn that alien invaders with a penchant for mummifying humans alive have taken over the place.

You have to fight your way through increasingly difficult levels with an unbelievable cast in order to finish it.

title: Primal Rage
description:
Primal Rage is a single-player and two-player one-on-one fighting game. The game is set after a massive meteor strike devastates Earth, reshaping it into a post-apocalyptic world known as Urth. From the destruction, seven ancient gods awaken in the forms of giant dinosaurs and apes. Each god seeks dominion over the ruined planet, and humanity’s survivors gather as tribes of worshippers around the creature they believe will rule the new world.

The player chooses one of the seven gods and fights the others for control of Urth. The roster includes creatures aligned with destructive, predatory, protective, or chaotic forces, such as fire-breathing tyrants, armored beasts, agile raptors, cold-dwelling apes, and venomous monsters. In single-player mode, the chosen god battles through the remaining opponents, while two-player mode allows both players to choose creatures and fight directly. Each character has special moves performed through button and directional commands. These include projectiles, lunges, stomps, aerial attacks, defensive techniques, and character-specific abilities tied to the creature’s theme. Combos and repeated hits can create openings, while blocking, spacing, and timing remain important because many attacks leave the fighter vulnerable if they miss.

Matches are fought from a side-view perspective using standard fighting-game rules. Each creature can walk, jump, crouch, block, throw, and attack with different strengths of strikes. Because the fighters are large monsters rather than human martial artists, their attacks include bites, claws, tail strikes, body slams, leaps, and other animalistic movements. The goal is to reduce the opponent’s life bar to zero across a best-of-rounds match.

A distinctive system involves human worshippers who appear at the bottom of the arena. These small followers represent the tribes devoted to the fighting gods. They can be attacked or eaten during battle, and eating them can restore health. This adds a resource element to matches, since a player may try to recover life while also remaining exposed to the opposing creature.

At the end of a match, defeated opponents can be finished with character-specific finishing moves. These sequences are performed with command inputs and are separate from ordinary attacks. They reinforce the game’s violent monster-god theme, but they do not create branching story paths or change the match structure. Progression remains based on winning fights and advancing through the roster.

The visual style uses digitized stop-motion animation based on physical creature models. This gives the fighters a different look from hand-drawn sprite-based fighting games, with large animated monsters placed against ruined or prehistoric arena backgrounds.

title: Princess Crown
aka_titles: プリンセス　クラウン
description:
You play as Gradriel, youngest daughter of Elfrenne, queen of Valendria. Twenty-five years ago Elfrenne destroyed the demonic forces that were threatening the country. With Elfrenne's passing, Gradriel is crowned the new queen at the age of thirteen, her court shelter the young tomboy queen inside her castle against her will. Fortunately for Gradriel, the fairy Aria sneaks into the castle with a direct petition for her: the fairy forest is wrongly framed for a crime, and the new Queen should come see the truth for herself. In exchange for following this request, Aria helps Gradriel sneak out of the castle to begin adventuring. In Gradriel's absence from her castle, an evil spirit has secretly invaded Valendria and is trying to take control over Gradriel's two older sisters. Will the young queen succeed in defeating the evil?

This is an action RPG, somewhat similar to the third game in Ys series. The entire game world is a side-scrolling platform on which fights, exploration, and conversation with the NPCs take place. The combat is detailed and contains elements of fighting games. Although the young queen develops like a RPG protagonist, she can also use various physical moves in combat: kick, dash, defend, crouch, etc.

title: Princess Maker 2
description:
A hero saved the human race from utter annihilation by the gods. This same hero then was charged by the heavens to take care of a young seed dropped from there. This seed becomes his daughter, and her guardian will be watching her progress.

In Princess Maker 2 the player assumes the role of a father to the blessed daughter of the heavens. For the next eight years, the hero will nurture and guide her in the path of the player's own choosing.

It is possible to choose the path of the zodiac-influenced daughter by scheduling her to jobs and schools, which will raise her statistics (strength, combat skills, cooking, faith, etc.). Each month allows the player to designate three different tasks for her to follow. Balancing between character development, stress level, health and financial income is the focus of this game.

Mini sub-quests and various plot options revolve around the young lady adventuring in the wilderness, provided that she's strong enough to tame the wilds. The player can equip her with armor and weapons to fight off wandering random monsters in turn-based combat.

The game starts with the daughter at age ten, from which point the player guides her until her adult years. Choices made during the course of the game will determine her eventual marital status, accomplishments, and her relationships with other people. There are 74 unique endings in the game.

title: Princess Maker: Fairy Tales Come True
aka_titles: Princess Maker 3: Fairy Tales Come True
description: The third main installment (and fourth game in all) in Gainax' Princess Maker simulation series. A young fairy wants to become a human princess. The fairy Queen first refuses to fulfill her wish, but the fairy becomes so upset that the Queen finally decides to make her reborn as a princess, and entrusts her future to you. You are the one responsible for what the little princess will become. You can give her a good education, let her study a lot, fight, develop her sense for arts, etc. The princess will go to school and make friends and rivals, and live her life to the full according to your plans.

title: Princess Maker: Yumemiru Yousei
description: The third main installment (and fourth game in all) in Gainax' Princess Maker simulation series. A young fairy wants to become a human princess. The fairy Queen first refuses to fulfill her wish, but the fairy becomes so upset that the Queen finally decides to make her reborn as a princess, and entrusts her future to you. You are the one responsible for what the little princess will become. You can give her a good education, let her study a lot, fight, develop her sense for arts, etc. The princess will go to school and make friends and rivals, and live her life to the full according to your plans.

title: Princess Quest
description:
In the Kingdom of Dilma, dignitaries from many other nations have gathered for the coronation of the new king. However, before the ceremony takes place, a treasure of the kingdom, a priceless jewel integral to the ceremony, has been stolen from the prince's bedroom. The suspect fled into the castle's dungeon, and the prince went after them but has not returned. There are five suspects who do not have an alibi: five beautiful princesses from other countries. The young knight Willow has been summoned to investigate, find the thief, and recover the stolen jewel.

Princess Quest is a first-person dungeon-crawler RPG with love adventure elements. The player controls Willow to investigate the theft, and Willow is also able to magically transform into a female form called Will. Willow and Will have different combat abilities, with Willow adept at physical attacks while Will excels at magic, and during the investigation some characters will only be willing to speak openly to one form or the other. The player can return to Willow's room in the castle to switch forms.

The player can explore the castle and surrounding town from a top-down perspective to speak with other characters and obtain clues and information. The dungeons are explored in first-person with up to two of the princesses accompanying the player. Only Willow/Will participates directly in the turn-based combat, while the other two characters provide special abilities to help the player.

The first-print limited edition of the game includes a set of three trading cards but is otherwise identical.

title: Prisoner of Ice
aka_titles: Call of Cthulhu: Prisoner of Ice
description:
Another game in Infogrames' line of H. P. Lovecraft inspired games started by Alone In the Dark, Prisoner of Ice puts you in the role of Lt. Ryan, an American agent stationed aboard the submarine H.M.S. Victoria on a rescue mission to the Antarctic. The Victoria picks up two mysterious crates during the course of the rescue. Before you know it the Captain is eaten alive by the cargo, a horrific monster with whom you are trapped aboard the submarine. And that's just the start of your problems.

Prisoner of Ice features a very simplified version of the classic adventure game interface, where you can left click with the cursor to operate an object or right click to look at it. The program won't let you do anything with these objects, other than the few appropriate actions needed to advance the game.

It includes a gallery of photos and video clips of 18 girls, as well as a quiz minigame with 10 questions. There is no bonus reward for completing the minigame.

プラドルＤＩＳＣ データ編 レースクイーン Ｇ

description: Private Idol Disc: Tokubetsu-Hen Kogyaru Daijyakka 100 is a Miscellaneous game, developed and published by Genki, which was released in Japan in 1997.

title: Pro Mahjong Kiwame S
description:
Pro Mahjong Kiwame S is a 4-player riichi mahjong game and part of Athena's long-running Pro Mahjong Kiwame series. As is standard for the series, it features the endorsement of the Japan Professional Mahjong League and includes the likenesses of 16 professional mahjong players.

The main arcade mode gives the player a choice of four different routes throughout Japan. Each stage on a route involves a match against specific real-life pro players, and the player must earn a set number of points in order to proceed to the next stage. The Saturn home version of the game adds a free match mode, a mahjong quiz mode, and an "analysis" mode where the player must select the correct moves for certain situations.

title: Pro Mahjong Tsuwamono 2
description:
Pro Mahjong Tsuwamono 2 is a mahjong game featuring the likenesses of 16 professional players, and the follow-up to Pro Mahjong Tsuwamono. While the selection of pros is different, most of the available modes and options are similar to the previous game. There is a free battle mode against any selection of pro players, a tournament mode with three different titles to earn, a parlor mode with six different specific situations, and a mahjong guidance mode that advises players on how to improve their mahjong gameplay.

The major updates in this edition are an improved guidance mode which advises players on higher level play, and the addition of detailed stat tracking. While each version of the game varies in audiovisual presentation and title, all versions include the same selection of game modes and feature the same 16 professional players.

title: Pro Pinball
description: In this pinball simulation, you play on a table called "The Web". With the help of three flippers, you must send the ball into the various openings, trapdoors, and ramps. You can gain various bonuses (such as several balls to knock at the same time) if you play particularly well. Some of the targets activate special missions when you hit them with a ball. Those missions vary from aiming at specific targets to playing mini-games, such as shooting asteroids. After you have completed five missions, you'll be able to face the Dark Queen, the off-screen antagonist of the game.

title: Pro Pinball: The Web
description:
In this pinball simulation, you play on a table called "The Web". With the help of three flippers, you must send the ball into the various openings, trapdoors, and ramps. You can gain various bonuses (such as several balls to knock at the same time) if you play particularly well. Some of the targets activate special missions when you hit them with a ball. Those missions vary from aiming at specific targets to playing mini-games, such as shooting asteroids. After you have completed five missions, you'll be able to face the Dark Queen, the off-screen antagonist of the game.

Unlike many other pinball games, "The Web" aims for realistic simulation of pinball. The game implements real table physics, and doesn't feature any unrealistic gadgets or living enemies.

title: Pro Shinan Mahjong: Tsuwamono
description:
Pro Mahjong Tsuwamono is a mahjong game featuring the likenesses of 16 professional players. There is a free battle mode against any selection of pro players, a tournament mode with three different titles to earn, a parlor mode with six different specific situations, and a mahjong guidance mode that advises players on how to improve their mahjong gameplay.

While each version of the game varies in audiovisual presentation and title, all versions include the same selection of game modes and feature the same 16 professional players.

title: Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '97
aka_titles: プロ野球 グレイテストナイン'97
description:
Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '97 is a baseball game featuring featuring an NPB (Nippon Professional Baseball) license and all twelve teams and all players from the Central and Pacific Leagues of Japanese baseball for the 1997 season, and the third game in Sega's Greatest Nine series of Sega Saturn baseball games.

The game features an overhauled visual style that uses fully-3D player models instead of the digitized sprites of the previous two games. Available modes are Open Game (Exhibition), Pennant Race, and Home Run Contest — the Tournament and All-Star modes have been removed. The Team Edit mode also returns, though the player database is no longer available. The Nagoya Dome and Osaka Dome stadiums — brand new at the time of the game's release — have also been added to the available real-life stadiums.

A modified version featuring American MLB teams and players was released internationally as World Series Baseball 98.

title: Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '97: Make Miracle
aka_titles: プロ野球 グレイテストナイン'97 メークミラクル
Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '97: Make Miracle
description: Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '97: Make Miracle is an updated release of baseball game Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '97. This version adds a "1997 Pennant" mode that recreates the actual events of the 1997 season, updates the player rosters, and allows for changing the camera viewpoint during play. It is otherwise nearly identical to the original version of the game.

title: Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '98
aka_titles: プロ野球 グレイテストナイン'98
description:
Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '98 is a baseball game featuring featuring an NPB (Nippon Professional Baseball) license and all 12 teams and all players from the Central and Pacific Leagues of Japanese baseball for the 1998 season, and the fourth main game in Sega's Greatest Nine series of Sega Saturn baseball games.

The game is very similar to the previous year's entry, featuring the same visual style and all of the same game modes: Open Game (Exhibition), Pennant Race, Home Run Contest, and Team Edit. New in this entry is the so-called Narikiri Mode, a variant of Pennant Race where instead of controlling a full team, the player picks a single player from one team to control.

title: Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '98: Summer Action
description: Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '98: Summer Action is an updated release of baseball game Pro Yakyū Greatest Nine '98. This version updates the player rosters to the most current data as of the end of the 1998 season, adds additional original teams, and adds additional management features to the Narikiri Mode introduced in the previous release. It is the last entry in the series to appear on the Sega Saturn.

title: Pro Yakyū Team mo Tsukurō!
aka_titles: プロ野球チームもつくろう！
description: Pro Yakyū Team mo Tsukurō! ("Let's Make a Pro Baseball Team, Too!") is baseball management simulation game spun off from Sega's better-known soccer management series. Selecting one of the 12 teams from the Japanese professional leagues, the goal is to build that team into the greatest baseball team in the world. Many aspects of managing a team are simulated and under control of the player, from hiring players and staff, determining training schedules and strategies before games, to even managing the team's finances and constructing facilities. The player can also create multiple custom players to sign to their team and train, and it is also possible to host an exhibition match against another player's team using a password function.

title: Pu•Li•Ru•La
description:
Pu-Li-Ru-La is a psychedelic side-scrolling arcade beat 'em up set in the magical land of Radishland. As the story goes, some evil magical entity has stolen the keys of time for the towns in Radishland, freezing time and turning every animal and creature into evil magical contraptions. Only Zac and Mel, empowered with their "invented magic sticks" are able to escape the curse and must thread through Radishland turning all the monsters back into their original form and recovering the keys of time.

Gameplay-wise the game is a side-scrolling beat 'em up in which you control your character in a 2.5D isometric plane as he clears each stage by beating the many wacky enemies with his stick and a few magic spells that are randomly selected whenever you start the game. At the end of each stage there is a harder "boss" creature you must defeat and upon doing so you proceed to the next stage.

The game is notable for its surreal graphic design, featuring digitized graphics merged with hand-drawn sprites and featuring mostly colorful nonsensical graphics. Features single player or co-op two-player gameplay modes.

title: Pukunpa: Joshikōsei no Hōkago...
description:
Pukunpa: Joshikōsei no Hōkago... is a falling-block puzzle game featuring a cast of cute anime girls who each represent a different school club.

The game plays very similarly to the popular Puyo Puyo series, with colored blobs falling in pairs which must be rotated and arranged by the player. Matching three or more blobs of the same color will cause them to vanish, allowing any stacked above them to fall down and potentially trigger a chain that will send garbage blocks to the opponent. The unique feature here is that some blobs actually contain two different colors; these pieces cannot be cleared on their own, but when a neighboring piece is cleared the double piece expands, releasing the two colored blobs from inside, and allowing for further chain attack potential. If the pieces stack all the way to the top of the well, then that player loses the round.

The game includes two game modes: a versus mode against the computer or a second player, and an endless mode for one or two players. The game also includes an alternate "Funny Mode" which replaces the anime-style girls with crudely-drawn fantasy characters.

title: Pup-Breeder
description:
Five young goddesses have been summoned on the orders of God: there's a shortage of guardians on Earth, and to decide who among them is fit to protect the people of Earth, these goddesses must prove their abilities through a test of leadership and compassion.

Pup-Breeder is a simulation game where the player takes the role of one of the goddesses, who is tasked with raising angelic creatures called "pups". These pups come in many different forms, which each have their own abilities and personalities — some may be good at fighting, some may have strong defense, some might have high agility or other unique skills — and the player starts out by selecting a team of five. Each of the pups functions like a virtual pet-style creature, tracking not only its health but also its trust and affection with the player.

The player character does not appear directly in the world or control the pups directly, but rather can issue commands to each of the pups such as to move or stop, use an item, attack a target, or activate a special ability. There are a variety of different missions which each have a different goal, such as causing the sun to rise, collecting shards of shooting stars, or defeating an evil familiar.

title: Purikura Daisakusen
description:
In Purikura Daisakusen, the Miracle Kingdom has been invaded by an evil mechanical army, all of its inhabitants have been magically transformed into animals, and the queen has been imprisoned. Taking on the role of either the gallant knight Grey, or one of the queen's sisters Kurara or Kirara, the player must reach the queen and save the land while demolishing any creature that stands in their way.

The game plays as an isometric scrolling shooter, in which the player must navigate their chosen character through stages, killing enemies with magic attacks while collecting power-ups and other unique items. Attacks can be melee or ranged, with each being capable of being upgraded via power-ups, and a dodge ability allows the player to avoid most basic attacks. Each character also has a "super" form, which becomes available with enough magic energy. The player also has a familiar with them at all times, which gradually evolves and increases its powers with each enemy defeated.

Features simultaneous 2-player cooperative gameplay and a bonus gallery mode with a fully-voiced commentary option.

title: Puyo Puyo 2
description:
The follow-up to Puyo Puyo is, like its predecessor, a falling block game in which the goal is to combine four or more blocks (Puyos) of the same color, which then disappear. The remaining Puyos will then fall down and can produce combos which can cause special blocks (Nuisance Puyos, that can only be destroyed by eliminating adjacent Puyos) to appear on the enemy's field.

This game includes a story mode, in which Arle (the main character) fights against computer enemies, a vs player mode, a four player mode (SNES only), and an endless mode (SNES only).

title: Puyo Puyo Sun
description:
Puyo Puyo Sun is the third entry in the main Puyo Puyo series of real-time puzzle games, its title being a pun involving the Japanese word for "three". The evil Dark Prince has caused the sun to augment its size and power to dangerous levels, and thus the Puyo Puyo world is on the verge of being scorched unless you prevent it.

The game features three distinct story campaigns, each pitting you against a different set of enemies which you must battle in classic Puyo Puyo fashion: In each stage you face off against an opponent in two different play areas, one for you and one for your opponent. As the blob-like "puyos" start falling in your play area, you must align them and create groups of the same color in order to clear the screen before you get flooded with puyos. Chaining puyos of different colors allows you to send several "garbage" puyos to the opposing player's play area in hopes of either flooding it, or slowing his advance, and whoever defeats the opposing player moves on to the next challenger.

New for Puyo Puyo Sun are the Sun Puyos, which can be added to combos for extra damage. Also includes 2P vs gameplay, challenge modes and galleries and other bonus features.

title: Puyo Puyo Sun for SegaNet
description: This special release of Puyo Puyo Sun is modified to exclusively support online multiplayer functionality via the Sega Saturn Modem and XBand service. Released at a lower price, most of the single-player content has been removed from this version, with only the single-player endless mode available for offline play.

title: Puzzle & Action: 2do Arukoto wa Sand-R
description:
Puzzle & Action: 2do Arukoto wa Sand-R (Puzzle & Action: Treasure Hunt) is the third and final instalment in the Puzzle & Action series, after Puzzle & Action: Tant-R and Puzzle & Action: Ichidant-R. Like the previous games, players play a series of timed mini games to overcome enemies.

Gameplay is similar to the previous games, although the games are in 3D. There are four rounds of a number of timed mini games, and two players are supported. Twenty-two categorized mini games are featured, and like the previous instalments, there is a 'Free Play' mode where they can be practiced. The Saturn version features a RPG-style 'Original mode', which features a shop where items such as torches and brooms can be purchased.

title: Puzzle & Action: Treasure Hunt
description:
Puzzle & Action: Treasure Hunt is the third game in the Puzzle & Action series of multiplayer minigame collections. There are a total of 27 different minigames, ranging from block puzzles and matching castle layouts, to opening a stubborn pickle jar and determining which bottle contains a hair growth medicine.

The main arcade mode has the players taking the role of explorers evading capture, searching for treasure, and ultimately chasing after pirates who steal the treasure. Each scene has multiple opponents who must be defeated by clearing randomly-selected minigames. The Saturn version includes an arranged mode which adds various items and shops throughout the game, as well as new boss minigames. The home port also includes a free play mode where any of the minigames can be practiced.

title: Puzzle Bobble 2X & Space Invaders
description: This two-disc bundle contains copies of Puzzle Bobble 2X and Space Invaders bundled together in a cardboard slipcase.

title: Puzzle Bobble 3 for SegaNet
description: This special release of Puzzle Bobble 3 is modified to exclusively support online multiplayer functionality via the Sega Saturn Modem and XBand service. Released at a lower price, most of the single-player content has been removed from this version, with only a short demo of the standard puzzle mode available for offline play.

title: Pyon Pyon Caruru no Mahjong Biyori
aka_titles: Pyon Pyon Kyaruru no Mahjong Biyori
Pyon Pyon Caruru no Mahjong Biyori
description: Pyon Pyon Caruru no Mahjong Biyori is a family-friendly 1-on-1 style mahjong game featuring a cast of cutesy cartoon characters. Gameplay is a straightforward translation of Japanese-style reach mahjong with no notable additional features, and includes both a story mode with five playable (plus one unlockable) characters and a free match mode, along with a gallery featuring unlockable artwork of the characters.

title: Quake
description:
An enemy codenamed “Quake,” believed to come from another dimension, is using teleportation gates to invade Earth. The player takes the role of a nameless soldier who arrives at his base only to discover that Quake’s forces have overrun it and killed everyone. Somewhere in the base is a teleporter leading to Quake’s realm. The mission is clear: enter the enemy’s dimension, fight through hordes of monsters, and strike back.

id Software’s follow-up to Doom and Doom II, Quake is a first-person shooter. Its main technological innovation is its use of a true 3D engine: the levels, enemies, and objects are built from polygons rather than sprites and flat level geometry. This allows for more natural level design, smoother character animation, vertical spaces, and more dynamic movement. It also supports gameplay elements such as bouncing grenades, projectiles traveling through three-dimensional space, and enemies attacking from above or below the player. The fully 3D environments make vertical movement more important than in id Software’s earlier shooters, with ledges, lifts, underwater passages, jumping, and enemies positioned at different heights.

The game begins in a start area where the player chooses a difficulty setting and enters gateways leading to the four episodes. In single-player mode, the player progresses through these episodes in search of exits while fighting enemies and collecting weapons, ammunition, health, armor, and keys. Interaction with the game world is minimal: since there is no dedicated use key, buttons and switches are activated by touching or shooting them. As in id Software’s earlier shooters, the levels contain numerous secret areas, including hidden exits that lead to secret levels.

Unlike Doom’s mixture of futuristic technology and demonic imagery, Quake’s setting combines several different styles. Each episode begins in a military base connected to the slipgate network, but later levels shift into environments inspired by medieval fantasy, gothic horror, and dark otherworldly architecture, including castles, dungeons, caverns, crypts, and temples. The visual style is darker and more muted than Doom’s, with many levels dominated by browns, grays, stone, metal, and earth tones. The game’s atmosphere is reinforced by an ambient soundtrack and sound design by Trent Reznor and Nine Inch Nails, emphasizing dread and isolation rather than traditional action music.

The enemy roster reflects this blend of themes. Early levels include human soldiers armed with shotguns or energy weapons, while later areas introduce knights, zombies, ogres with grenade launchers and chainsaws, leaping fiends, floating scrags, and larger supernatural creatures. The player’s weapons are mostly modern or industrial in function but have a rough, brutal feel. The arsenal includes an axe, shotguns, nailguns, grenade and rocket launchers, and the Thunderbolt, which discharges electrical energy.

Quake was one of the early first-person shooters designed with both LAN and Internet play in mind. The single-player levels can be played cooperatively, but the game became especially known for its deathmatch mode. Free-for-all matches, team play, and one-on-one duels are supported, with an emphasis on fast reactions, map knowledge, weapon control, and skillful movement through fully 3D spaces. Single-player maps can be used for multiplayer, and the game also includes maps designed specifically for deathmatch.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Quantum Gate
aka_titles: Quantum Game I: Akuma no Joshou
Quantum Gate: No One Dreams Here
description: Quantum Gate is an adventure game set on a distant planet, in which you are sent out to fight in a war with an alien race. Most of the game is played in a first person perspective, as you travel around your base and talk to other people. There are also fighting segments, done in FPS mode, in which you and your computer allies must battle alien soldiers.

title: Quantum Gate I: Akumu no Joshou
description: Quantum Gate is an adventure game set on a distant planet, in which you are sent out to fight in a war with an alien race. Most of the game is played in a first person perspective, as you travel around your base and talk to other people. There are also fighting segments, done in FPS mode, in which you and your computer allies must battle alien soldiers.

title: Quarantine
aka_titles: Death Throttle: Kakuzetsu Toshi kara no Dasshutsu
description:
Quarantine is a single-player vehicular combat and taxi-driving action game.

The game takes place in Kemo, a violent city sealed off from the outside world and used as a quarantine zone. The player controls Drake Edgewater, a taxi driver trapped inside the city and looking for a way to escape. Kemo’s streets are filled with criminals, rival vehicles, hostile pedestrians, gangs, and other hazards, making even ordinary fares part of a fight for survival.

Drake’s work as a cab driver provides both income and access to the city’s underground. Passengers can be picked up from the street and delivered to their destinations for money, while special assignments from resistance contacts and undercover clients move the story forward. The larger objective is to gain enough resources, information, and access to leave Kemo rather than simply continue driving fares forever.

Gameplay is viewed from inside the taxi, with the player driving through the city in first person. The player steers through streets, intersections, alleys, and traffic while watching the map and destination indicators to find passengers and drop-off points. Passengers usually have a time limit or destination requirement, so the player must balance speed, route choice, and survival.

The cab is armed and can be upgraded. Weapons include mounted guns and heavier equipment used against enemy vehicles, hostile citizens, and other threats. Money earned from fares and missions can be spent on weapons, armor, repairs, ammunition, and vehicle improvements. Service stations and shops are important between jobs, since entering the streets without enough protection or ammunition can make later missions difficult.

Combat and driving are closely linked. The player may need to fight through traffic, clear attackers from the road, or destroy enemies while still trying to reach a destination. Collisions, enemy fire, and reckless driving can damage the cab, while running out of ammunition or armor can force the player to retreat for repairs. Pedestrians and traffic are part of the active city environment, giving each route a mixture of navigation, shooting, and hazard avoidance.

Kemo is divided into multiple districts, and progression depends on completing missions that unlock access to new areas. Ordinary taxi work helps fund upgrades, but story missions are required to advance toward escape. These missions may involve deliveries, combat objectives, contact work, or travel through dangerous parts of the city. Passwords or saved progress allow the player to continue from later stages depending on the version.

title: Quarterback Attack
description:
Quarterback Attack is a single-player full-motion-video American football simulation game. The player takes the role of a rookie quarterback starting in a major championship game for a fictional professional football team. Rather than controlling every player on the field, the game places the player in the quarterback’s role for the entire contest. Mike Ditka appears as the team’s coach, giving instructions, criticism, and reactions from the sideline as the game progresses.

The story structure is limited to this one football game. After the opening kickoff and return, the player’s job is to lead the offense down the field, call plays, avoid the pass rush, complete passes, and score enough points to win. The game does not include a season mode, team management, player trades, or a full roster simulation.

Before each offensive play, the player chooses from a playbook of running and passing plays. Passing plays are the main focus. Once the ball is snapped, the view shifts behind the quarterback, showing the pocket, the approaching defenders, and the field ahead. The player must decide quickly whether to stay in the pocket, move away from pressure, scramble, or attempt a pass.

Passing is handled through receiver views and a targeting cursor. The player can switch attention to eligible receivers, look for an open target, and aim the pass before releasing the ball. Timing is important, since waiting too long can allow the defense to sack the quarterback, while throwing too early or aiming poorly can lead to an incompletion or interception.

Running plays and scrambling give the player limited ground options. These are not controlled like a conventional football game with full team movement, but they allow the quarterback and offense to gain yards without relying entirely on passing. The player must still manage downs, field position, time, and scoring opportunities within the structure of the single game.

The game uses full-motion video and digitized player footage to present the action. Football sequences, sideline reactions, defensive rushes, receiver views, tackles, and coaching comments are shown through filmed clips and composited images rather than polygonal or sprite-based football play. The interaction is built around choosing plays, making quick passing decisions, and responding to the filmed situation as it unfolds.

title: Quarterback Attack with Mike Ditka
description:
In this semi-FMV game you play a rookie facing his first game as starting quarterback on a fictional team, and this just happens to be The Big Game.

The entire game consists of this confrontation. When starting the game you watch a video of a kickoff and return, and then you get to select among 110 plays (100 passing and 10 running). The meat of the game is on the passing plays, where you are switched to a 3rd person behind-the-quarterback view from which you can see oncoming rushers. You can also zoom in on any receiver and via a targeting cursor make passes, or scramble if you don't find an open man.

Graphics consist mostly of FMV and super-imposed digitized images of no more than 320 x 200 pixels in resolution. There are also 6 difficulty settings to choose from.

title: Quiz Nanairo Dreams: Nijiiro-chō no Kiseki
aka_titles: Quiz Nanairo Dreams: Nijiirochou no Kiseki
QUIZ なないろDREAMS 虹色町の奇跡
Quiz Nanairo Dreams: Nijiiro-chō no Kiseki
description:
One night in Nijiiro Town, you look up and see eight meteors falling from the sky. One lands near you, and it turns out to be a small fairy. She tells you that the other seven meteors are a crystal that seals away a demon king in her world, split apart into pieces. These crystals have been found by seven girls throughout the town, and if you aren't able to collect their power within six months, the demon king will be revived. So to restore the crystal's power and prevent the world's destruction, you must befriend these seven cute girls and earn their trust... by answering trivia questions!

Quiz Nanairo Dreams: Nijiiro-chō no Kiseki is a cross between a quiz game, a board game, and a dating simulation. Each space on the board represents a day, and the player spins a roulette to determine how many spaces to move. Each space contains various events, recovery items, or one of the girls. Meet with a girl and she'll ask you a series of trivia questions; get enough of them right and her story will continue. At the end of each month you'll face a boss battle against the demon king's minion Linz, and at the end of the game you must face the demon king himself, again as a battle of trivia questions.

The console versions of the game add proper endings for both Linz and the fairy, and also changes the names of all the characters to avoid trademark issues; it is otherwise the same game.

title: QuoVadis
description:
Far in the future, humanity has spread across the galaxy, and following a long period of war, peace finally came after a treaty between the 10 great powers of the galaxy. It has been 99 years since then, and peace has prospered. On the 100th anniversary of the treaty, a new peacekeeping fleet not controlled by any one power is being established to strengthen galactic peace. But some of the nations are planning a rebellion, and the students joining this new fleet are about to be swept up in something much greater than they could have ever imagined.

Quovadis is a turn-based isometric sci-fi war strategy game. The player controls a fleet of up to eight space warships that gradually increases in size and capability, eventually expanding to multiple fleets with different capabilities. In each mission, the player must issue commands to each ship, with the goal of defeating all enemy ships.

title: QuoVadis 2: Wakusei Kyōshū Ovan Rei
aka_titles: クォヴァディス2 惑星強襲オヴァン・レイ
description:
Ten years ago, the elite officer Ovan was assigned to the president's security detail at his inauguration. Following a barely-averted assassination attempt, he attempts to track down the group responsible, but his plane is shot down and he's soon branded a traitor, wrongly accused of masterminding the attack. Forced to flee his home planet, Ovan becomes a mercenary and eventually finds and joins the group responsible for the assassination attempt, hoping to exact his revenge.

QuoVadis 2: Wakusei Kyōshū Ovan Rei ("The Ovan Rei Planet Assault") is a sci-fi realtime strategy game. It is the sequel to QuoVadis, though the gameplay is completely different and the story is largely unrelated despite taking place in the same universe. The player commands a squad of various primary and support units, with the primary interaction being simply to direct units around the map as they will attack automatically when within range of enemies. Each mission has specific objectives such as taking control of a location or protecting certain units from attack as they travel across the map, and between missions the player can configure the loadout and characteristics of each unit in detail according to the next mission's requirement.

title: R?MJ: The Mystery Hospital
description: R?MJ is an interactive movie horror adventure game with full voice-acting and without subtitles to feel more like a movie. The story takes place in a summer of 1999, as a large explosion occurred in a General Hospital. Due to a deadly virus being released, the hospital is on lockdown, and you are left with no way out. The player assumes the role of Hajime, who after going to visit his best friend, finds himself trapped in a hospital along with two friends, Ryou and Tomowo, and a rookie nurse, Aya. The gameplay consists of exploring locations in the hospital by moving in a certain direction (forward, turn left or right, or turn back) which uses pre-rendered animation for every movement from one point to another. Certain locations can be zoomed in to give you more details or to pick up an item. Your companions will often give you some comments while you explore, most of which may seem a selection of five sentences that are randomly selected. The game also features the use of player's senses (sight, hearing, touch, smell and taste) which must be used at key locations and events in order to progress the game.

title: Rabbit
description:
Rabbit is a 2D fighting game, with cartoonish colorful graphics. The game has 8 playable characters - Wu Ling (Rabbit), Tien-Ren (hawk), Eight (ox), Hou-En (wolf), Ja-Koh (snake), Yu-Lan (fox), Rex (tiger) and Eddy (wild boar). The player chooses one from these heroes, and must defeat all opponents, plus the final boss.

Each character has a special animal spirit that helps with the battle (e.g. JoJo's Bizarre Adventure) - and they have a spirit' bar to use these specials. The game uses the joystick plus 4 buttons - for light punch, heavy punch, light kick, and heavy kick.

title: Race Drivin'
description: Race Drivin' is an updated remake of the 1990 coin-op racing game of the same title. It features the original Hard Drivin' course, the courses added in the original Race Drivin', and three brand new courses only found in this new version. The number of available vehicles has also increased from 3 to 8. The game includes both a single-player championship mode and an arcade time attack mode.

title: Rad Mobile
description:
Rad Mobile is a 1st-person racing game where the scenarios are 2D and all of them correspond to 20 zones across the United States. The only available camera is the one inside the car, from where you can see the wheel and indicators (again, in 2D). Also, the game features weather effects, like rain, fog and night, for which you should use either the headlights or the windscreen wiper to succeed in the race.

The Saturn version is similar to the Arcade version except that your rivals are fully polygonal cars. It also adds Full Motion Video sequences, as well as a CD soundtrack.

title: Radiant Silvergun
description:
Radiant Silvergun is a single-player and multiplayer vertical scrolling shoot-'em-up with a time-traveling narrative and a weapon system built entirely around strategic versatility.

The story begins in the distant future, where humanity faces extinction after the awakening of a mysterious alien construct known as the Origin. Pilots of the battleship Radiant Silvergun are transported back in time in a last attempt to alter history. Their mission is to destroy the Origin before it can awaken, battling through waves of enemies across multiple time periods to prevent the annihilation of civilization.

Unlike many shoot-'em-ups that rely on limited power-up items, the game equips the player’s fighter with seven distinct weapons available from the start. These include forward-firing Vulcan shots, homing lasers, wide-spread guns, and more specialized attacks that can be combined to create new firing patterns. A sword weapon is also included, capable of absorbing certain enemy bullets to charge an energy attack. Weapons level up through use, encouraging players to adapt their style and specialize as they progress.

Scoring emphasizes chaining kills of the same enemy color, which multiplies points and unlocks higher weapon levels more quickly. Mastery of the chaining system is essential for high-level play and replay value, creating a strong risk-versus-reward loop. Boss encounters punctuate stages with large-scale mechanical enemies, each requiring memorization of patterns and precision use of the available arsenal.

The game offers multiple modes across its various releases. The original Saturn version included a story-driven arcade mode and a score-focused Saturn mode with persistent weapon leveling. Later ports, such as the Xbox 360, Switch, and PC releases, added visual upgrades, widescreen support, online leaderboards, and optional rebalancing.

title: Ragnagard
description:
Ragnagard is a classic one-on-one beat-'em-up game. The fighters are eight divine beings, gods struggling against one another to acquire power over the heaven.

Controls make use of all of the four buttons of the original Neo Geo arcade stick. Available moves, combat moves and combat actions are explained in a section preliminary to the game and are: punch, kick, dash and quick dash, jump, jump attack, throw, super throw, cushion throw (a throw that does nothing but invert the position of the fighters on the fighting field), counterattack, meter build up (the fighter can not move while charging the power meter: once that is done, a Super God move of gargantuan power can be released). It is possible to dash forward, and perform fight moves while on air for a time longer than normal, on account of the preterhuman nature of the battlers (the game is defined as «aerial battle action game» in the spine of Neo Geo version package). Each divinity wields a personal weapon of medieval fashion, like for instance an imposing sword, a bow, a dreadful halberd. Victory goes to who prevails in 2 out of 3 rounds (the duration of each of which is 60 seconds), and a bonus score related with time and energy left is given to them.

Slight gameplay alterations distinguish the Saturn game version.

title: Rampage World Tour
description:
Rampage World Tour is an updated version of the classic Rampage. Rampage World Tour starts off at Scumlabs International where three lab technicians, George, Lizzy, and Ralph have mutated in an accident involving toxic waste. George has turned into a gigantic ape, Lizzy a gigantic lizard or dinosaur, and Ralph some sort of gigantic wolf. The three destroy the lab they previously worked at and then embark on a path of destruction encompassing the entire globe.

The player chooses one of these three characters and begins destroying buildings, eating civilians, knocking planes out of the sky, and stepping on tanks. The ultimate goal of the game is to rid the world of Scumlabs by traveling to the cities where they are located. Being creatures of such massive size, there are many cities that must be destroyed along the way. Scumlabs and the various militaries make it a priority to destroy you and optionally another player that can play simultaneously.

The graphics are worth noting as they are of a unique, colorful "cartoon" flavor. Gameplay includes players climbing buildings while punching, kicking, and eating their inhabitants to destroy them. Once all the buildings for a particular stage have been destroyed, the stage is clear and players proceed to the next stage. Players can get many different kinds of power-ups that make them more powerful or restore health.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Rampo
description:
Rampo is an interactive movie which uses pre-rendered backdrops and live actors much in the veins of The 7th Guest, without the puzzle-solving part. The game features Edogawa Rampo, a Japanese mystery novel writer, as a protagonist and is based on the movie with the same name which was released a year earlier. In real life, Edogawa Rampo (江戸川 乱歩) is a pseudonym of Hirai Tarou (平井 太郎), a Japanese novelist who wrote mystery fiction in the early-to-middle of 20th century.

Having a writer's block and still under influence that your work has been banned from publishing due to the level of disturbance portrayed, with your editor, Yokomizo Seishi, pressing you to write your next piece, you just can't wrap around your head to make it happen. So you get up from your writing desk and head to do the landlord business and pick up the rent from the occupants. The place is man-exclusive, there is no women allowed, yet you secretly find out someone has been bringing a woman and not just to talk to. What may have started as debauchery will soon turn your life around when it reveals a much bigger mystery than you bargained for.

The game is played in 1st-person perspective where you can turn left or right, or move forward and backward. Moving forward in closed locations will often end up in zooming certain objects and occasionally pick them up if they are of any importance. Picked up objects can be viewed in your inventory and used in certain locations or during dialogues. Movie is not free 3D movement, but instead uses pre-rendered cutscenes for every movement animation. Characters will often cycle through their dialogues unless there is a time where you can inquire about some item from your inventory. Yokomizo Seishi, your editor, will accompany you and will often provide comments when you won't be able to go to certain areas or if you try to do weird things (i.e. try to go outside without a reason, or try to unlock someone else's room without a proper cause). Occasionally your protagonist will also speak, at which moment the picture will be frozen (there is no idle movements of characters or animate objects in the areas when you're talking or just standing still).

title: Rayman
description:
Rayman is a single-player side-scrolling platform game.

Rayman’s world is kept in balance by the Great Protoon, around which the Electoons gather. When Mister Dark steals the Great Protoon and defeats Betilla the Fairy, the Electoons lose their stability, scatter across the world, and are captured by hostile creatures. Rayman, a limbless guardian of the world, sets out to free the imprisoned Electoons, recover the Great Protoon, and restore harmony.

The journey takes place across a series of themed regions connected by a world map. These include forests, musical landscapes, mountains, picture-themed areas, underground caverns, and a final confectionery-themed domain. Each region contains multiple side-scrolling stages with exits, hidden routes, environmental hazards, and enemies suited to its theme. Some stages end normally, while others lead to boss encounters or new sections of the map.

Rayman begins with basic movement abilities such as walking, jumping, crawling, and climbing on vines. Stages require careful timing as the player avoids spikes, pits, water, moving platforms, collapsing surfaces, and enemy patrols. Many areas are built around precise jumps and hazards that force the player to observe movement patterns before advancing. Reaching the exit sign usually completes the current stage section and opens new paths on the map.

As the game progresses, Betilla grants Rayman permanent abilities. These include the telescopic fist, which lets him punch enemies and objects from a distance, the ability to hang from ledges, a grabbing fist used with flying rings, running, and a helicopter technique that slows his descent by spinning his hair. These powers expand the range of movement and make it possible to reach areas that were inaccessible earlier, encouraging the player to revisit previous stages.

Combat is based mainly on Rayman’s fist attack. The punch can be charged for greater distance, and certain power-ups strengthen it or restore Rayman’s energy. Rayman loses energy when hit by enemies or hazards, and losing all energy costs a life. Extra lives, health pickups, and other bonuses can be found throughout the stages. The Photographer appears at certain points and serves as a checkpoint, allowing the player to resume from that location after losing a life.

Freeing Electoons is a major part of progression. Each level has a medallion with spaces representing hidden Electoon cages, and breaking a cage fills one of those spaces. Many cages are placed off the main route, behind hazards, or in locations that require abilities obtained later. Finding all of the Electoon cages in the first five worlds is required to open the final area, making exploration and backtracking part of the main structure rather than purely optional completion.

The game also includes temporary powers and special stage mechanics. Certain characters grant abilities used only in specific areas, such as growing plants from magic seeds, flying freely with a super helicopter power, using a firefly to illuminate dark caves, or shrinking to pass through narrow spaces. Tings function as collectible items and can be spent to enter bonus stages run by the Magician, where successful play can reward the player with extra lives.

title: RayStorm
description:
RayStorm is a shoot'em-up game created for the arcades, later ported to the Playstation and Saturn home consoles. Although there is no story connection, it is often thought of as the spiritual successor to Galactic Attack, which had similar gameplay.

You have 2 weapons at you disposal, a vulcan gun and a lock-on missile attack. You can also do 2 special attacks by using the lock-on system in a special way. The graphics are all in 3D, but the gameplay mechanics are in 2D. There are 7 stages, each ending with a giant end boss.

title: Re-Loaded
description:
This is the sequel to 1995's Loaded, with an improved graphics engine, and just as much violence and blood. Re-Loaded puts you in the shoes of a number of characters, such as Sister Magpie or Butch. Each character is weird, deformed, and generally strange.

It is a mission based game, where you must complete various objectives to successfully win in each of the 12 worlds. Throughout each mission, you must kill lots of people, with a variety of weapons such as plasma cannons, lasers and ultra bombs.

title: Real Bout Fatal Fury
aka_titles: ACA NeoGeo: Real Bout Fatal Fury
AkeAka NeoGeo: Real Bout Garō Densetsu
description: The fourth title of fighting Fatal Fury series. Now, you can destroy fight scene objects and the "Fatal Fury 2" fighters are back forming this list: Terry Bogard, Andy Bogard, Joe Higashi, Franco Bash, Mai Shiranui, Bob Wilson, Geese Howard, Billy Kane, Hon-Fu, Ryuji Yamazaki, Sokaku Mochizuki, Blue Mary, Kim Kaphwan, Jin Chonrei, Jin Chonshu and Duck King.

title: Real Bout Fatal Fury Best Collection
aka_titles: Real Bout Garō Densetsu Best Collection
description: This is a compilation that includes the award winning arcade versions of the fighting games Real Bout Fatal Fury and Real Bout Fatal Fury Special for Sega Saturn.

title: Real Bout Fatal Fury Special
aka_titles: ACA NeoGeo: Real Bout Fatal Fury Special
AkeAka NeoGeo: Real Bout Garō Densetsu Special
Nettō Real Bout Garō Densetsu Special
description: It was the sequel of Real Bout Fatal Fury, with which sixth delivery of the series was arrived at his, in this we had 20 characters (Terry Bogard, Andy Bogard, Joe Higashi, Mai Shiranui, Tung Fu Rue, Cheng Chinzan, Laurence Blood, Wolfgang Krauser, Duck King, Kim Kaphwan, Blue Mary, Hon-Fu, Bob Wilson, Mochizuki Sokaku, Franco Bash, Ryuji Yamazaki, Jin Chonshu, Jin Chonrei, Billy Kane and Geese Howard) and their aspects are 100% remodeled. Also, the game maintains the capacity to destroy some things of the fight zone.

title: Real Bout Garō Densetsu Special (Okaidoku Set)
description: This release of Real Bout Garō Densetsu Special includes the game along with a Sega Saturn 1MB RAM Expansion Cartridge.

title: Real Bout Garou Densetsu
description: Real Bout changes the play controls from the previous Fatal Fury games, reducing the number of attack buttons from four to three: a standard Punch and Kick button, a "Strong Attack" button which can be either a stronger punch or kick attack, depending on the character. The game retains the three-plane "oversway" system from Fatal Fury 3, which features a main lane for fighting, with foreground and background planes used to avoid attacks or leap towards the opponent. A dedicated button is now used to make an "oversway" (or change plane) towards the background or foreground. Real Bout introduces a Power Gauge, which fills up as the player performs normal or special techniques against their opponent or defend themselves, similar to many super move gauges featured in other fighting games. The Power Gauge allows players to perform one of three types of Special Techniques, depending of the level of the Power Gauge. Real Bout also introduces stages with ring-outs, a gameplay feature previously introduced in 3D fighting games such as Virtua Fighter. If the player performs certain attacks on their opponent while next to the boundaries, the character will eventually destroy the barrier keeping the opponent in the ring and be able to knock them out of the stage for an easy win.

title: Real Bout Garou Densetsu Special
description: The supreme trial of strength awaits! 19 of Fatal Fury's hottest heroes collide! One year since the fearsome conclusion to "Real Bout", the hungry wolves ready themselves for a new battle, "Real Bout Special" - the paramount pugilistic proving ground! The game retains the cast of the original Real Bout, with the addition of Tung Fu Rue, Cheng Sinzan, Laurence Blood and Wolfgang Krauser from Fatal Fury Special, with Krauser serving as the new final boss. Geese Howard, who was killed off in the end of the original Real Bout, appears in this game as a hidden final boss in a special "Nightmare Match" and as an unlockable playable character in the home versions. The game also features hidden "extra" versions of Tung Fu Rue, Billy Kane, Blue Mary, and Andy Bogard, for a total of 23 (24 if counting Geese) characters.

title: Real Mahjong Adventure: Umi e Summer Waltz
description: This spin-off title in the Super Real Mahjong series takes a much different approach. It's a visual novel. You can pursue a relationship with several girls from Super Real Mahjong PV, P VI, and P7. There is a lot of talking, and you often have to make choices of what to say or do. An overworld map system is utilized, as the girls are in different locations.

title: Real Mahjong Adventure: Umi e Summer Waltz (P's Club Genteiban)
description: This limited-edition release of Real Mahjong Adventure: Umi e Summer Waltz was only sold via Seta's Super Real Mahjong fan club and includes the game along with a CD soundtrack. The game disc also has full-color artwork unique to this release.

title: Real Sound: Kaze no Regret
description:
Mizu Sakura is a Tokyo elementary student who is transferred to a new school. There, she falls in love with a boy named Hiroshi Nonoichi. The two decide to elope together, fearing that nobody will accept their relationship at such a young age. However, Mizu never shows up for the meeting; a while later Hiroshi learns that she has been transferred to another school.

Several years have passed. Mizu is looking for a job and Hiroshi attends college. It looks like both have moved on with their lives. But their past catches up with them when they learn about a mysterious disappearance in the subway system.

Real Sound: Kaze no Regret is an audio game: it has no graphics or other visuals of any kind. Gameplay-wise, it is identical to visual novels, with written text and images being replaced by sound. The player listens to the voice-acted story, which is occasionally interrupted by a chime, prompting the player to make a decision and branch the plot. The Dreamcast port adds some minimal visual elements: a title screen and a "Visual Mode" consisting of static backgrounds.

title: Refrain Love: Anata ni Aitai
description:
Refrain Love is a dating simulation adventure game and a story of seven men and women, including the player. The protagonist is a male college student (character's name is not pre-defined, but entered by the player) who made a vow with couple of his friends, Tetsuya Yamo, Kousuke Satou, and Taizou Sakaki, to find a woman by next Christmas. One day, you meet a girl that looks like a dead ringer of the mysterious woman that's been plaguing your dreams recently. Chance, fate, or just dumb luck, it makes you feel like you just might have a chance to make your wish come true.

The game's story follows the events in the year and ends on the Christmas Eve, hopefully with the girl of your dreams right by your side. Two main gameplay modes in the game are simulation and adventure mode. Adventure mode is similar to visual novels but with much more choices to select during conversations with your buddies or the girl you're on a date with. Additionally, you can use the city map to visit various different locations. The simulation mode consists of part-time job where you get to earn some money, spending time alone with a hobby of your choice, playing with your friends, or taking a girl to a date. The obvious girl of your choice features Tomomi Sakura, the girl from your campus, Ran Yuuki, your childhood friend, and Shouko Takamiya, a working woman.

title: Resident Evil
description:
A team of S.T.A.R.S (Special Tactics And Rescue Squad) members are called to investigate a series of murders near Raccoon City. While searching the woods near the city, the team is attacked by bloodthirsty dogs and they have to retreat to a nearby mansion.

The player chooses between Jill Valentine or Chris Redfield and starts to explore the mansion. It soon becomes very clear that it isn't just any mansion, but a hellish place where the undead walk the corridors, and other horrors are lurking in the darkness, waiting to eat some heads. While solving puzzles, collecting keys, and shooting monsters, the player has to unravel the mystery behind this mansion and, if possible, get out alive.

Exclusive to the SEGA Saturn version is a Battle Mode bonus mode, where, with limited ammo and under the threat of limited time, the player must survive a series of rooms filled with monsters.

title: Return Fire
description:
Return Fire is a single-player and two-player vehicular action strategy game. It is the spiritual successor to Fire Power.

The game is built around a military capture-the-flag contest between opposing bases. The player commands a small motor pool and must locate the enemy flag, take it from the opposing bunker, and return it to the player’s own base. The battlefield is filled with roads, bridges, water, hills, buildings, gun emplacements, mines, and enemy vehicles, making each mission a combination of scouting, attack, defense, and route planning.

There is no story campaign centered on named characters. Instead, each map presents a tactical objective: use the available vehicles to break through the enemy’s defenses and either capture the flag or destroy the opposing base. The player may switch vehicles at the home base, deciding which machine is best suited to the current task. Winning depends on understanding each vehicle’s strengths and using them together rather than treating them as interchangeable.

The four vehicles are the jeep, tank, helicopter, and Armoured Support Vehicle. The jeep is fast and lightly armored, and it is the only vehicle that can pick up and carry the enemy flag. The tank is slower but durable, with a rotating cannon suited to direct attacks on defenses and enemy vehicles. The helicopter can fly over terrain and water, making it useful for scouting, striking isolated targets, and bypassing ground obstacles. The Armoured Support Vehicle is slower and heavier, but it can deliver powerful long-range attacks and provide support against fortified areas.

Each vehicle has limited fuel, ammunition, and durability. Fuel and ammunition can be replenished at appropriate depots, while damage can force the player to abandon a vehicle or return for another attempt. Running out of fuel can leave a vehicle stranded, and losing the wrong vehicle at the wrong time can make the flag difficult or impossible to recover without changing strategy. Because resources are limited, the player must decide when to attack, when to retreat, and when to prepare the battlefield for the jeep’s flag run.

Combat takes place from an overhead view. The player drives or flies one vehicle at a time, firing weapons at enemy turrets, vehicles, bunkers, bridges, buildings, and other targets. Destroying defenses can open safer routes, while careless destruction may remove useful cover or make the return trip more dangerous. The helicopter and support vehicle are especially useful for softening enemy positions before the jeep attempts to enter the base and escape with the flag.

Maps vary in terrain layout, defensive placement, and distance between bases. Some emphasize direct assault, while others require scouting, bridge destruction, water crossings, mine avoidance, or careful planning around narrow routes. The player can win by bringing the enemy flag home, which is the main objective, or by destroying the enemy base outright. The alternate victory condition gives each battle room for different approaches, from fast raids to prolonged demolition.

The game supports two-player competitive play, with each player controlling a base and vehicle set while trying to capture the other’s flag. In multiplayer, offense and defense occur at the same time, and players must decide whether to protect their own bunker, attack the enemy base, intercept a flag carrier, or destroy key vehicles and routes. This makes the same vehicle roles more dynamic than in single-player, since both sides can adapt to one another’s tactics.

title: Return to Zork
aka_titles: Return to Zork: An Epic Adventure in the Great Underground Empire
Return to Zork: Ein episches Abenteuer im großen Reich der Unterwell
Return to Zork: Une aventure héroïque dans le Grand Empire Souterrain
description:
You are standing behind the white house. There is something in the mailbox. A video message from a wizard informing you that you are the sweepstakes winner to the Valley of the Sparrows... right now, by magic flight. Upon arriving at this mysterious place however, not everything is as it should be. There's nobody to meet you and those who you do come across don't seem to have any knowledge about a sweepstakes. It looks like this is a private vacation and you'll need to find your own way through this land.

Return to Zork is a first-person adventure game using live actors and video sequences. The game is similar to Myst in interface; the player is also able to rotate the viewpoint to discover new areas and uncover items that can be used or picked up. Various characters will be met along the way and spoken to via a system of dialog choices. The game allows the player to experiment with items in various ways, including discharging them; however, this often leads to "dead ends", rendering it impossible to complete the game.

title: Reverthion
description: Eight warriors seek "Sentien", to obtain the ultimate power of creation and the title of "Reverthion". Reverthion is a third-person arena-based action game that pits two mechanized creatures against one another. It plays very similarly to Sega's contemporary hit Virtual On, and includes eight playable characters each with their own unique moveset and abilities. There is a single-player campaign with unique endings for each character, as well as a 2-player split screen versus mode; the Saturn version, Hyper Reverthion, adds system link support for two-player matches between two consoles.

title: Revolution X
aka_titles: Revolution X: Music is the Weapon
Revolution X: Music Is the Weapon
description:
Revolution X is about the ol' Rock & Roll.

There is an evil nation putting the youth down and banning our beloved rock music. Who you gonna call? Aerosmith! With the help of Aerosmith, the player must shoot his/her way through enemy infested levels, (light) guns blazing, collecting power-ups and releasing hostages.

Almost all of the graphics are digitized and Aerosmith themselves are too! There are also lots of fmv videos.

title: Riglord Saga 2
description:
The sequel to Blazing Heroes, originally known as Riglord Saga. You play the role of Mieu, the princess of Dragoon Kingdom. One day the castle is attacked by two men from a mysterious organization called the Seven Wisemen. The princess and her best friend have no choice but to escape, but it seems that they are the ones their enemies are looking for!

The game utilizes the same gameplay system as the predecessor. You form a large party with which you participate in long, strategic turn-based battles. You move your characters on the battle field, attacking enemies or casting magical spells. The strength of your attacks depend on the amount of movements you have made before.

title: Rise 2: Resurrection
description: In the sequel new troubles in ElectroCorp have begun. As we remember, this corporation made robots for civilian jobs, but one Supervisor decided to make robot-killers. Human brains were implanted on some of them. But this time, one hacker has infected the ElectroCorp's network with a virus, so Supervisor lost control over robots and they began to kill each other. You are one of them.

title: Riven: The Sequel to Myst
description:
After the Stranger has rescued Atrus, the master of "linking books", from the imprisonment caused by his sons, a new task awaits the hero. Atrus's wife, Catherine, has been taken by Gehn, his own father. Gehn has appointed himself as the one to rule the Age of Riven, and has driven his world to collapse. Now he holds Catherine hostage on Riven, hoping that his son will restore the book link to the Age and free him from there. The Stranger is requested by Atrus to travel to Riven and find a way to rescue Catherine.

Riven is a sequel to Myst, and is very similar to its predecessor in gameplay style, controls, and visual presentation. The game world is presented as a series of computer-generated still screens; the player explores it in a point-and-click fashion.
