Blast your way through over 100+ levels, shooting the creatures that come out from the other side of the web to drag you in. Collect power-ups (jump, AI robots and more) to trippy graphics and colorful explosions as a thumping techno-house soundtrack blasts in the background.

Collect enough bonuses, and be subjected to two different types of bonus rounds as you navigate through rings, or try to ride a spiral tube.

Also included in the gameplay is an intense two-player mode to team up with or go head to head against another player, or even play a version of the original arcade game. There are four modes of gameplay in all: Traditional Tempest, Tempest Duel, Tempest Plus and Tempest 2000.

Face the web....

title: Ten Pin Alley
description:
In this bowling game, you must choose from one of eight very different characters. Choose power and accuracy from a meter that is very similar to the Links golf games. Let go and watch the action.

The game consists of single game, league and tournament (amateur and pro) modes. The selected player may be edited by changing their shirt, hair, pants and skin color and is distinguished by four factors: power, release, spin and hand usage. Each strike consists of choosing the lane arrow, setting the bowler position and operating the bowling meter. Operating the bowling meter involves specifying spin velocity, power of the bowl and release point. The game shows the release animation, ball path and the moment of impact with the pins. After two strikes, the next player takes his position. The results are presented in the table after every completed round.

The Windows version of the game allows to play up to 10 human or computer players on a single computer (hot seat mode) or via internet connection.

title: Tenant Wars
description:
Tenant Wars is a board game for the Sega Saturn. Though the Saturn version was not released outside of Japan, the PlayStation port saw a limited release in North America as Board Game: Top Shop in 2001. 

The gameplay of Tenant Wars mimics that of Monopoly, but expands on the property management aspect of that game. As in Monopoly, players move across a game board in accordance to the number they roll on a die, purchase unowned properties when they land on such and earn money when they reach the bank. Rolling an "E" triggers a random event, while landing on an elevator space can affect the direction in which the player moves.

In addition to multitap support, Top Shop features eight maps, eleven characters, and forty-four shops. It can be played in either story or free play mode.

title: Tenchi Muyō! Mimiri Onsen: Yukemuri no Tabi
description:
Tenchi and the many beautiful ladies who live with him are going on vacation! On Ryoko's insistence, the group is off to a hot springs resort... but not just any hot springs, they're traveling to an entire hot springs planet! However, once they get there, it turns out Ryoko doesn't actually know where the resort is. Add in a mysterious young girl named Mimiri, and it's going to be an adventure for Tenchi and his friends just trying to have a relaxing vacation.

Tenchi Muyō! Mimiri Onsen: Yukemuri no Tabi is a Japanese-style adventure game based on the Tenchi Muyo anime series. The game is fully-voiced, not including even a dialogue display or subtitles, and progresses as is standard for Japanese adventure games. In each scene, the player can inspect various parts of the scene, move between locations, and talk to each of Tenchi's companions, with the story generally progressing after all relevant options have been exhausted. There are ten different endings depending on the player's choices and who they decide to talk to.

title: Tenchi Muyō! Rensa Hitsuyō
description:
Tenchi and his friends are having a karaoke party! But Ryoko is hogging the mic and not giving anyone else a turn, and Ayeka is fed up with her hogging the spotlight. Washu suggests a game to decide who gets to sing next, but it's not nearly as simple as a game of janken...

Tenchi Muyō! Rensa Hitsuyō is a competitive falling-block puzzle game based on the Tenchi Muyo! anime series, similar to the popular Puyo Puyo series. Pairs of blocks in various colors fall into the playfield, and the player must arrange them; if three or more of the same color are matched together, they will vanish from the playfield and allow blocks above them to fall into their place and potentially trigger combo chains. Combo chains will cause the water level in the opponent's playfield to rise; blocks cannot be dropped below the water line, and if either the blocks or the water reach the top of the playfield that player loses the match. Several other special blocks also appear on occasion: Heart blocks will lower the water level when matched, Anchor blocks will push any blocks below them down into the water, and Ryo-oki blocks will trigger the selected character's special move when matched.

The game includes a single-player story mode, a two-player battle mode, and a free battle mode against the CPU, as well as a tutorial that explains the game rules. There are six playable characters, all of them the girls from the show; Tenchi himself is not playable.

title: Tenchi Muyō! Ryō-ōki: Gokuraku CD-ROM for Sega Saturn
description: Tenchi Muyō!: Ryō-ōki - Gokuraku CD-ROM for Sega Saturn is a fan disk for the Tenchi Muyo! franchise, based on a series of earlier PC releases, which contains a variety of promotional illustrations, video and voice clips from the show, and information about other Tenchi Muyo-related releases and merchandise. There is also a quiz mode which tests the player's knowledge of the series, including video and sound clip questions.

title: Tenchi Muyō! Tōkō Muyō: Aniraji Collection
description:
Tenchi Muyō! Tōkō Muyō (天地無用! 登校無用) is an anime-like visual novel with constant video clips and CG events featuring full voice-acting for dialogues and Tenchi's thoughts without text-only descriptions whatsoever. The game uses autoplay feature and doesn't wait for you to press button to progress the dialogues, although they can be skipped. At certain moments player's actions let you affect the course of dialogues, but it does not affect an overall ending. The story centers on school love of Tenchi Masaki (柾木 天地) filled with love troubles. Key heroines from anime series, namely Ryoko (魎呼), Aeka (阿重霞) and Sasami (砂沙美) are also present in the story.

Sega Saturn release came out several months after the original PlayStation release, but this package includes:

  • Tenchi Muyō! Tōkō Muyō game
  • Bonus CD with opening theme and three audio drama tracks
  • Bonus CD booklet features a short 4 page comic

title: Tenchi o Kurau II: Sekiheki no Tatakai
aka_titles: The Devouring of Heaven and Earth II: Battle of Red Cliffs
Tenchi o Kurau 2: Sekiheki no Tatakai
Tenchi wo Kurau II: Sekiheki no Tatakai
description:
Tenchi o Kurau II: Sekiheki no Tatakai is a 2D side-scrolling beat 'em-up and sequel to Tenchi o Kurau, taking place in ancient China. Akkila-orkhan the dark lord of Shang-Lo has decided to conquer the neighboring countries. The wise Kuan-Ti has summoned the five greatest warriors of the lands to stop this from happening.

As you make progress you encounter numerous different enemies including spearman, archers, mace wielding soldiers, hand to hand fighters and bosses. Various weapons dropped by enemies can be picked up and used. Along the way health can be replenished by consuming food as well as mounting a horse. The game can be played solo or with up to two friends in the arcade version. The Saturn and PlayStation version allow two players to play.

Both games are based on the Tenchi o Kurau manga series which ran for a brief period between 1983 and 1984.

title: Tenga Seiha
description: Tenga Seiha is a historical simulation game set in the Warring States period of Japanese history, which chronicles the life and rise to power of shogun Ieyasu Tokugawa. The game is divided into two main sections: adventure segments and battle segments. In the adventure segments, the player can speak with advisors and villagers to gather information. The battle segments play out in real-time with the player giving basic orders to units, such as to move to a specific location or to launch an attack. The game includes recreations of 26 real-life battles, and numerous story branch points where the scenario can diverge significantly from historical fact.

title: Tengai Makyō: Daiyon no Mokushiroku - The Apocalypse IV
aka_titles: Far East of Eden: The Apocalypse
天外魔境 第四の黙示録
Tengai Makyou: Daishi no Mokushiroku: The Apocalypse IV
Tengai Makyou: Daiyon no Mokushiroku: The Apocalypse IV
description:
New Orleans, Louisiana, 1893. A boy named Rizing is exploring the surroundings of his hometown together with a couple of friends. They discover a mysterious old house, go inside, and discover what seems to be a mummy in a coffin. They don't realize that at this moment they unleashed a powerful demon into the world, and that this demon has already possessed the soul of one of the boys...

The Apocalypse IV is the first Tengai Makyō game that is set outside of the Japan-like country Jipang. Much like Jipang of earlier games, United States of the late 19th century is not in a historically correct environment in this game, but an alternate world populated by demons, Biblical figures, and deliberate clichés (cardboard Native Americans, pop culture references, etc).

The gameplay largely follows the general Japanese RPG template and Tengai Makyō gameplay style in particular. As in the previous games, magic spells have to be sought out and acquired rather than learned or bought. A notable change is the absence of random enemies - all the enemies are visibly wandering on the world map or in the dungeons. Other gameplay additions include special attacks that can also performed by several members of the party as a combo, and obtaining money by selling trophies received in battles.

title: Tennis Arena
description:
Tennis Arena is a comedic, arcade take on tennis. Featuring a total of 10 selectable characters (five male and five female), the game allows for both singles and doubles matches, as well as tournament play and a world tour mode.

Some players have unconventional outfits, such as overweight William Lee Chan, who plays barechested with baggy pants and a large gold necklace. The game also features wacky sound effects and special shots, which can be deployed after racking up six straight returns.

Available court options include a New York City park, a traditional professional stadium, the Sahara Desert, the Roman Coliseum, and an ocean cruise liner.

title: Terra Cresta 3D
description: This 3D sequel to Terra Cresta takes a simple, cut-down approach to shooting. Players blast off into space to take out waves of enemy spacecraft through several different levels. Most of the game is presented from an overhead view with a slightly tilted camera, giving the player a slightly longer view of the stage. A few stages switch the camera up to a chase camera, which is set behind the player's craft as they shoot at enemies as they fly towards the camera instead. There are three different craft, but unlike in most shooters players don't choose one at the beginning; instead, players can switch forms at any time to respond to the current situation. Unlike in most arcade-style shooters, there's no score whatsoever: the player's goal is simply to survive to the end of the game, not to reach any kind of high score.

title: Terra Phantastica
description:
In the Selecion Empire, the Grand Duchy of Mais is led by Alexis I. One day, his young son Alexis II visits an ancient temple, and is fascinated by a beautiful stone statue within. This statue is said to be of the goddess that protects Mais, but no records of her exist and she doesn't even have a name; the young Alexis II decides to give her a name himself. Not long after, the monster nation of Beaufon advances eastward toward Mais, and in the battle Alexis I loses his life. However, as Zaitan, one of the the Demon Generals of Beaufon, approaches the capital and all seems lost, a mysterious beautiful woman appears and defeats him with an inhuman strength. However, she has no memory of her past; she joins Alexis and Mais to fight against Beaufon and to find the meaning of her own existence, and so begins a fight for the fate of the world.

Terra Phantastica is a turn-based tactical strategy RPG in the vein of Tactics Ogre. The main game consists of battle sequences in which the player and the opposing forces commands numerous units around a grid-based map, moving and attacking enemies. Each unit consists of a leader and multiple soldiers, which can be arranged in various formations; soldiers can be lost as a unit is attacked, reducing its effectiveness and eventually eliminating that unit from the battle. Combat engagements between units can take multiple turns, with attacks, retreats, formation changes and other commands available on each turn turns. Between battles the player can consult with various other characters as well as arrange, equip, and train their units. Multiple endings are possible depending on the player's actions and the main character's relationship with Alexis II.

title: Tetris Plus
description: This is yet another updated version of Tetris which was released for PlayStation, Saturn, and Game Boy. This version features Classic mode, Puzzle mode, Versus mode, and Edit mode. In Puzzle mode, you must save the professor who climbs his way to the top. In order to do that, you must clear the blocks away and bring him to the bottom. Versus mode brings you head to head with another player. Edit mode allows you to create and save your own custom levels.

title: Tetris S
description:
Tetris S is the second of two Tetris games released for the Sega Saturn in 1996. Unlike the arcade port Tetris Plus which was released a few months earlier, it was specifically made for the console. This version includes a single player mode as well as multiplayer against an AI or between two human players.

The single player mode works like traditional Tetris and uses the same rotation rules as Sega's earlier arcade game conversions. Like always the player guides blocks down a well with the aim of creating lines at the bottom. These lines are then removed and the player earns points. The game ends when the blocks reach the top of the well, but in this version there is a continue option allowing the player to keep playing at the current level. The multiplayer works the same way but with one difference: if more than one line is removed the opponent's next few blocks will fall at a greater pace. The number of lines removed affects how many blocks will be sped up. A multiplayer game is played over a set number of matches and the aim is simply to stay alive longer than the opponent.

title: Texthoth Ludo: Arcana Senki
description:
Ages ago, there were 22 guardian deities who watched over the four races: humans, dwarves, elves, and pixies. However, conflict led to war, and war led the supreme deity "World" to seal itself and the 21 other deities away. The people of the world however discovered the power of "Arcana", which allowed them to again reach the power of the deities, and when a human Arcana user tried to revive World, the power of Arcana was released all at once. Monsters were created from this energy, and the world once again entered an age of darkness. Will this land ever know peace again?

Texthoth Ludo: Arcana Senki is a multiplayer board game based on tarot cards. Players use cards from their hand to move forward on the board and to perform other actions depending on the type of space occupied; cards can summon or upgrade creatures to fight for the player, or be fused together to create more powerful cards. If two players or creatures occupy the same space, they can choose to battle; a defeated summon will return to their owner's deck, while a defeated player will be sent back to the start of the board. Up to four players compete on a board, and the goal is simply to be the first player to reach the goal space with their summoner.

The game includes a story mode with 22 maps, and depending on the player's choices the story may branch and lead to several different paths toward the ending. There is also a versus mode for up to four players. A password system lets players bring their character and deck to a friend's game, even between platforms. The original Sega Saturn release included a set of 22 tarot cards as a bonus; the later PlayStation port adds a more comprehensive tutorial mode to aid new players.

title: The Book of Lulu
aka_titles: LULU: Un Conte Interactif de Romain Victor-Pujebet
description: The Book of Lulu is an interactive multimedia book by Romain Victor-Pujebet where player can flip the pages to read through and click on various images in the book. Certain images in the book allow for slide changes or result in a small video animation, while others open in full screen mode with ability to interact with them by clicking on a certain area. Interactive images allow changes such as changing the sky, weather, season, colors and mode, while interactive videos let you interact with objects and characters which result in a short FMV sequence.

title: The Conveni 2
aka_titles: The Conveni 2: Zenkoku Chain Tenkai da!

title: The Conveni 2: Zenkoku Chain Tenkai da!
description: In The Conveni 2, you run convenience stores as you try to expand your chain nationwide. As the owner, try to boost sales and increase your number of stores to achieve the goals on each map. The game's graphics have been completely retooled and more maps have been added! A high-speed mode has also been added! Even playability has been improved! This is a complete convenience simulation in which you can send spies to rival stores to collect information and even buy out your competitors! Go for it! Expand till you are a nationwide chain!

title: The Conveni: Ano Machi wo Dokusen Seyo
aka_titles: The Conveni: Ano Machi o Dokusen Seyo
description:
Become the owner of a convenience store franchise, and experience the fun of arranging products and customizing your store to meet land features and seasons!

Can you bring in lots of customers? Can you succeed in opening up ten stores?
Can you serve a million customers? ...A store owner faces so many challenges!

Experience the first installment of the hit convenience store management simulation!

title: The Conveni!
aka_titles: The Conveni: Ano Machi o Dokusen Seyo

title: The Crow: City of Angels
description:
The Crow: City of Angels is a video game adaption of the 1996 film of the same name.

Brought back from the dead by the mysterious crow, Ashe will stop at nothing to avenge his and his son's execution at the hands of the minions of Judah, the city’s crime lord. One by one they will face the crow!

The Crow: COA is a 3D fighting game in which the player wanders from screen to screen, fighting everybody they come across with a wide variety of kicks and punches that vary based on your proximity to your foe. There is also a large range of weapons including pistols, shotgun's, knives, pool cues, pipes and steel drums.

title: The Horde
description:
The Horde is a single-player action strategy game. The player controls Chauncey, a serving lad who saves King Winthrop the Good from choking during a royal meal. As a reward, the king gives Chauncey the magical sword Grimthwacker and grants him land in the kingdom of Franzpowanki. Chauncey’s new responsibility is to make the settlement prosper while defending it from the Horde, a race of hungry creatures known as Hordlings.

The Hordlings attack each season and try to eat or destroy the village’s people, crops, cows, and other resources. Chauncey must protect the settlement well enough to earn money, keep the king’s favor, and advance to more difficult regions of the kingdom. His success also draws the attention of Kronus Maelor, the High Chancellor, who tries to hinder Chauncey through taxes, politics, and other schemes.

Each season is divided into two main phases. During the build phase, the player prepares the village before the attack begins. The player can place defenses, alter terrain, cut trees, dig or fill holes, and plan how the village should survive the next wave. Buildings, crops, cows, roads, and villagers develop between seasons, so preparation focuses on shaping the battlefield and protecting the settlement’s most important assets.

The action phase begins when Hordlings enter the map. The player directly controls Chauncey from an overhead view, moving around the village and striking enemies with Grimthwacker. Different types of Hordlings behave in different ways, with some rushing toward villagers, some targeting crops or cows, and others creating additional hazards. The player must decide which threats to stop first, since enemies may attack several parts of the settlement at once.

Economy and defense are linked. Surviving crops and cows produce income, while lost villagers and destroyed resources reduce the settlement’s success. Hordlings may also drop money when defeated. Gold can be spent between seasons on improvements and special items, but taxes and poor performance can reduce what the player has available. A village that survives the attack but loses too many resources may still struggle to grow.

Chauncey can acquire magical items and other tools that help against the Horde. These may include effects that attack enemies, protect parts of the village, or change how Chauncey handles emergencies. Magic is powered through Chauncey’s ATM card, the Automated Transfer of Mana, which converts gold into usable magical energy. This means magical help is useful but also tied to the player’s finances.

Progression is organized by years and regions. After surviving enough seasons in one area, Chauncey may be sent to another part of the kingdom, where new terrain, resources, Hordling types, and defensive problems appear. The changing regions require the player to adapt village planning and combat priorities rather than relying on the same layout every time.

The game uses live-action video scenes for its comic story sequences, including messages from King Winthrop, Kronus Maelor, and the Franzpowanki News Network. These scenes frame the campaign and report on Chauncey’s progress, while the main gameplay remains focused on alternating construction, resource protection, and real-time combat.

title: The House of the Dead
description:
The House of the Dead is a rail shooter. Go through the four chapters with branching paths and kill all the zombies, avoid killing the humans, and rescue the girl. Shooting various special targets along the way or in a certain time period give the player temporary health and weapon upgrades.

The Saturn version of the game contains two extra modes called Saturn Mode and Boss Mode. Saturn mode plays like the arcade game, but offers the player different characters to choose from. Character selection matters since they each have varying attributes such as their reload time and how much damage they can take before dying. The Boss Mode allows the player to fight one boss of their choosing or all of the game's four boss monsters consecutively.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: The Incredible Hulk: The Pantheon Saga
aka_titles: O Incrível Hulk: A Saga do Panteão
description:
The Incredible Hulk is an isometric 3D action game.

The popular Marvel comic book hero The Hulk returns to the PC, Playstation and Saturn systems to battle tons of lowly enemies and the occasional monstrous super-villain. When the lawful Pantheon society of superheroes kidnaps the green giant, he joins forces with his abductors and smashes through 13+2 isometric 3D levels (in a look reminiscent of the Loaded series of games).

True to the comic books, the Hulk relies on no other weapons than his massive muscles to punch, kick and crush his enemies. When he has accumulated enough gamma energy, he may use powerful special moves like a Vortex Spin or the Floor Hammer. Rare bonus items also allow the Hulk to summon one of the four Pantheon team members Atalanta, Ulysses, Ajax and Hector to assist in the thick of battle.

Most levels include at least one arch-enemy, such as Piecemeal, Trauma & Lazarus or the U-Foes. Luckily, the Hulk’s regenerative powers allow him to regain health slowly. Little seems to be left of the Hulk’s legendary leaping capacity, however, so the green meat ball is forced to hop from platform to platform every now and then.

You can find more information on The Incredible Hulk comic books in the trivia and links sections.

title: The King of Fighters '95
description:
The first sequel in the King of Fighters series picks up a year after the end of the first tournament. Once again, fighters from all over the world receive a mysterious invitation to a team-based fighting tournament. And just like last year, it appears that the notorious criminal Rugal Bernstein is behind it, apparently returning from the dead to raise havok once again...

The King of Fighters '95 introduces Kyo Kusanagi's rival Iori Yagami, and firmly places Kyo as the main character for the rest of the series. The gameplay of The King of Fighters '95 is essentially unchanged from the previous title, though it does introduce the "team edit" concept which would remain as a standard feature of the series. Using the "team edit" feature, it is possible to create a totally customized team using any of the available fighters, or use one of the default teams if you wish.

title: The King of Fighters '96
aka_titles: The King of Fighters: Heat of Battle
description:
"Violent fighting to come again!"

SNK's flagship series returns for another year. Many of the changes in this year's KOF release come in the form of improved graphics, sound effects, music and totally redone character sprites. The gameplay of the system has been altered with the addition of "Rush" multi-hit combos and new moves for practically every character. The storyline of the series receives heavy focus in this release with the Orochi Saga swinging into high-gear.

The King of Fighters '96 has 27 regular characters plus 2 boss characters (who can be unlocked with the use of a code). Newcomers to the tournament include Mr. Big from the Art of Fighting series, the bosses from Fatal Fury (Wolfgang Krauser and Geese Howard), and completely original characters like Leona Heidern, Mature and Vice. Other features carried over from the previous year include the ability to choose between the default "Team Fighting" mode or the traditional "Single Fighter" style of gameplay, plus the "Versus" and "Survival" gameplay modes.

title: The King of Fighters '96 (Okaidoku Set)
description: This release of The King of Fighters '96 includes the game along with a Sega Saturn 1MB RAM Expansion Cartridge.

title: The King of Fighters '96 + '95 (Gentei KOF Double Pack)
description:
This double-pack bundles together two games from the King of Fighters series:

  • The King of Fighters '95
  • The King of Fighters '96

Also included is a Sega Saturn 1MB RAM Expansion Cartridge.

title: The King of Fighters '97
description:
Another year, another KOF. Additions this year come in the form of slightly improved graphics and sounds, new moves and a new game mode. Gameplay is much more plot-driven, as you have middle-bosses that can change depending on what team you select. In addition, there are several special endings which are only shown when certain "Edit Team" combinations are selected.

As of The King of Fighters '97, you can play in either the Extra or Advanced game modes. Extra Mode is the typical AOF/KOF scheme, in which your power gauge fills up as you defend yourself or charge yourself up. The new Advanced Mode, on the other hand, only allows you to charge your gauge as you perform special moves and attacks, similar to the Street Fighter series. Extra allows one to sidestep attacks while Advanced allows the character to roll past and dodge attacks; Advanced also allow a character to perform a potent "Super Desperation Move" (or SDM) at any time provided the character has at least two full bars of charged energy stored. In contrast, SDMs can only be performed in Extra when a character has less than a quarter of their health left.

New characters include the New Face Team, the Fatal Fury Outlaw Team (featuring the KOF debut of "Blue" Mary Ryan and Ryuji Yamazaki, and the return of Billy Kane), and Kyo's pupil Shingo Yabuki. In total, The King of Fighters '97 sports 29 separate characters (without counting the six Orochi-related boss characters, which are all accessible via a secret code).

title: The King of Fighters '97 (Okaidoku Set)
description: This release of The King of Fighters '97 includes the game along with a Sega Saturn 1MB RAM Expansion Cartridge.

title: The King of Fighters Best Collection
description:
The King of Fighters Best Collection is a pack containing all KOF games released for the Sega Saturn, plus the required ROM cartridge for KOF '95 (which included data from the game which wasn't available on the disc). The list of games included is as follows:

  • The King of Fighters '95
  • The King of Fighters '96
  • The King of Fighters '97

title: The Legend of Heroes I & II
description:
The Legend of Heroes I & II is a bundle composed of two games of the Legend of Heroes series:

  • The Legend of Heroes
  • The Legend of Heroes II

The bundle was only released in Japan.

title: The Legend of Heroes I & II: Eiyuu Densetsu
description:
The Legend of Heroes I & II: Eiyuu Densetsu is a bundle released for the Sega Saturn by GMF in Japan in 1998. It contains two RPGs from Falcom, Dragon Slayer: Eiyuu Densetsu and Dragon Slayer: Eiyuu Densetsu II. Though the music has been rearranged, graphics appear to try to recreate their originals on 1980s Japanese home computers (to the point that they do not have smooth scrolling).

Dragon Slayer: Eiyuu Densetsu is a traditional medieval-themed Japanese RPG with turn-based combat viewed from first-person perspective (like in Dragon Warrior games). The enemies are semi-random: they do appear out of nowhere and attack suddenly, but they are visible on the screen, and if you flee from a battle they will still be there to pursue you.

Dragon Slayer: Eiyuu Densetsu II is very similar to the first game, graphically and gameplay-wise. The only major difference is the fact that the enemies are now completely visible on screen before battles, so that the player can avoid fighting them if they want to.

title: The Legend of Heroes III: Shiroki Majo
description:
Jurio is a young boy who must travel to five sacred shrines as part of his warrior initiation rite. The lovely magician Chris accompanies him on his journey. But soon the two young people discover that they must face dangers far beyond those they have imagined. The prophecy of the mysterious White Witch is about to be fulfilled: a great wave will destroy the entire world of Tirasweel if nobody stops the man behind it...

The third entry in Legend of Heroes series (and also the first without the reference to Dragon Slayer universe in its title) introduces a new battle system: the battles in the game occur in pre-set locations, and evolve automatically. The player's task is to program the actions of the heroes (up to four in the party) before the battle. There are eight total "programs", with five moves each (for example, "attack", "attack", "cast healing magic", "attack", "cast offensive magic", etc.), and the player can switch between them during the battle.

Other game elements in Shiroki Majo are fairly typical for a Japanese-style RPG, including reliance on plot events, linear progression through the story, automatic leveling, etc.

title: The Legend of Oasis
aka_titles: 托尔传说2 精灵王纪传
光之继承者2 精灵王纪传
description:
Long time ago, Reharl, the King of Spirits, fought the destroyer Agito. Both sides used powerful armlets - Golden and Silver. Many years later, a warrior named Ordan found the Golden Armlet. recognizing unseen powers in his apprentice Leon, Ordan gave the armlet to him. Leon must become the new King of Spirits and defeat Agito, who is believed to be in possession of the Silver Armlet. In order to gain the power of the six Spirits, Leon must descend into the Spirits' dungeons.

The Legend of Oasis is the prequel to Beyond Oasis, also known as The Story of Thor. Like its predecessor, it is an action game with role-playing elements. The gameplay is quite similar to that of Beyond Oasis. Leon can attack with melee weapons or use a bow for long-ranged attack. His armlet also allows him to summon spirits, who would damage the enemy or heal Leon. Instead of the usual experience points system the game features "ranks" (equivalent to levels); higher ranks increase the protagonist's hit points and can be gained by recovering his health multiple times.

title: The Lost World: Jurassic Park
description:
The dinosaurs are back in this monstrous sequel. Take a dinosaur-stomping adventure through 'Site B' as you try to reach a radiophone to call a helicopter to get you out of there. But your journey won't be easy, because along the way you'll run into fierce, menacing dinosaurs that'll try to catch and eat you.

Play as characters from the movie and use weapons such as the tranquilizer, rocket launcher, and the shotgun. Featuring music straight out of the movie, many levels and fast gameplay, JURASSIC PARK is back... with bite!

5 different playable characters, over 30 levels, 20 different dinosaurs, variety of secret paths and hidden areas, 3D rendered graphics.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: The Mansion of Hidden Souls
aka_titles: La Mansión de las Almas Ocultas
Mystery Mansion: Das Haus der verlorenen Seelen
Shinsetsu Yumemi Yakata: Tobira no Oku ni Dareka ga...
La Mansion de las Almas Ocultas
description:
This Saturn-exclusive game is actually a sequel to the Sega CD game Mansion of Hidden Souls, even though the title might lead one to believe it is a remake.

This game takes place after the events of the first game. The souls of the hidden mansion have asked you to return, because they have recognized that you possess special powers that allow you to see the butterfly manifestations of the souls living there. Something terrible is afoot at the mansion, and you must investigate things and set them right. Along the way you must discover the true purpose of the mansion and it's significance in the universe.

Much like the Sega CD game, this is an FMV adventure. You move from location to location via video sequences, and solve puzzles to move on in the story.

title: The Need for Speed
aka_titles: Road & Track Presents: Over Drivin' DX
Road & Track Presents: The Need for Speed
description:
The Need for Speed is a single-player and multiplayer racing game focused on licensed sports cars and road racing.

The game places the player behind the wheel of high-performance cars in races across open roads and closed circuits. Rather than using a story campaign, it presents automotive competition as a series of timed races, head-to-head contests, and tournaments. The objective is to choose a car suited to the course, drive through traffic and hazards, pass checkpoints, and finish ahead of the opposition while maintaining control at high speed.

The selectable cars include real-world sports cars such as the Dodge Viper RT/10, Lamborghini Diablo, Ferrari 512 TR, Porsche 911 Carrera, Chevrolet Corvette ZR-1, Mazda RX-7, Toyota Supra Turbo, and Acura NSX. Each car differs in acceleration, top speed, braking, handling, and stability. Vehicle selection affects how the player approaches corners, straightaways, traffic, and police pursuit, since a faster car may be harder to control while a more balanced car may be easier to keep on the road.

Races are presented from several camera viewpoints, including an in-car cockpit view and external views. The player steers, accelerates, brakes, shifts gears where applicable, and attempts to maintain speed while avoiding collisions. Traffic vehicles appear on many road courses, requiring lane changes and careful passing. Colliding with traffic, walls, or roadside obstacles slows the player and can allow opponents or police to catch up.

The main road courses are divided into point-to-point segments, with each route running through a distinct environment such as city streets, coastal highways, or mountain roads. These courses include checkpoint gates and may include police vehicles that pursue the player. If a police car catches the player, the race can be interrupted by a ticket. Repeated police stops can end the run in arrest, making pursuit avoidance part of the race strategy rather than only a visual feature.

Other courses use closed circuit layouts, depending on the version. These races focus more on lap consistency, braking points, and opponent management than on checkpoint-to-checkpoint progression. Tournament-style play links races together and requires the player to perform well across multiple events. Single-race options allow individual cars, tracks, opponents, and race conditions to be selected without committing to a full tournament.

The game includes presentation features built around its licensed vehicles. Each car has specification screens, photographs, video sequences, and spoken or written information describing its performance and characteristics. These materials function as an in-game showcase for the vehicle roster, allowing players to compare cars before racing. Replay features allow completed races to be viewed from different angles, depending on the version. Some versions include additional tracks, time-of-day choices, two-player racing, or special modes, while others are limited to the original course and mode selection.

title: The Psychotron
aka_titles: Psychotron: Dominez l'esprit... Dominez le monde!
The Psychotron: Dominate the mind... Dominate the world!
description:
The Psychotron is an adventure from the early development time of live video, set in a wild Texan environment. A sort of Mission Impossible type of game with much usage of live video.

You have been assigned by the US President and the FBI to find a missing top-secret science project - a mind-control device developed during the time of the Soviet Union, recently sold by Russia to the US government... and vanished in transit. The video interaction is very sharp and the game also offers the player many puzzles, card and board game sequences.

title: The Scottish Open: Virtual Golf
description:
In the golf simulator you are allowed to win in Scottish Open on Championship Golf Courses, including The Bowery, Kilmarney, Penperro, and Carnoustie. There are many players in the game, who can rise during the playing. You can choose, edit or create one of them. Choosing a club, striking a ball, and counting turns, you have to beat your opponents, taking into account wind and height of landscape.

The game employs 3 different camera angles to capture the most realistic aspect on the course.

title: The Star Bowling
description: The Star Bowling is a 3D bowling game where the player competes against one of five real-life voice actresses. The main story mode has the player select a girl and play against them in multiple games; winning against each opponent will unlock video clips of that girl in a bonus gallery on the second disc. Various ball and lane variations are included, and there is also a two-player versus mode.

title: The Star Bowling Vol. 2
description: The Star Bowling Vol. 2 directly expands on the first game's concept, providing five more real-life actresses to bowl with. As before, winning against each girl will unlock video clips of them, and there are multiple ball and lane types to choose from. New in this edition is a trial mode where the player must clear a sequence of pin setups with a limited number of balls, and the multiplayer mode now supports up to four players.

title: The Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love
aka_titles: Chō Jikū Yōsai Macross: Ai Oboete Imasu ka
Chou Jikuu Yousai Macross: Ai Oboete Imasu ka
Choujikuu Yousai Macross: Ai Oboete Imasu ka
description: The Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love is a fast-paced sci-fi side-scrolling 2D shooter which very closely follows the storyline of the anime movie of the same title, allowing you to play through every battle sequence from the movie. You play the game as the main protagonist Hikaru Ichijyo and your craft can transform into Fighter, Gerwalk and Battroid modes any time during battle. Unlike the movie however, the game begins off the coast of South Ataria Island, with Skull Squadron preparing to battle the invading Zentradi fleet and there is newly animated cut-scene segments created just for the beginning of the game as well. Seconds after Skull Squadron takes off, the aircraft carrier Prometheus is sliced in half by a Zentradi attack fired from Earth's orbit. After you finish the first stage, all surviving Skull Squadron units fly toward the Macross, which executes a space fold, escaping. The actual beginning of the film starts at the second stage of the game.

title: The Tower
description:
Your goal is to build a skyscraper that is both tall, aesthetically pleasing, popular, and, most importantly, economically profitable. To be successful, your building cannot just be endless levels of office space or purely an apartment sky-rise, but rather a multi-functional haven for humanity featuring everything from penthouses to theatres, restaurants to shopping malls. The centerpiece of your tower design is your elevators and proper management is key.

You can watch your Sims enter and leave your grand tower, getting impatient waiting for elevators, or having a hectic workday at the office. You can even train in on one or two, to serve as a metering stick for their compatriots, or just to peek into the average workday of the little people living in your building. Or watch the security and rescue crews race as disasters like bomb threats and fires rampage through your well-crafted skyscraper.

title: The Unsolved
description:
The Unsolved is an adventure game in style of The X Files that uses real-actors and real photo backdrops. The player assumes a role of a police detective who is trying to solve the series of murders in downtown Los Angeles, where all the victims are women. All the victims seem to be missing organs and depleted of their blood, and modus operandi of the perpetrator is unknown. Police is tapping in the dark, and the closer you get to the truth, the story mixes science fiction and supernatural, much like The X Files.

While actors use English, this game is not released outside of Japan, and subtitles as well as any other in-game text are in Japanese.

title: The Unsolved: Hyper Science Adventure
description:
The Unsolved is an adventure game in style of The X Files that uses real-actors and real photo backdrops. The player assumes a role of a police detective who is trying to solve the series of murders in downtown Los Angeles, where all the victims are women. All the victims seem to be missing organs and depleted of their blood, and modus operandi of the perpetrator is unknown. Police is tapping in the dark, and the closer you get to the truth, the story mixes science fiction and supernatural, much like The X Files.

While actors use English, this game is not released outside of Japan, and subtitles as well as any other in-game text are in Japanese.

title: The Yakyūken Special
description: The Yakyūken Special is an updated port of a 3DO striptease game of the same name. As before, the player visits various models who challenge the player to a game of janken (rock-paper-scissors), doing a dance before making their move. Each time the player wins, the opponent removes an article of clothing, leaving her fully nude after five rounds. This version includes a total of twelve young ladies to challenge: the same eight from the original 3DO release, plus four new girls exclusive to this Saturn version.

title: The Yakyuu Ken Special: Konya wa 12-kaisen
description: The Yakyuuken Special is an updated port of a 3DO striptease game of the same name. As before, the player visits various models who challenge the player to a game of janken (rock-paper-scissors), doing a dance before making their move. Each time the player wins, the opponent removes an article of clothing, leaving her fully nude after five rounds. This version includes a total of twelve young ladies to challenge: the same eight from the original 3DO release, plus four new girls exclusive to this Saturn version.

title: Theme Park
description:
Theme Park is a construction and management simulation game in which the player designs, operates, and expands an amusement park. The goal is to attract visitors, keep them entertained, and turn the park into a profitable business.

The player begins with an open plot of land and must build paths, queues, rides, shops, and scenery. Early attractions include smaller rides such as teacups and haunted houses, while later research unlocks more elaborate attractions, including water rides and custom-designed roller coasters. Trees, lakes, and other decorative features can improve the park’s appeal, while careful path and queue placement helps visitors move efficiently between attractions.

Visitors have needs and reactions of their own, becoming hungry, thirsty, bored, sick, or frustrated by high prices, crowded paths, long queues, and poorly placed facilities. Shops and stalls are therefore an important part of the business. Visitors can buy food, drinks, and souvenirs, and the player can adjust details such as pricing and product ingredients. For example, increasing salt in food can encourage visitors to buy more drinks, while sugar and caffeine can affect demand for other items. These small management choices can improve profits, but they may also affect guest satisfaction.

The park also requires staff to run smoothly. Handymen keep paths clean, mechanics repair rides, entertainers improve guest happiness, and security guards help prevent trouble. Staff wages must be managed, since workers may demand higher pay or go on strike if they feel underpaid. Rides must also be maintained as they age, since breakdowns, accidents, and poor reliability can hurt the park’s reputation and endanger visitors. Litter, long queues, high prices, and visitor complaints all need attention if the park is to remain successful.

Beyond day-to-day park operation, the player must manage finances, research, and competition. Statistics screens provide information about attendance, income, guest happiness, ride performance, and overall financial health. Funding research unlocks new rides, shops, and improvements, while competing parks provide a measure of the player’s success in the wider amusement-park industry. Successful parks can eventually be sold for profit, allowing the player to buy land in new locations and continue building a global amusement-park empire.

The game can be played in three modes. Sandbox emphasizes park design and construction with fewer business concerns, while Sim adds more management elements. Full mode includes the most strategic depth, requiring the player to handle broader business systems such as finances, staff relations, research, competition, loans, land value, company shares, and stock market activity while building a successful park.

title: Three Dirty Dwarves
description:
Three Dirty Dwarves is a side-scrolling action game with an interesting plot: genetically altered "super kids" playing Dungeons & Dragons open a portal that allows their "alter-egos" (the three dirty dwarves) to enter our world and try to rescue them from their evil Army Base captivity.

Once the dwarves arrive, they ransack the local "armory" (a sporting goods store) for weapons and set off to rescue the kids. The portal also lets in a number of fantasy bad guys too and they must be squashed on the way.

The main game mechanics allows the player to switch between each dwarf and uses its special attack (e. g. baseball bat and baseballs, bowling pins and bowling balls, and a shotgun). Additionally, there is the DwarfMorph" attack where the dwarves act as one.

title: Three Wonders
description:
Three Wonders contains three different games: Midnight Wanderers (side-scrolling action), Chariot (shoot-em-up) and Don't Pull (puzzle).

Midnight Wanderers: Quest for the Chariot Midnight Wanderers (Roosters in the Japanese version) is a run-and-gun game. The player walks along side-scrolling stages while shooting enemies with a bow. The player can grab power-ups such as stronger shot, or a companion that follows the avatar and shoots. The gameplay is very similar to Ghosts 'N Goblins, made by the same developer. If the avatar gets hit he loses his clothes and will walk in his underwear in the same way.

Chariot: Adventure Through The Sky Chariot is a shoot-em-up similar to Gradius. The player shoot enemies on a vertically scrolling screen, collect power-ups and fight end bosses. The player collects power-ups such as three-way shot, stronger laser, extra points, bombs and shields. If the player picks up extra bombs, they attach to the chariot like a tail. The end bosses are themed after the classic elements, like the sun, or based on Zodiacs like Gemini.

Don't Pull Don't Pull is essentially a polished and updated version of Pengo. In this single screen game, the player plays as a bunny or squirrel walking through a maze full of baddies. The player can push the blocks of the maze to crush the enemies.

If a tile that is pushed is blocked by another tile, it is crushed and clears the way through the maze. There also are special blocks, for example a block with a bomb icon, that explodes and stuns any nearby enemies. Bonus points are earned for crushing multiple enemies with a single block push.

title: Thunder Force V
description: The first instalment in the Thunder Force series made for 32-bit consoles. As a pilot for the Thunder Force group, it's up to you to destroy an evil alien race bent on destroying the Earth and all of its inhabitants. As in its predecessors, the gameplay is fast and furious, with more powerful weapons. All weapons now have an extra powerful blast mode, triggered by holding down the fire button. Sprites have been forfeited in favor of 2D polygons made possible by the new platform. The musical score contains a lot of techno rearrangements of old Thunder Force themes.

title: Thunder Force V (Special Pack)
description: This Special Pack of Thunder Force V includes a music CD containing arranged and remixed music from Thunder Force games.

title: Thunder Force V: Perfect System
description: The first instalment in the Thunder Force series made for 32-bit consoles. As a pilot for the Thunder Force group, it's up to you to destroy an evil alien race bent on destroying the Earth and all of its inhabitants. As in its predecessors, the gameplay is fast and furious, with more powerful weapons. All weapons now have an extra powerful blast mode, triggered by holding down the fire button. Sprites have been forfeited in favour of 2D polygons made possible by the new platform. The musical score contains a lot of techno rearrangements of old Thunder Force themes. In spite of all the changes, Thunder Force V aims to please fans of old-schoolers by not abandoning concepts and details introduced in earlier games in the series.

title: Thunder Force: Gold Pack 1
description: Thunder Force: Gold Pack 1 is a re-release of both Thunder Force II and Thunder Force III for the Saturn. Both chapters in the side-scrolling shooter saga have been faithfully emulated with the addition of CD music, new CG cutscenes and other bonus features.

title: Thunder Force: Gold Pack 2
description: Thunder Force: Gold Pack 2 is the second re-packaged release in the Thunder Force series, featuring emulated versions of Thunder Force IV and the arcade-only Thunder Force AC. The re-packaged versions include new CG cutscenes and a few extra features such as the ability to control other ships.

title: Thunder Storm & Road Blaster
aka_titles: Interactive Movie Action: Thunder Storm & Road Blaster
サンダーストーム＆ロードブラスター
description:
Thunder Storm & Road Blaster is a bundle composed of two discs that features two FMV arcade games by Data East:

• Thunder Storm LX-3
• Road Blaster

Thunder Storm LX-3 is an "on rails" style helicopter shooter with the player controlling only the aiming of the shooting but not the direction of the helicopter. Your job is to shoot down the enemies as you are flown through footage of New York streets, the Statue of Liberty, the Atlantic Ocean, Italy, the Grand Canyon and finally, the treacherous corners and return fire of the enemy's stronghold on Easter Island.

In Road Avenger, players assume the role of an angry cop on a wild ride as he pursues a gang of bikers who killed his wife. Players need to race through oncoming traffic, squeeze between trucks, trash motorcycles and steer through lots of explosions. The only thing needed are quick reflexes to follow the instructions on the screen (with an increasing difficulty) in order to keep the animation going.

title: Thunder Storm LX-3 & Road Blaster
description:
Thunder Storm & Road Blaster is a bundle composed of two discs that features two FMV arcade games by Data East:

  • Thunder Storm LX-3
  • Road Blaster

The bundle was only released in Japan.

title: Thunderstrike 2
description:
This is the sequel to Core's Sega CD game, AH-3 Thunderstrike. Like the previous game in the series, this is a helicopter simulator/shooter. It features realistic features like multiple weapons selection, full freedom of movement, and a mission-based structure. On the other hand, it also throws lots and lots of enemy tanks and helicopters at you to blow up.

The graphics in Thunderstrike 2 are drawn completely with 3D polygons, including the helicopter's cockpit. As you track an enemy, the view changes so that it is always in your sights. There are 8 campaigns to complete, each with multiple missions.
publishers: Tec Toy Indústria de Brinquedos S.A.

title: Tilk: Aoi Umi kara Kita Shōjo
description:
Billy is a young boy who lives in a village on the island of Tilk. He and his friends have a secret hideout, and they have grand make-believe adventures as a group. But one day, a mysterious young girl named Silky appears on the island, and it seems that Billy and his friends may be embarking on an adventure for real now.

Tilk: Aoi Umi kara Kita Shōjo is an adventure game in chapters with tactical-style battle sequences. Each chapter consists of a sequence of side-view dialogue sequences in which the characters interact and converse automatically. Player interaction is limited to occasional dialogue choices which will affect the story's progression. Each chapter may also contain one or more battle sequences in which the group of kids fight against other kids or against monsters. These are turn-based top-down tactical battles in the vein of Shining Force where the player controls each member of the party individually.

title: Time Bokan Series: Bokan to Ippatsu! Doronbo
aka_titles: Time Bokan Series: Bokan to Ippatsu! Doronbo Kanpekiban
description:
Bokan to Ippatsu! Doronbo is a vertically-scrolling shoot-em-up based on the Time Bokan anime franchise produced by Tatsunoko Production and best known for the Yatterman series. The player controls the villainous Doronjo and her two henchmen, fighting against the heroes of the various Time Bokan shows while piloting various mechanical contraptions. There are initially six vehicles to pilot, with three more unlocked as the game progresses; each has a different set of weapon abilities, and can temporarily transform into a huge and highly-destructive super form after collecting enough powerups.

The later Sega Saturn port, dubbed "Kanpekiban" ("Perfect Edition"), adds an additional stage with a new boss to fight, a new animated opening movie, and additional voice acting for all characters.

title: Time Bokan Series: Bokan to Ippatsu! Doronboo Kanpekiban
aka_titles: Time Bokan Series: Bokan to Ippatsu! Doronbow Kanpekiban
description:
Bokan to Ippatsu! Doronboo Kanpekiban is a vertically-scrolling shoot-em-up based on the Time Bokan anime franchise produced by Tatsunoko Production and best known for the Yatterman series. The player controls the villainous Doronjo and her two henchmen, fighting against the heroes of the various Time Bokan shows while piloting various mechanical contraptions. There are initially six vehicles to pilot, with three more unlocked as the game progresses; each has a different set of weapon abilities, and can temporarily transform into a huge and highly-destructive super form after collecting enough powerups.

Saturn port adds an additional stage with a new boss to fight, a new animated opening movie, and additional voice acting for all characters.

title: Time Commando
aka_titles: Time Commando: Fight your way through time. Or you're history.
description:
In the near future, the military has created an advance computerized combat simulation, which allowed participants to be trained in various forms of combat throughout human history. However, a programmer working for a corporation that seeks the downfall of the simulation developers infects the system with a virus. This virus creates a dimensional vortex that threatens to swallow the entire world. Stanley Opar, a member of S.A.V.E (Special Action for Virus Elimination) enters the vortex with one goal: destroy the virus before the universe ceases to exist.

Time Commando is an action game with light puzzle-solving elements. The player character travels to eight different time periods: Prehistoric, Roman Empire, Feudal Japan, Medieval, Conquistador, Wild West, Modern Wars, and Future. Each era has its own characteristic enemies and sets of weapons: for example, Stanley fights with rocks and bone knives in the Prehistoric era, switching to shurikens and katanas in Japan, revolvers and shotguns in the Wild West, laser pistols in the future, etc.

Most of the time in the game is spent fighting enemies. Character navigation and combat resemble those of Alone in the Dark. The navigation is character- rather than camera-based, similarly to survival horror games. During combat, Stanley has three attack moves at his disposal, as well as a blocking move. Part of the challenge relies on choosing the right weapons against particular enemies.

Stanley starts with a small life bar that can be increased by picking up life power-ups, as well as multiple lives. Time limit is imposed on each level. To lower the countdown, the player has to deposit computer chips collected throughout the levels in special orb pools. The game utilizes animated pre-rendered sequences to represent locations, and polygonal models for the characters.

title: Time Gal & Ninja Hayate
description:
Time Gal & Ninja Hayate is a bundle comprised of two discs with two FMV arcade games:

  • Time Gal (previously converted to MSX, SEGA CD and LaserActive)
  • Ninja Hayate (released for the SEGA CD as Revenge of the Ninja)

The bundle was only released in Japan.

title: Time Warner Interactive's VR Virtua Racing
description:
Virtua Racing is a polygon-based racing game in which you must beat an opponent, who is either human or computer controlled. In the conversion to the Saturn, many new features were added:

  • 7 new tracks, which brings the total number of tracks in the game to 10.
  • 4 new cars, which brings the total number of cars in the game to 5. The new cars are a go-kart, a Porsche 911, an F-160 racer, and a GTP-class car.
  • A new Grand Prix mode. The Grand Prix mode is a career simulation. You must work your way up from one class of vehicle to next be accumulating points in a series of races.

title: TNN Motor Sports Hardcore 4x4
description:
TNN Motorsports Hardcore 4x4 is an off road racing game. You drive a 4x4 like a Jeep or pickup truck around cross-country loops and attempt to get to the finish line first. There are three race types. In single race mode you participate in only one race on a track of your choice against 5 other competitors. Championship allows you to race through all 6 courses in a row in an attempt to win a hidden truck. Time trial lets up to 8 players compete round-robin style for the fast lap time around a track.

This game utilizes 3D environments and truck models. The sound track features hard rock music.

title: Tokimeki Mahjong Graffiti: Toshishita no Tenshi-tachi
aka_titles: Tokimeki Mahjong Graffiti: Toshishita no Tenshi-tachi
description: Tokimeki Mahjong Graffiti: Toshishita no Tenshi-tachi is a strip mahjong game and the follow-up to Tokimeki Mahjong Paradise. While nominally a sequel, it features a completely different cast of new characters. It is a standard 2-player riichi mahjong game with a variety of rules options. The main mode is "Date Mode", in which the player must earn enough points by winning at mahjong to cause each girl to remove their clothing in fully-animated scenes. There is also a free battle mode and a "Memories" mode where completed reward scenes can be reviewed.

title: Tokimeki Mahjong Paradise: Koi no Tenpai Beat
description: Tokimeki Mahjong Paradise: Koi no Tenpai Beat is a Mahjong tile-based game with two game modes. The Date Mode has the player competing against five girls to win their hearts. Each time they lose a match, the girls strip of some of their clothing in a cutscene, but whenever the player loses, they refuse any further favors. The Free Play allows the player to practice the game without any rewards for winning or consequences for losing.

title: Tokimeki Memorial Drama Series Vol. 3: Tabidachi no Uta
description:
Tokimeki Memorial Drama Series: Vol.3: Tabidachi no Uta is the third and final game in the Tokimeki Memorial Drama Series trilogy of visual novel side stories to Konami's dating simulation series. This edition focuses on the heroine Shiori Fujisaki; the protagonist has fallen for her, but is unsure of how she might feel about him in return, and so he decides to pour all his passion and energy in the weeks before their high school graduation into preparing for an upcoming marathon.

The game is a linear Japanese-style adventure game, with limited commands available such as look, talk, and move. There are also several mini-games throughout, such as a guitar mini-game which returns from the previous entry, and an arcade-style shooting game. There are also bonus scenarios included for players with completed save files for the previous Drama Series entries, which are short stories centered around those games' heroines — Saki Nijino and Ayako Katagiri — as they graduate from high school.

title: Tokimeki Memorial Drama Series: Vol.1 - Nijiiro no Seisyun
description:
Nijiiro no Seisyun (虹色の青春) is the first story in the Tokimeki Memorial Drama Series trilogy which takes place within the same years of school life depicted in the original Tokimeki Memorial: Forever with You, but focuses on a shorter time period. Each of the three games features different protagonist who are all childhood friends of Shiori Fujisaki, the main heroine from the Tokimeki Memorial series. Player can enter the name of the protagonist at the beginning of the game, or accept the default one.

In this, first story, the protagonist is a high-school sophomore who is member of a soccer club. As substitute player he doesn't get much chance to play, but is secretly practicing in order to gain skill level and show his teammates and the coach why he should play. Luckily for him, he's not alone, as the manager on the team, Saki Nijino, is supporting him in his training. Unlike visual novel gameplay style, which is also present, you can often move mouse cursor around the screen to interact with objects (i.e. look, take, throw, etc.) and characters (.e. look, talk, call to, etc.), and while talking to characters there will be various topics and sub-topics you can talk about. Beside adventure style gameplay, the game also features soccer mini-games which requires you to kick the ball at the designated target to score a point. That gameplay elements is most similar to golf games, where you adjust the point where you want to kick the ball and use a power-bar to select the intensity of your kick.

title: Tokimeki Memorial Drama Series: Vol.2 - Irodori no Love Song
description:
Irodori no Love Song is the second game in the Tokimeki Memorial Drama Series which centers around another heroine from the Tokimeki Memorial franchise, namely Ayako Katagiri. The game takes place during the season of autumn in the same high-school during the culture festival. The protagonist is an amateur yet popular guitarist in the school who wrote an original song for festival competition. He forgot his encounter in the past with Ayako, but the more fate brings them back together, the more he will start to remember, and his feelings will turn into a love song.

The game mostly plays as a visual novel with adventure elements such as selecting actions to perform (i.e. see, talk, etc.), but also includes several action mini-games such as guitar game, comic dialogue game, knitting game, and swimming game. While game supports both gamepad controller and mouse, some of the mini-games (namely guitar game and knitting game) do not support mouse controller.
developers: Konami Computer Entertainment Japan Co., Ltd.

title: Tokimeki Memorial Drama Series: Vol.3 - Tabidachi no Uta (Sotsugyō Kinen Set)
description: This Graduation Commemorative Set edition of Tokimeki Memorial Drama Series: Vol.3 - Tabidachi no Uta includes the game along with a mini photo album and a poster packaged in a diploma case. This deluxe edition was the only release of the game for the Sega Saturn.
developers: Konami Computer Entertainment Japan Co., Ltd.

title: Tokimeki Memorial Selection: Fujisaki Shiori
description:
This is a spin-off from the main Tokimeki Memorial game series with main focus on Shiori Fujisaki, the main heroine from the original Tokimeki Memorial game.

Gameplay-wise, the game contains four really shot date visual novels, one for each season (spring, summer, fall and winter) and a rock-paper-scissors mini-game you can play with Shiori. The mini-game rules are like this: the one who wins the rock-paper-scissors game points toward left or right and the one that lost has to look in the right direction or losses a point. The winner is the one who first gets three points. The game features full voice-acting for Shiori whenever she is talking on the screen, whether in visual novels, mini-game or various extras.

Extras consist of two music video which use animated Shiori incorporated on the live animated backdrops. Videos mostly show sea and nature, as well as some rural and known Japanese cities such as Yokohama. The portrait collection contains over a dozen of scrollable portraits of Shiori in various different outfits and locations. The voice collection includes various words and sentences you can hear Shiori say upon selection. Shiori's mini-character is walking around the screen and stops to say to selected word or a sentence.
publishers: Konami Computer Entertainment Japan Co., Ltd.

title: Tokimeki Memorial: Forever with You
description:
This is an updated version of the first Tokimeki Memorial. This version has improved graphics and sound, new cut-scenes, and new mini-games.

You are a young boy who is going to study three years at the Kirameki High School in Japan. Your goal is to win the affection of one (and possibly more) of the twelve beautiful girls who also study with you, especially of Shiori, with whom you were in love some years ago. This is a simulation game with a high-developed statistics system. You have to increase your statistics in different disciplines, depending on the girl you are interested in. You communicate with people via your telephone, and date girls by going with them to various places. You have to keep your promises, otherwise a girl will become angry and even tell bad things about you to other girls, which will spoil your reputation.
developers: Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo Co., Ltd.

title: Tokimeki Memorial: Forever with You (Special-ban)
description: This limited-edition release of Tokimeki Memorial: Forever with You includes the game along with a Backup Memory Cartridge and a binder, in addition to the calendar and set of trading cards also included with the standard release.

title: Tokimeki Memorial: Taisen Puzzle Dama
aka_titles: ときめきメモリアル対戦ぱずるだま
description:
Tokimeki Memorial Taisen Puzzle Dama is a Puyo Puyo style puzzle game based on the dating game Tokimeki Memorial. The player chooses between the different girls from Tokimeki Memorial to compete in falling block battles. Colored blocks fall in pairs that the player rotates and places in the game matrix as they fall. There are two different types of blocks. When three or more regular blocks of the same color touch, they get cleared. Smaller blocks don't disappear like the regular blocks do when they are aligned, but grow into regular blocks when adjacent ones get cleared. This can be used to perform combos.

The goal of the game is to defeat another player or COM opponent by clearing series of blocks and making combos, which makes batches of small blocks fall into the opponent's matrix, until the opponent fails at clearing enough blocks and his matrix is full.
developers: Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo Co., Ltd.

title: Tokimeki Memorial: Taisen Tokkaedama
description:
Tokimeki Memorial: Taisen Tokkaedama is a competitive puzzle game which combines the gameplay of Taisen Tokkaedama with the characters from Tokimeki Memorial. Each player controls a floating cursor in a well full of colored pieces; the cursor carries one piece and can swap it with any other on the board, and lining up three pieces of the same color will clear them from the board. Some pieces are trapped in a container, which can be moved but not directly cleared and will be released when a neighboring piece is cleared, allowing for elaborate combo chains which will launch attacks at the opposing player. If a player's well completely fills with pieces, they lose the round.

The game includes three single-player modes: Tokimeki Mode (Story Mode), Kirameki Mode (Normal Mode), and Hirameki Mode (Quiz Mode). There is also two-player versus play with three game types.
developers: Konami Computer Entertainment Sapporo Co., Ltd

title: Tokusō Kidōtai JSWAT
description:
In the near future, an epidemic of crime and gun violence has swept across Japan. To counteract this threat, the secret police force JSWAT — Japanese Special Weapons and Tactics — has been formed. They are called in for the most dangerous missions, from gang warfare to hostage situations, and you are the newest recruit.

Tokusō Kidōtai JSWAT is a police-themed, first-person shooter with live-action cutscenes and digitized graphics. For each mission, the player must select a weapon loadout and attempt to neutralize all threats. While lethal force is available as an option, subduing and arresting criminals is the preferred approach, and is reflected as such in mission rankings. The player must also be careful not to harm hostages and civilians, and pay attention to instructions received over radio during each mission.

title: Tokyo Highway Battle
description:
One of the earliest in the Shutokou Battle series, where the player took control of 12 different cars and 60 different parts and upgrades available to choose from.

There are a variety of tracks to choose from, all recreated to resemble actual Tokyo roads and highways and featured the "Drift" button that allowed the player to take a turn faster. Players can also earn points through this action as well as from winning races to upgrade their car and go head-to-head against the computer or against three CPU opponents.

Keiichi Tsuchiya, a racing champion from Tokyo and Masaaki Bando, a top automotive expert from Japan both lent their expertise to the game to ensure authentic handling and physics for each vehicle that was rendered in the game.

title: Tokyo Shadow
description:
Hide doesn't get to see his girlfriend Kyoko very often, and so when she calls to invite him to a concert in Shibuya, he gladly accepts. However, while on his way to meet her, he sees a flash of red lightning across the sky. It seems nobody else around him could see it, and soon, Hide finds himself dead and turned into a ghost. Knowing Kyoko must be in danger too, he decides that even as a ghost he must protect her at all costs. However, it seems a demonic force is about to twist its grip around all of Tokyo, and it's not just Kyoko whose life is in danger next.

Tokyo Shadow is an FMV adventure game based on the novels of the same title written by Aya Nishitani. The story plays out via video clips and still photographs, and the player is occasionally given choices which branch the storyline to one of nearly 50 different endings. As specific endings are reached, more decision points are added to certain scenes, and the game keeps track of which endings have been seen.

title: Tomb Raider
aka_titles: Tomb Raider en vedette Lara Croft
description:
Lara Croft is a Tomb Raider, an archaeologist who explores ancient sites in search of valuable artifacts, who is hired to retrieve an artifact from a tomb in Peru, which turns out to be one of three parts of the Atlantean Scion. Soon betrayed by her employer, Lara Croft travels to Greece and Egypt to recover the other parts before this powerful device falls into the wrong hands.

Tomb Raider is a 3D action game with platforming and puzzle-solving elements, in which players control Lara Croft from a third-person perspective. The camera follows Lara as she climbs, jumps, and swims through detailed environs overcoming environmental obstacles and deadly fauna. Moving through levels often involves finding spots where Lara can climb, looking for spots where Lara can use her acrobatic ability, and sliding blocks and pushing levers to solve puzzles and open passageways.

Lara is armed with twin pistols with infinite ammunition, but she can pick up higher caliber weapons to take on deadlier human opponents. Lara also comes across restorative health packs and has a compass with which she can orient herself. Lara’s opponents include animals, gunmen, as well as primeval and supernatural beings. Careful explorers can also find secret areas and avoid traps.

title: Top Anglers: Super Fishing Big Fight 2
description: Top Anglers: Super Fishing Big Fight 2 is a fishing game and a sequel to Super Fishing Bigfight. The main mode is a series of four tournaments, each of which takes place in a different environment and has a specific type of target fish. There is also a free fishing mode where the player can select from each of the locations and choose a target fish, rod type, season, and time of day to freely fish that area.

title: Touge King: The Spirits 2
description: As a sequel to Tōge King: The Spirits, this game continues in the same vein of fast racing over the dangerous ridges and mountain tops. The game expands on the first one adding more details and additional content. Game contains only three courses consisting of curved and challenging Japanese mountain roads, plus they can be played in various seasons which requires a whole new driving tactic. Main racing modes include "King Battle" (main mode where you have to prove yourself to be the king and win all the races), "Free Battle" (one player mode where you can select your rival and your car and test your skill), "VS Battle" (a two-player mode where you can play against your friend in a split-screen view), and "Training" (which offers Time Attack, Free Driving and Dricon where you get rewarded based on your drifting skill).

title: Tour Party: Sotsugyō Ryokō ni Ikō
description:
Tour Party: Sotugyō Ryokō ni Ikō is a romance-themed board game set during a school graduation trip. Up to five players each select a character and a partner of the opposite gender from a selection of eight male and eight female characters, then take turns spinning a roulette to move around the game board. The goal is to land on the same space as your partner to first introduce yourself, then to invite them on dates and finally to confess your love to them.

Each space on the game board represents a specific type of date spot, and each character has specific date types that they like best; landing on certain spaces can also trigger events which will increase a character's stats or award cards. Cards can be used to give that player a benefit or hinder other players, and some allow the player to trigger certain types of special date events. The goal of the game is to raise your partner's affection level as high as possible, then meet them on a specific space to confess your love to them and win the game.

title: Touryuu Densetsu: Elan Doreé
description: Elan Doreé is originally a ST-V arcade from the unknown developer Sai-Mate. This game adds a lot of new aspects to traditional fighting games, just like the battles with flying dragons and the magic attacks. Each character rides a dragon which means that you're actually supposed to be flying at all times. Most of the fighting takes place on a 2D plane, but you do have complete freedom of 3D movement.

title: Transport Tycoon
description:
In Transport Tycoon, the player is in charge of a transport company starting in 1930 in the midst of The Great Depression, and the aim is to build up an empire of trains, ships, lorries, planes and helicopters, with technological evolution gradually taking place and allowing for better vehicles to be used. The game can be played alone, or with a number of computer-controlled rivals.

At the beginning of the game, a large terrain is generated. It is shown in isometric projection and includes hills, rivers, lakes, bridges, industrial facilities and a lot of small towns. It is up to the player to decide how to start building a transport empire.

All transport connections involve linking towns and/or factories, constructing vehicle depots and purchasing vehicles. For example, a common starting move includes connecting two towns with a road, building a vehicle depot somewhere next to the road, and setting up bus stops in both towns. Then, a bus needs to be purchased, its schedule set, and ordered to start. As it goes between both bus stops, taking passengers and unloading them, it earns its owner money. Train networks are built similarly, but require individual locomotives and appropriate wagon types to be assigned to each train. Most businesses offer certain types of cargo and are ready to pay for transporting other cargo to them; for example, a steel mill has a lot of steel to fill entire wagons, and will gladly accept iron ore any is available.

Landscaping tools are also available, best used for clearing terrain for new roads or tracks, or for creating canals for ships to pass through. Some buildings like airports require large sections of flat land.

Clicking on any vehicle brings up a small window where a live feed of what the vehicle is doing can be observed and its status is shown. If anything important happens during the game (such as a particular station accepting its first vehicle), it is shown as a newspaper headline at the bottom of the screen.
